The mould is placed on a small article in the bottom of a pan of boiling water.
This enables the water to circulate around the mould.
Care must be observed in keeping the kettle two-thirds full of boiling water all of the time of cooking.
(Bettina used the method in the fireless cooker.
) She started the brown bread in the cooker utensil on the top of the stove.
When the water was boiling vigorously, she placed it over one hot stone in the cooker.
The water came two-thirds of the distance to the top of her cans.
In the cooker, she did not have to watch for fear the water would boil away.
After fastening the lid tightly on the cooker-kettle in which the bread was to steam, she did not look at it again for four hours.
(It takes a little longer in the cooker than on the stove.
recipes.name: Boston Brown Bread

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Put two crackers in the meat grinder, add bits of meat and pork and the rest of the crackers.
The crackers first and last prevent the pork and meat from sticking to the grinder.
Add other ingredients in order named.
Pack in a well-buttered bread-pan.
Smooth evenly on top, brush with white of an egg and bake one hour in a moderate oven.
Baste frequently.
The meat may be cooked in a fireless cooker between two stones.
It is perfectly satisfactory cooked this way, and requires no basting.
recipes.name: Veal Loaf

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Melt the chocolate, add a little powdered sugar, then water and flavoring and sufficient sugar to allow the icing to spread on cake.
Usually one and one-half cups is the necessary amount.
Spread on the cake.
recipes.name: Chocolate Icing For Cake

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Cream the butter, add the sugar gradually, and the egg well beaten.
Mix and sift the flour and baking powder and add alternately with the milk.
Add the vanilla.
Bake in a loaf- cake pan twenty-five minutes in a moderate oven.
recipes.name: One Egg Cake

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron

ingredients.name: cooked mixed diced vegetables
ingredients.note: string beans, carrots, peas or celery
ingredients.raw: 1 cup cooked mixed diced vegetables, (string beans, carrots, peas or celery)

instructions: Cooked vegetables may be combined for this salad.
Soak the gelatin in cold water a few minutes, add the meat stock or water and stir until the gelatin is thoroughly dissolved.
If it is not completely dissolved, heat over a pan of hot water.
Add the vegetables in such proportions as desired or convenient.
Add the salt, lemon juice and pimento ; turn the mixture into a moistened mould.
(A ring mould is attractive.
) Allow to stand for one hour or more in a cold place.
When ready to serve, remove from mould to a chilled plate.
If a ringed mould is used, the center may be filled with flaked salmon over which salad dressing has been poured.
If the vegetable part is used as a salad, salad dressing may be placed around the vegetables.
recipes.name: Salmon Salad with Jellied Vegetables

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron

ingredients.name: leftsp over cooked vegetables
ingredients.raw: 2 tablespoon leftsp over cooked vegetables, (peas, beans, celery or corn)

ingredients.name: chopped cooked ham or cooked bacon
ingredients.raw: 1 tablespoon chopped cooked ham or cooked bacon

instructions: Wash the tomatoes thoroughly and cut a slice one inch in diameter from the blossom end, reserving it for future use.
Carefully scoop out the pulp, being careful to leave the shell firm.
To the tomato pulp, add bread crumbs, left-over vegetables, chopped meat, egg, melted butter, salt and paprika.
Cook the mixture four minutes over the fire.
Fill the shells with the cooked mixture.
Put the slices back on the tomatoes.
Place in a small pan and bake twenty minutes in a hot oven.
recipes.name: Stuffed Tomatoes Bettina

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix the veal and sauce.
Heat and serve hot on rounds to toast.
recipes.name: Creamed Veal

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Wash and peel medium-sized potatoes ; cook in boiling water (salted) until tender.
(About twenty minutes.
) Drain and shake over the fire a minute or two until they are a little dry.
Either mash with potato masher, or put through potato ricer.
Add butter, salt, paprika and milk.
Beat till very light, fluffy and white.
Reheat by setting the saucepan in a larger kettle place over flame.
More milk may containing boiling water.
Be needed.
Pile them lightly on the hot dish in which they are to be served.
recipes.name: Mashed Potatoes

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Melt the butter in a frying-pan, slice the onion in it and sauté gently until golden brown in color.
Remove the onion from the butter, cut the flank steak into pieces three by two inches.
Dredge these lightly in one tablespoon flour and sauté in the butter until well browned.
Remove the meat from the frying- pan ; add the salt, pepper, paprika, mustard, vinegar and flour.
Mix all together and add the water slowly.
Replace the steak in the pan, cover closely and simmer one hour, or until the steak is tender.
Serve on a warm platter and pour the gravy over it.
recipes.name: Devilled Steak

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Wash, peel and core the apples.
Add water and cook slowly in a covered utensil until tender.
Remove cover, add the sugar and cook two minutes.
Sprinkle cinnamon on the top.
recipes.name: Apple Sauce

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Butter the bottom of a saucepan or frying-pan.
Fill half full of boiling water.
Break the eggs one at a time in a sauce dish, and slip them very gently into the pan of boiling water.
The eggs will lower the temperature of the water to a point below the boiling point.
Keep the water at this point (below boiling).
Allow the eggs to remain in the water four to six minutes, or until the desired consistency.
Remove from the water with a skimmer and serve on slices of toast which are hot, buttered, and slightly moistened with water.
The proper length of time for poaching eggs is until a white film has formed over the yolks and the white is firm.
A tin or aluminum egg poacher is very convenient.
When using rings, butter the rings, fill each compartment with an egg, and dip into the boiling water.
These are inexpensive, and economical, as no part of the egg is wasted.
recipes.name: Poached Eggs

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Cream the peanut butter, add the butter.
Cream again, add the salt and salad dressing, mixing well.
Cut the bread evenly.
Butter one side of the bread very thinly with the peanut butter mixture.
Place the lettuce leaf on one slice and place another slice upon it, buttered side down.
Press firmly and neatly together.
Cut in two crosswise.
Arrange attractively in a wicker basket.
recipes.name: Peanut Butter Sandwiches

author: Margaret W Howard
instructions: Allow 1 cup of fruit for four servings.
Wash thoroughly, cover with cold water, soak for several hours, and cook gently in same water till soft.
About 15 minutes before removing from fire add sugar to taste.
The flavor is improved by the addition of a few slices of lemon with the sugar.
Strain before serving.
Stewed apricots variation: make as above, omitting lemon and do not strain.
Stewed peaches variation: replace apples with peaches.
Stewed prunes variation: use 2 cups for four servings and do not strain.
recipes.name: Dried-apple Sauce

instructions: Work the flour quite smooth with the water, add the butter just slightly melted, and stir in the whites of the eggs well beaten up.
Cut the meat thin, season with pepper and salt, mix it with the batter, drop a small quantity at a time into a frying-pan of boiling lard, and fry for six or seven minutes.
Brown both sides.
recipes.name: Meat Fritters

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Wash the radishes thoroughly with a vegetable brush.
Cut off the long roots and all but one iach of green tops.
These tops make the radishes easier to handle and more attractive.
Serve in a bow! Of chopped ice.
recipes.name: Radishes

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Soak the gelatin in one tablespoon cold water for three minutes.
Add the boiling water and dissolve thoroughly.
Add the meat, onion, pimento, salt, pepper, lemon juice and parsley.
Stir well together and turn into a mould that has been moistened with cold water.
(A square or rectangular mould is preferable.
) Stand in a cold place for two hours.
When cold and firm, unmould on lettuce leaves and cut into slices.
Salad dressing may be served with it.
recipes.name: Jellied Beef

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix well.
Cream the butter, add the sugar.
Add the egg yolks, slightly beaten, and the potato.
Stir, add the chocolate, milk and then all the dry ingredients which have been mixed and sifted together.
Fold in the white of the eggs beaten stiffly.
Add the vanilla.
Pour into two layer-cake pans which have been prepared with waxed paper.
Bake in a moderate oven for thirty minutes.
Ice with white mountain cream icing.
recipes.name: Moist Chocolate Cake

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix ham, olives and pickles with salad dressing and spread on lettuce or nasturtium leaves between buttered slices of bread.
Trim off the crusts, and cut the sandwiches in fancy shapes.
recipes.name: Ham Sandwiches

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix the ingredients in the order given.
Use a silver fork for mixing.
Garnish with lettuce leaves.
recipes.name: Lobster and Salmon Salad

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Cream the butter, add the sugar and the egg.
Mix well add the flour, baking powder, cinnamon, nut-meats, salt, milk, vanilla and lemon extract.
Beat two minutes.
Pour into a loaf-cake pan prepared with waxed paper.
Bake thirty minutes in a moderate oven.
recipes.name: Loaf Cake (Bettina's Nut Special)

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Chop the mint leaves very fine.
Add the boiling water and sugar.
Cover closely and let stand one-half hour.
Add the vinegar, pepper and salt.
recipes.name: Mint Sauce

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Place half of the drippings in a sauce-pan.
Add the four, and allow it to brown.
Add slowly the water, salt and the rest of the drippings (two tablespoonsful).
Boil one minute.
recipes.name: Lamb Gravy

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Wash the lamb with a damp cloth.
Wipe dry and sprinkle with two teaspoons of salt.
Place the lard in a frying-pan.
Place when hot, add the lamb, and brown well on all sides.
The meat in the fireless utensil.
Sprinkle the potatoes with salt and paprika.
Arrange these about the leg of lamb.
Place the disks, heated for baking, over and under the baking pan.
Cook three hours in the fireless.
Use the drippings for gravy.
recipes.name: Roast Leg of Lamb with Potatoes

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Boil sugar and water ten minutes without stirring, add lemon cool and bottle.
Juice, and any other fruit juices.
Keep on ice and dilute with ice water when desired for use.
Serve mint leaves with the fruit juice.
recipes.name: Fruit Juice

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Remove the skin and eyes from the pineapple.
Cut cross- wise in half-inch slices, and the slices in cubes, at the same time discarding the core.
Sprinkle with sugar and stand in a cold place for an hour before serving.
recipes.name: Pineapple Sliced

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Arrange lettuce on serving dishes.
Place portions of tomato, cucumber and pimento on the lettuce.
Sprinkle with salt and paprika.
Serve with french dressing.
recipes.name: Tomato, Cucumber and Pimento Salad

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix ingredients, which have been thoroughly chilled, and beat until the mixture thickens.
Pour over the vegetables.
recipes.name: French Dressing

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Remove ends and strings from green beans.
Add water and cook over a moderate fire for twenty-five minutes.
Drain off the water, add butter, salt and paprika.
Reheat and serve.
recipes.name: String Beans with Butter Sauce

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Wash one pound of halibut steak and wipe dry.
Cut in two pieces.
Roll in flour, and cook ten minutes in a frying pan in hot fat.
Brown on one side, and then on the other.
Season with salt and paprika.
Serve very hot.
recipes.name: Halibut Steak

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix ingredients in order named.
Fill small buttered moulds or cups one-half full.
Set in a pan of hot water, and bake twenty minutes in a moderate oven.
Serve with the egg sauce.
recipes.name: Salmon Timbales

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Melt the butter, stir flour in well, and slowly add the milk.
Let it boil about two minutes, stirring constantly.
Season, add yolk of egg, and mix well.
(The oil from the salmon may be substituted for melted butter as far as it will go.
recipes.name: Egg Sauce

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Cut stale bread in one-third inch cubes.
Brown in the oven.
Add melted butter and salt.
Mix and reheat the croutons.
recipes.name: Croutons for the Soup

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Pick over selected berries, place in a colander and wash, draining carefully.
Press powdered sugar into cordial glasses to shape into a small mould.
Remove from glasses onto centers of paper doilies placed on fruit plates.
Attractively arrange ten berries around each mound.
Berries should be kept cool and not hulled.
Natural leaves may be used very effectively on the doily.
recipes.name: Strawberries au Naturel

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix dry ingredients, add egg and milk.
Beat well and add melted butter and extract.
Bake twenty-five minutes in a well buttered mould.
Serve hot with the lemon sauce.
recipes.name: Baked Cottage Pudding

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron

ingredients.name: lemon extract
ingredients.raw: 1 teaspoon lemon extract, or 1/2 tsp lemon juice

instructions: Mix sugar, flour and salt.
Slowly add the hot water.
Cook until thick, stirring constantly.
Add flavoring and butter.
recipes.name: Lemon Sauce

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron

ingredients.name: chopped onion
ingredients.raw: 1 teaspoon chopped onion, or 1/4 tablespoon onion salt

ingredients.name: chopped ham
ingredients.raw: 1/3 cup chopped ham, or 1 tablespoon salt pork

instructions: Remove the stems of the peppers and take out all the contents.
Remove small slices from the blossom end so they will stand.
Cover peppers with boiling water, allow to stand five minutes and drain.
Mix rest of ingredients thoroughly and fill peppers cases.
Bake in a moderate oven twenty-five minutes, basting frequently with hot water.
recipes.name: Stuffed Green Peppers

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Place alternate layers of diced cooked potatoes and sliced hard-cooked eggs in a baking dish.
Season.
Pour a thin white sauce over all of this.
Place in a moderate oven fifteen minutes.
recipes.name: Potatoes Anna

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Simmer the tomatoes, onion, bay leaves, cioves, sugar and water for fifteen minutes, rub through the strainer.
Melt butter, add flour and salt, add strained tomato juice and pulp.
Cook until the desired consistency.
recipes.name: Tomato Sauce III

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron

ingredients.name: cooked meat
ingredients.note: one or more kinds may be used
ingredients.raw: 1 cup cooked meat, ground fine (one or more kinds may be used)

ingredients.name: green pepper
ingredients.raw: 1 tablespoon green pepper, or pimento chopped fine

instructions: Beat the egg, add milk, seasonings, melted butter, bread- crumbs and meat.
Mix thoroughly.
Fill buttered cups three- fourths full of mixture.
Place in a pan of boiling water, and bake in a moderate oven fifteen minutes.
The mixture is done allow them to as soon as it resists pressure in the center.
Remain in the pans a few minutes, then remove carefully upon a serving plate.
They may be made in a large mould or individual ones.
Serve with the tomato sauce.
recipes.name: Boubons

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Cut the fat into the flour, salt and baking powder until the consistency of cornmeal.
Gradually add the milk, using a knife to mix.
Do not handle any more than absolutely necessary.
Toss the dough upon a floured board or a piece of clean brown paper.
Pat into the desired shape, and place in a pan.
Bake in a hot oven for 12 to 15 minutes.
Split, spread with butter, and place strawberries, crushed and sweetened, between and on top.
Serve with cream.
recipes.name: Strawberry Shortcake

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Melt the butter, add the flour, salt and paprika.
Thoroughly mix, slowly add milk, stirring constantly.
Allow sauce to cook two minutes.
recipes.name: White Sauce for New Potatoes

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Scrape four medium sized new potatoes.
Cook in boiling water (salted) until tender when pierced with a fork.
Drain off the water, and shake the kettle over the fire gently, to allow the steam to escape and make the potatoes mealy.
Make the white sauce and pour over the potatoes.
recipes.name: New Potatoes in Cream

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Wipe the meat carefully with a wet cloth.
Remove superfluous fat and any gristle.
Cut the edges to prevent them from curling up.
When the broiling oven is very hot, place the meat, without any fat, upon a hot flat pan, directly under the blaze.
Brown both sides very quickly.
Turn often.
Reduce heat and continue cooking about seven minutes, or longer if desired.
Place on a warm platter ; season with salt, pepper and bits of butter.
Set in the oven a moment to melt the butter.
If salt is added while cooking, the juices will be drawn out.
A gravy may be made by adding hot water, butter, salt, pepper and parsley to the pan.
Pour the gravy over the steak.
recipes.name: Pan-Broiled Steak

author: Louise Bennett Weaver
Helen Cowles LeCron
instructions: Mix well.
Melt the butter, add the flour, salt and pimento.
Gradually pour in the milk.
Allow the mixture to boil one minute.
Stir constantly.
Add the fish, cook one minute and pour over toasted strips of bread.
recipes.name: Creamed Tuna on Toast Strips

author: Estelle Taylor
instructions: Grind peaches into pulp, straining all juice from them into separate container.
Mix peach juice with one-third apricot juice and add to peach pulp.
Mix and freeze in ice cream freezer.
recipes.name: Montmarte Non-fattening Peach Ice Cream

author: Marie Prevost
instructions: Drain cherries and pineapple.
With knife pit cherries and re-fill with a filbert.
Cut up the pineapple into small pieces.
Cut grapes in half and remove seeds.
Place all the above in a large mixing bowl and fold in a mayonnaise dressing that is made as follows.
Beat eggs until light, add butter, sugar, salt, mustard, then add vine- gar diluted to taste, cook until thick in double boiler; when done add generous pinch of cayenne pepper.
When cold, beat in 1/2 cup of whipped cream, beaten until almost stiff.
Serve on lettuce leaf.
recipes.name: Beverly Hills Salad

author: Irene Rich

ingredients.name: a narrow strip of green pepper
ingredients.raw: a narrow strip of green pepper

ingredients.name: a narrow strip of red pepper
ingredients.raw: a narrow strip of red pepper

instructions: Remove the pulp from the grapefruit and orange without breaking the membrane.
Cut the pear in lengthwise slices.
Cut the endive in halves, discard the outer leaves, and wash with care.
Dispose the endive halves on plates, set the pear fan shape over these.
Back of the pears place a section of orange pulp, and a section of grapefruit just above the tips of the leaves.
To the fruit juice add the olive oil and salt; beat vigorously, and pour over the salad.
recipes.name: Salad a la Philippine

author: Vegetable Souffle
instructions: Beat the yolks of eggs and fold them into the stiffly beaten whites of eggs.
Add peas, spinach, which had been put through a sieve, and carrots, cut up the size of a pea.
Season with salt and pepper and last of all add a scant half cup of good rich milk.
Pour into a buttered baking dish and put in a moderately slow oven.
This should bake from 15 to 25 minutes, depending upon the time when the crust is nicely browned.
It should be eaten immediately.
recipes.name: Vegetable Souffle

instructions: Cook potatoes in skins until soft.
Peel and slice.
Add onion.
Fry bacon till crisp; don't let bacon fat get too brown.
Remove bacon from pan, drain and crumble.
Pour off all but 2 tablespoon bacon fat, add butter and stir in cornstarch, sugar, then vinegar, water, salt and pepper.
Bring sauce to a boil, stirring constantly, and pour over potatoes and onion.
Reserve some crumbled bacon and two eggs, sliced, for garnish.
Chop rest of eggs and sprinkle eggs and bacon over salad, mixing in gently.
Garnish with reserved bacon, eggs and chopped parsley.
recipes.name: German Potato Salad

instructions: Wipe the meat with a damp cloth.
Brown in hot skillet in fat which cooks from the meat.
Season.
Cover with creole sauce.
Cook in moderate oven (350Â°f) for one hour.
For sauce: cook the chopped vegetables in the lard until brown.
Add the flour and stir until smooth.
Gradually add the tomato juice and seasonings.
Pour over pork steaks.
recipes.name: Pork Steaks with Creole Sauce

instructions: Buy round steak cut one-half inch thick.
Wipe meat with a damp cloth.
Cut into six servings.
Brown the diced bacon and chopped onions.
Spread on meat which has been seasoned with salt and pepper.
Roll, fasten with skewers.
Brown in the remaining bacon fat.
Add one-half cup water, cover, reduce heat and simmer gently for 1 hi hours.
These may be finished in a moderate oven (350f).
recipes.name: Round Steak Rolls

instructions: Have the meat cut in two-inch cubes.
Brown in hot fat.
Add the barley, onions, parsley, celery tops, seasoning and water.
Simmer 1 1/2 hours.
Add other vegetables.
Continue cooking until vegetables are done.
Serve on a large platter, the meat heaped in the center.
Arrange vegetables around the edge and pile barley on top of meat.
recipes.name: Scotch Stew

instructions: Heat green beans.
Drain and save liquid.
Combine crumbs, seasonings, vinegar and liquid of beans.
Boil one minute, stirring constantly.
Add mixture to hot milk and pour over beans.
recipes.name: Sweet Sour Beans

instructions: Dissolve gelatin in hot water.
Cool.
Arrange sliced peaches in loaf pan.
Pour half the gelatin mixture over the peaches.
Set in refrigerator to chill.
Mix well drained raspberries with rest of gelatin and when quite thick pour over first layer.
Chill until firm.
Unmold on oval tray.
Serve either as a salad or a dessert.
recipes.name: Layered Peach and Raspberry Mold

instructions: Wipe meat with a damp cloth.
Season with salt and pepper and rub with garlic, if desired.
Place skin side down on a rack in an open pan.
Do not add water.
Do not cover.
Roast in a slow oven (300f) until the desired degree of doneness is reached.
If a roast-meat thermometer is used it should register 175f, for medium-done lamb, and 180f, for well-done lamb.
Allow approximately 30-35 minutes to the pound.
recipes.name: Leg of Lamb Moderne
recipes.yield: 6-8 servings for six pound leg of lamb

instructions: Boil water and sugar to a thick syrup.
Pour quickly over the mint which has been cut fine.
Cover and allow to steep for one hour.
Strain over the fruit juice and rind.
Add coloring if desired.
When cold pour into freezing tray of refrigerator and freeze.
When mushy turn into a chilled bowl and beat until smooth.
Fold in the stiffly beaten egg white and continue freezing.
A few drops of oil of peppermint or one-half teaspoon of peppermint extract may be used in place of the fresh mint leaves.
recipes.name: Mint Sherbet

instructions: Drain the beets.
Heat in the butter.
Season.
Turn into serving dish and sprinkle with chopped parsley.
recipes.name: Parsley Beets

instructions: Dice bacon and brown.
Add diced onion and green pepper.
Cook gently for 5 minutes.
Add stock and tripe which has been washed and shredded.
Season.
Simmer for one hour.
Add potatoes and cook for 30 minutes.
Mix the flour and butter to a smooth paste and thicken soup.
Just before serving add milk.
recipes.name: Philadelphia Pepper Pot

ingredients.name: Homemade Biscuit Mixture
ingredients.raw: 3 cup Homemade Biscuit Mixture, for dough

instructions: Grind the cooked liver and onion together.
Add other ingredients.
Cook slowly until thick.
Cool.
Add enough milk to the homemade biscuit mixture to make a soft dough.
Roll to one-fourth inch thickness.
Spread with cooled liver mixture, allowing one inch around the edge for overlapping.
Roll like a jelly roll.
Brush edges with water and pinch together.
Slide the roll onto a cookie sheet and form a crescent.
Sprinkle with finely chopped uncooked bacon.
Bake in hot oven (425f) for 25 to 30 minutes.
Serve with hot undiluted tomato soup or gravy.
recipes.name: A Crescent of Liver

author: Claire V Pulliam
instructions: Combine one-half the sugar and 1/2 cup syrup drained from pineapple with slightly beaten egg yolks.
Cook over hot water until smooth and thickened, stirring constantly.
Soften gelatin in water for 5 minutes.
Add to the hot mixture and stir until dissolved.
Chill until it starts to thicken, then add pineapple, sieved cottage cheese, grated lemon rind and lemon juice.
Fold in stiffly beaten egg whites, salt and whipped cream.
Combine crumbs, remaining sugar and butter or margarine.
Line pan with crumbs, saving out about a third for the top.
Add cheese mixture and cover with remaining crumbs.
Chill several hours until firm.
recipes.name: Pineapple Chiffon Cheese Cake

author: Yorkraft Inc
instructions: Break and soak yeast in water until soft.
Scald and then cool milk.
Cream together butter, sugar and salt.
Add well beaten eggs, lemon and spice.
Add lukewarm milk to yeast and mix with half the flour.
Work in butter and sugar mixture and enough flour to knead into a smooth dough.
Keep it as soft as can be handled readily.
Let rise over night at about 80 degrees.
As soon as dough is fully doubled in bulk, knead down and let rise again for an hour.
recipes.name: Sweet Roll Dough

author: Soad Mansour
Layla Risk
Suzy Grindi
instructions: Wash lentils thoroughly.
Add water, garlic, onion and carrot to lentils, and cook over medium heat for 45 minutes and add the cumin, salt and pepper.
Put in the blender for 2 minutes.
Add butter; simmer for 2 minutes.
Serve.
recipes.name: Shorpa Ads (Lentil Soup)

author: Soad Mansour
Layla Risk
Suzy Grindi
instructions: In a medium-sized saucepan, melt butter; stir in flour and cook for two minutes until the flour becomes golden in color.
Gradually blend in the broth.
Add the artichoke hearts,lemon juice, salt and pepper and simmer for 30 minutes.
Serve hot.
recipes.name: Shorpa Kharshofe (Artichoke Soup)

author: Order of Eastern Star Chapter 69

ingredients.name: (1 cup plus 2 tbsp) sifted cake flour
ingredients.raw: 1 1/8 cup (1 cup plus 2 tbsp) sifted cake flour, (Spoon lightIy into cup, don't pack)

ingredients.name: sieved very ripe bananas
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup sieved very ripe bananas, (1 to 1 1/2)

instructions: Preheat oven to 325f (moderate and slow).
Measure-(all level measurements)-and sift together into mixing bowl, flour, sugar, baking powder, salt.
Make a well in the center of dry ingredients and add in order: oil, egg yolks, water, bananas, flavoring.
Beat with spoon until smooth.
Measure into another large mixing bowl: egg whites, cream of tartar.
Whip until whites form very stiff peaks.
They should be much stiffer than for angel food or meringue.
Do not underbeat.
Pour egg yolk mixture gradually over whipped egg whites, gently folding with rubber scraper just until blended.
Do not stir.
Pour into ungreased 9-inch tube pan, 31' inches deep immediately.
Bake 50 to 55 minutes in slow moderate over, 325f, or until top springs back when lightly touched.
Immediately turn pan upside down, placing tube part over neck of funnel or bottle.
Let hang, free of table, until cold.
Loosen from sides and tube with spatula.
Turn pan over and hit edge sharply on table to loosen.
Split cake crosswise in three even layers with saw-toothed knife.
Spread whipped cream filling between layers (widest layer on bottom) and over top and sides.
Garnish with banana slices.
Keep in refrigerator until serving time.
Dip banana slices in lemon, orange, grapefruit or pineapple juice to keep from turning dark.
recipes.name: Banana Cream Chiffon Cake

author: Yorkraft Inc
instructions: Beat cream, sugar, vinegar and salt together thoroughly until the dressing is like whipped cream.
Discard outer leaves of cabbage.
Shred the rest finely and combine with dressing just before it is ready to serve.
As variation: add shredded green and red peppers.
recipes.name: Pennsylvania Cole Slaw

author: Soad Mansour
Layla Risk
Suzy Grindi
instructions: Add sugar to water and boil for five minutes; add the rest of ingredients.
Continue to boil for another minute; reduce heat and cook for seven minutes.
Set aside to cool, then chill.
Serve cold, garnished with whipped cream.
recipes.name: Khoshaf (Dried Fruit Salad)

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club

ingredients.name: salt pork
ingredients.raw: 1/8 pound salt pork, or bacon in thin strips

ingredients.name: large potatoes
ingredients.raw: 2 large potatoes, cut in 1/2 inch cubes

ingredients.name: -1/2 pound haddock fillets
ingredients.raw: 1 -1/2 pound haddock fillets, fresh or frozen

instructions: In heavy kettle, fry pork until golden brown.
Remove and save to add later.
Saute onion until soft, but nut brown.
Add 1/2 cup hot water and potatoes.
Season well with salt and pepper.
Cover and simmer until half done.
About 5 minutes.
Add fish.
Thaw in package if frozen, and add juice.
Season each layer well.
Cover and simmer slowly until fish begins to separate into flakes.
About 10 minutes.
Fish juices makes more liquid, but water may be added if potatoes begin to stick to pan.
If fish had skin on it, remove now.
Add hot milk (for rich chowder use 1/2 cup cream or undiluted evaporated milk and 1 1/2 cups regular milk).
Add salt pork cut or crumbled into small bits to float on top.
Season to taste.
Let stand at least 10 minutes to blend flavors.
Flavor improves with age.
recipes.name: New England Fish Chowder, Maine Style

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Preheat oven to 375f.
Mix beaten egg, mushroom soup, milk, and tuna flakes.
Add cooked peas, olives, cashes, and noodles.
Place mixture in a greased casserole and garnish with ripe olives and chinese noodles.
Bake for 30 minutes.
recipes.name: Tuna Noodle Crunch

author: Clarkson Woman's Club
instructions: Cut meat into bite size pieces.
Place the meat in pressure cooker with water or boil in kettle.
Add: celery salt, chili powder, celery (optional), parsley, onion, celery salt, pepper, paprika.
Boil 50 minutes under 10 lbs pressure or boil until tender.
While the above is cooking place 2 tbsp grease in a medium sized skillet on medium heat.
Blend in flour.
Brown, stirring frequently.
Cool.
Add 1 1/2 cups water gradually.
Stir until smooth.
Set aside.
Place gingersnaps in a bowl.
Pour 1/2 cup water over the ginger snaps.
Set aside until the meat is done.
When the meat is tender, add the ginger snaps and the browned flour mixture.
Add: ketchup, brown sugar, vinegar, 1/2 cup water, kidney beans (or more if desired).
Goulash is best when allowed to set 3 or 4 hours after being prepared.
If goulash becomes quite thick 1/2 cup water may be added.
recipes.name: Gulas (Goulash)

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club

ingredients.name: granulated sugar
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup granulated sugar, or 2/3 cup brown sugar

instructions: Combine rice, milk, sugar, and salt; pour into greased 1-1/2 quart baking dish.
Bake in a slow oven (300f) one hour, stirring several times.
Add lemon peel, nutmeg, and raisins.
Continue baking 2 to 2 1/2 hours.
Serve hot or cold.
recipes.name: Old-Time Rice Pudding

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Brown spareribs.
Add salt and pepper.
Put sauerkraut in bottom of pan and sprinkle with the brown sugar.
Place ribs and potatoes over sauerkraut; add water.
Cover; bring pressure to 10 pounds and cook for 20 min.
Reduce pressure normally 5 minutes, then place pan under faucet.
recipes.name: Spareribs, Sauerkraut and Potatoes

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club

ingredients.name: large slice of ham
ingredients.raw: 1 large slice of ham, cut 1/2 inch thick

instructions: Cut the ham into six servings the size of the pineapple slices.
Place in a flat baking pan with a slice of pineapple on top of each ham slice.
Make six sweet potato cakes and put one on top of each of the above.
This may be topped with a marshmallow, if desired.
Mix the sugar, flour, butter, and pineapple juice together and pour over each serving.
Sprinkle each serving with crushed wheaties.
Bake one hour at 325f.
recipes.name: Baked Ham Special

author: Mrs Lyle Garrett
instructions: Cook noodles in plenty of boiling, salted water until just tender.
Cook onion and celery in butter until tender, blend in flour, salt and mustard.
Ada milk.
Cook and stir until thickened.
Blend in worcestershire sauce, tabasco, flaked tuna, pimiento, parsley, olives, and cheese.
Mix with cooked noodles: and turn into a greased 3-quart casserole, top with buttered crumbs.
Bake one hour in moderate oven, 360 degrees.
recipes.name: Tuna Casserole

author: Mrs M M Lunning

ingredients.name: remaining milk
ingredients.raw: 1 cup remaining milk, in baking dish

instructions: Cut fish fillets into serving size pieces.
Brush pieces with melted butter and sprinkle with salt, glutamate, and pepper.
Place in shallow baking dish and completely cover with milk.
Bake, uncovered 1 n a moderate oven, 350 degrees, for 30 minutes.
Remove fish to warm platter and keep warm, to serve over fish, make cream sauce as follows: melt butter and remove from heat.
Blend in flour until smooth and add 1 cup remaining milk gradually.
Return to heat and stir continually until thickened.
Add seasonings and if desired.
A, bit of parsley or pimiento for color.
recipes.name: Baked Fillets Margo

author: Mrs
instructions: Dice onion and celery and brown in oil.
Add remaining ingredients except rice and simmer 2 -3 hours.
Before serving add rice and cook 20 minutes longer or until rice is tender.
recipes.name: Rezuto

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Pare whole melons; cut a slice from the top of each and reserve; scoop out seeds; shave bottom of each melon slightly so that it stands up well.
Blend milk with cheese- until smooth; use to frost melons and the reserved tops; sprinkle with nuts.
Set melons in center of a serving platter; fill with some of the fruit; surround with green leaves and rest of the fruit.
Set tops in place; refrigerate.
To serve: remove tops of melons; cut melons into wedges from top to bottom; spoon fruit onto each wedge.
Pass french dressing, if you wish.
recipes.name: Beauty Fruit Salad

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Toast bread squares in shallow pan in 300f.
Oven for 20 minutes, or until golden brown, turning often.
Tear lettuce into bite-size pieces.
Rub salad bowl with garlic.
Just before serving, sprinkle cheese over greens.
Pour over greens the salad oil mixed with worcestershire sauce, salt, and pepper.
Toss gently.
Break whole raw egg over greens; pour lemon juice over the salad.
Toss until all of the egg disappears and all of the greens are shiny.
Sprinkle bread crumbs over top of the salad; toss lightly, and serve at once.
recipes.name: Caesar Salad II

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Mix together flour, sugar, egg, soda, salt and drained fruit cocktail.
Place in ungreased 8-inch square pan.
On top of this spread a mixture of the brown sugar and nuts.
Bake in moderately slow oven (300 degrees) one hour.
When cool, cut in squares and serve with whipped cream.
recipes.name: Fruit Cocktail Torte

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: In large saucepan, add onion and potatoes.
Cook covered for 15 minutes or until the potatoes are tender.
Blend in milk, and salt.
Heat, but do not boil.
recipes.name: Potato Soup IV

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Cook the noodles in boiling, salted water to which the garlic has been added, for 10 minutes.
Drain.
Mix, with other ingredients.
Put in a buttered casserole, and bake 45 minutes, in a moderate oven (350 f).
Sprinkle generously with cheese and paprika.
Return to oven for 5 minutes.
recipes.name: Scalloped Noodles, Hungarian Style

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Cream butter and add sugar gradually.
Add berries and nuts.
Mix well.
Fold wafer crumbs into beaten egg whites.
Arrange alternate layers of wafer mixture and fruit.
Chill at least 12 hours.
Cut into squares and serve with whipped cream and garnish with a whole berry, if desired.
recipes.name: Virginia Strawberry Supreme

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Cut chocolate cake in half.
Place on a board or cookie sheet covered with paper.
Beat the egg whites with the vanilla and cream of tartar until frothy.
Add sugar gradually and continue beating until stiff and glossy (holds peaks when beater is removed).
Place cooled cake on several thicknesses of wrapping paper on a board and pan.
Cut neopolitan ice cream into 3 equal pieces and place on cake.
Cover cake and ice cream with meringue.
Make sure the ice cream is completely sealed in.
Bake in very hot oven (500f) for 3 minutes, until meringue is delicately brown.
Slip from board to platter.
Serve at once.
recipes.name: Baked Alaska

author: Mrs F Kalm
instructions: Drain liquid from salmon and to it add strained tomatoes, salt, sugar, and pickling spices.
Bring mixture to a boil and strain.
Saute onion in butter until tender but not brown.
Add strained tomato mixture.
Remove any outside skin from salmon, cut in slices.
Lay slices in tomato mixture and simmer for 30 minutes.
recipes.name: Point Adams Special

author: Mrs Mary Lum
instructions: Grind sturgeon twice, add remaining ingredients except onion, whip together thoroughly, add onion and mix.
Drop by small teaspoon into boiling chicken broth, and cook a few minutes until done.
For fish patties, eliminate chicken broth, form fish mixture into patties and fry on both aides in a small amount of peanut or salad oil.
recipes.name: Sturgeon Balls II

author: Anne Strachan
instructions: Combine all ingredients, except lettuce, being careful not to break the fish into small pieces.
Chill.
Serve in lettuce cups.
recipes.name: Rockfish Salad

author: Mrs Clifford Olsen

ingredients.name: large carrots
ingredients.raw: 3 large carrots, cut in 3/4 in. cubes

ingredients.name: fresh or thawed frozen cod
ingredients.raw: 1 1/2 pound fresh or thawed frozen cod, filets

ingredients.name: potatoes
ingredients.raw: 1 1/2 pound potatoes, cut in 3/4 inch cubes

ingredients.name: celery seed
ingredients.raw: 1/2 teaspoon celery seed, or 1/4 cup diced celery

instructions: Saute bacon in deep kettle or dutch oven until lightly browned.
Remove bacon and set aside.
In same kettle, saute onion slices until tender.
Add fish, cut in 2 1/2 inch pieces, add next seven ingredients.
Simmer covered, until vegetables are tender, about 25 minutes.
Add tomatoes, heat through.
Garnish with parsley and bacon bite.
recipes.name: Codfish Stew

author: Mrs C M Love
instructions: Marinate fish fillets in french dressing to cover for 1 hour.
Saute eggplant slices in oil.
Remove slices, and add parsley, onions, and seasonings, and saute.
Oil a 2 quart casserole, and alternate layers of sauteed seasonings, egg plant and fish fillets.
Top with tomato sauce that has been mixed with 1 can water and mushrooms.
Bake in hot oven, 450 degrees for 20 minutes.
Serve with garlic bread.
recipes.name: Armenian

author: Mrs Harold Johnson

ingredients.name: medium potatoes
ingredients.raw: 6 medium potatoes, (boiled and mashed without milk)

instructions: Boil halibut: bone, work until fine.
Add mashed potatoes, beat well.
Add sauce, then egg yolks, mix well.
Season to taste with salt, pepper and mace.
Fold in beaten egg whites.
Bake an hour in a moderate oven in buttered casserole.
Serve with melted butter.
recipes.name: Norwegian Halibut Casserole

author: Suzanne Englund
instructions: Soften gelatin in cold water and dissolve in hot tomato soup.
Cool.
Thoroughly combine remaining ingredients and gradually stir in gelatin mixture.
Tour into 2 1/2 quart fish mold.
Chill until firm.
Unmold and serve on crisp lettuce leaves with a french dressing.
recipes.name: De Luxe Shrimp Salad

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Sear meat in a little butter.
Work up with fork so it is very fine.
Simmer onions and celery with meat over low heat, and then add the soups and blend together.
Mix with prepared noodles.
Add milk if more moisture is needed.
Bake tor one hour.
Sprinkle potato chips on top for a crust, if desired.
recipes.name: Tomato-less Casserole

author: Susan Latvala

ingredients.name: cooked elbow or shell macaroni
ingredients.raw: 4 cup cooked elbow or shell macaroni

ingredients.name: cooked shrimp
ingredients.raw: 1 cup cooked shrimp, or 2 4 1/2 oz. cans

instructions: Combine ingredients and mix in mayonnaise to which a small amount of chili sauce has been added.
recipes.name: Macaroni-Shrimp Salad

author: Mrs A E Young
instructions: Blend crab meat, celery, egg, and mayonnaise, adding seasoning to taste.
Cut rolls lengthwise, remove part of bread, butter and fill with salad.
Serve on crisp lettuce with sliced dill pickle.
recipes.name: Crab Meat Rolls

author: Mrs Bessie Miller
instructions: Saute bacon and onions together for five minutes, do not brown.
Drain off fat.
Add bacon and onions to potatoes, water, salt, and butter.
Cook until potatoes are done.
Add clams and milk.
Heat just to boiling point and serve.
(Do not boil).
recipes.name: Clam Chowder II

author: Mrs Harold Johnson

ingredients.name: salt pork
ingredients.raw: 2 slices salt pork, or bacon diced

instructions: Brown salt pork or bacon with onions.
Add water and potatoes, carrots, and celery.
Cook until vegetables are tender, season with salt and pepper.
Add milk and clams, and simmer until hot.
This chowder may be thickened if preferred.
recipes.name: Mother's Clam Chowder

author: Mrs Jennie Olson
instructions: Saute bacon until golden but not brown.
Add onions and celery tops to bacon and cook until onion and celery are wilted.
Add next 5 ingredients, simmer until potatoes are tender, about 1/2 hour.
The base is now completed.
Melt butter and blend in flour.
Remove from heat and slowly stir in milk.
Return to heat and cook until slightly thickened.
Add clam chowder base and heat through but do not boil, add a little butter and paprika to taste.
Serves 8.
recipes.name: Clam Chowder

author: Mrs G Wallis Ohler
instructions: Arrange halibut steaks in shallow pyrex baking dish, and pour over them the remaining sauce.
Broil until tender (about 15 minutes).
Do not turn steaks.
Garnish with paprika and parsley before serving.
recipes.name: Broiled Halibut Supreme

author: Mrs Clifford Olsen

ingredients.name: fresh or thawed
ingredients.raw: 1 1/2 pound fresh or thawed, frozen cod fillets

ingredients.name: peeled white potatoes
ingredients.raw: 1 1/2 pound peeled white potatoes, cut in 3/4 inch cubes

ingredients.name: celery seed
ingredients.raw: 1/2 teaspoon celery seed, or 1/2 cup diced celery

ingredients.name: large peeled carrots
ingredients.raw: 3 large peeled carrots, cut in 3/4 inch cubes

instructions: Saute bacon in deep kettle or dutch oven until lightly browned; then set bacon aside.
In same kettle, saute onions until tender.
Add fish cut in 2 1/2 inch pieces; add next seven ingredients.
Simmer, covered, until vegetables are tender, about 25 minutes.
Add tomatoes, heat through.
Garnish with parsley and bacon bits.
recipes.name: Cod Fish Stew (Danish)

author: Mrs Andrew Young
instructions: Combine first 5 ingredients.
Chill.
Add cabbage and toss.
Add potato chips just before serving, toss.
Heap in lettuce-lined bowl.
Garnish with eggs and tomato wedges.
recipes.name: Seafood Surprise Salad

author: Mrs J H Wood
instructions: Combine first 5 ingredients.
Chill.
Add cabbage and toss.
Add potato chips just before serving, toss.
Heap in lettuce-lined bowl.
Garnish with eggs and tomato wedges.
recipes.name: Tuna Crunch Salad

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club

ingredients.name: mushroom soup
ingredients.raw: 1 can mushroom soup, or chicken soup

instructions: Brown hamburger and onion.
Cook celery in bean sprout juice.
Mix soup, sprouts, hamburger and onion, celery and juice together.
Put in a baking dish and sprinkle one can of chow mein noodles on top.
Bake one hour at 350f.
recipes.name: Chow Mein Hamburger Casserole

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Slit franks lengthwise, but don't cut completely through.
Fill with fillings.
Wrap strip of bacon tightly around each frank, covering slit well.
Pin with pieces of toothpick.
Place in cold skillet.
Fry over medium heat, turning often, until bacon is crisp.
Pour off fat.
Add tomato sauce, sugar, and mustard.
Blend well.
Simmer 10 to 15 minutes.
recipes.name: Fancy Frank Fry

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Drain oysters over bowl to save juice.
Remove bits of shell from oysters individually.
Butter 1 quart casserole.
Alternate layers of oysters and crumbs, seasoning with salt and pepper and a little scraped onion.
Reserve crumbs for top.
Pour in oyster juice and milk enough to reach top layer of oysters.
More milk may be added later if mixture seems dry.
Sprinkle with buttered crumbs.
Bake in moderate oven 350f about 30 minutes until golden brown and oysters are ruffled.
Over cooking makes them tough and dry.
recipes.name: Scaloped Oysters

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Remove pits from prunes and mash to a pulp.
Add lemon juice, peel, and 2 tablespoon sugar; blend well.
Add remaining 2 tablespoon sugar to egg whites; beat until stiff.
Fold prune mixture slowly into egg whites.
Pile lightly in greased baking dish.
Bake in moderate oven (350f) 20-30 minutes.
recipes.name: Baked Prune Whip

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Mix white sugar, flour, milk, raisins, baking powder and put in greased casserole.
Mix together brown sugar, butter and hot water.
Pour over batter.
Bake for 45 minutes.
Can be served in its own sauce or with cream added to pudding.
recipes.name: Boston Pudding

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club

ingredients.name: narrow noodles
ingredients.raw: 32 ounce narrow noodles, wider for more servings, cooked

ingredients.name: American cheese
ingredients.raw: 2 pound American cheese, diced in 1/2 inch cubes

ingredients.name: crisp chow mein noodles
ingredients.raw: 1 cup crisp chow mein noodles, for topping

instructions: Brown the onions in butter or drippings, add beef and brown.
Mix all ingredients.
Pour the mushroom soup over all.
Bake in greased casserole 1 hour at 375 f.
Put on the topping for the last 15 minute.
One may use crumbled shredded wheat in place of chow mein noodles.
Add topping.
recipes.name: Chicken Noodle Casserole

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Sift together: flour, sugar, baking powder, salt.
Add to the dry ingredients and beat well for 2 minutes: butter, pecans or walnuts, milk, vanilla.
Pour into an 8 x 8 inch pan.
Mix together and sprinkle over the batter in the pan: 1 cup sugar, cocoa.
Pour over the cake batter: water bake for 35 minutes in 350f.
Oven.
Cool and serve with whipped cream.
recipes.name: Chocolate Upside-down Cake

author: United States Department of Agriculture

ingredients.name: sliced beef
ingredients.raw: 1 pound sliced beef, lamb, or pork liver

ingredients.name: fresh or canned (No. 2 can) tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 2 1/2 cup fresh or canned (No. 2 can) tomatoes

instructions: Dip liver slices in flour and cube at once.
Brown liver in the fat; add onion, green pepper, garlic clove, mushrooms, tomatoes, salt, and pepper.
Cover and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add cooked noodles or spaghetti and cook 10 minutes longer.
Or place noodles or spaghetti and liver mixture in alternate layers in a greased baking dish.
Top with bread crumbs.
Bake in a moderately hot oven (375f) 15 to 20 minutes or until mixture is heated through and crumbs are browned.
recipes.name: Spanish Liver

author: United States Department of Agriculture

ingredients.name: medium size tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 6 medium size tomatoes, ripe or green

instructions: Remove stem ends and quarter tomatoes (peel ripe tomatoes, if preferred).
Add onion for flavor, if desired.
Cover and cook until tender, 10 to 20 minutes for ripe tomatoes, 20 to 35 for green.
Season with salt; a little pepper; sugar, if desired, 1/2 teaspoon for ripe tomatoes, 1 tablespoon for green; and fat.
For variety, add bread crumbs before serving or top with toasted bread cubes.
recipes.name: Stewed Tomatoes II

author: United States Department of Agriculture

ingredients.name: fresh or canned (No. 2 can) tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 2 1/2 cup fresh or canned (No. 2 can) tomatoes

instructions: Cook together celery.
Green pepper, and onion in the fat, 8 to 10 minutes, stirring frequently.
Blend in the flour.
Add tomatoes, cheese, and salt.
Cook over low heal; stir constantly until mixture thickens and cheese melts.
Gradually add some of the tomato mixture to beaten eggs; mix well, then pour all back into the tomato mixture.
Continue to cook over low heat; stir constantly until thickened and creamy (2 to 3 minutes).
If desired, add a few dashes of tabasco sauce.
Serve on toast or crackers.
recipes.name: Tomato Rabbit

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club

ingredients.name: chopped green onions
ingredients.raw: 3/4 cup chopped green onions, or 1/2 cup chopped onions

instructions: Cook potatoes in boiling water.
Peel and dice.
Add vinegar and seasonings.
Fry bacon until crisp.
Cook eggs 4 minutes.
Combine potatoes, bacon, 2 tablespoon bacon fat, soft-cooked eggs, and chopped onions.
Mix well.
Serve hot salad on a bed of lettuce with big frankfurters.
recipes.name: Hot German Potato Salad

author: United States Department of Agriculture

ingredients.name: fresh or canned (No. 2 can) tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 2 1/2 cup fresh or canned (No. 2 can) tomatoes

instructions: Soften gelatin in the water.
Cook tomatoes, onion, and bay leaf about 20 minutes for fresh tomatoes, 10 for canned.
Press through a sieve and measure 1 3/4 cups (if not enough, add boiling water).
Add hot, sieved tomatoes to gelatin and stir until gelatin is dissolved.
Season with sugar, salt, pepper, and lemon juice.
Chill.
When gelatin mixture begins to stiffen, add cucumber and celery.
Mix well.
Pour into a mold or pan rinsed in cold water.
Chill until firm.
Serve with salad dressing on lettuce or other salad greens.
recipes.name: Jellied Tomato Salad

author: United States Department of Agriculture
instructions: Combine lima beans with white sauce and cheese.
Pour into baking dish and place quartered tomatoes cut side down on bean mixture, bake in moderate oven (350f) 20 to 30 minutes or until tomatoes are tender.
recipes.name: Lima Bean-Tomato Casserole

author: United States Department of Agriculture
instructions: Combine tomatoes with milk.
Heat slowly to serving temperature.
Add salt, a little pepper, and fat.
recipes.name: Quick Cream of Tomato Soup

author: United States Department of Agriculture

ingredients.name: fresh or canned (No. 2 1/2 can) tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 3 1/2 cup fresh or canned (No. 2 1/2 can) tomatoes

instructions: Cook bacon until crisp, remove from fat.
And drain.
Combine 2 tablespoons of the bacon drippings with tomatoes, green pepper and onion.
Bring to boiling, add about 3 cups cooked rice, cook 10 - 20 minutes or add 1 cup uncooked rice and 2 cups water, and cook gently 40 to 45 minutes or until rice is tender.
Add more water if mixture becomes dry.
Season with salt and pepper.
Add bacon.
recipes.name: Savory Rice with Tomatoes

author: United States Department of Agriculture

ingredients.name: fresh or canned (No 2 1/2 can) tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 3 1/2 cup fresh or canned (No 2 1/2 can) tomatoes

ingredients.name: minced green pepper
ingredients.raw: 2 tablespoon minced green pepper, if desired

instructions: Combine tomatoes (ripe or green), onion, green pepper, salt, pepper, and sugar if used.
Place in a baking dish alternate layers of tomato mixture and bread crumbs, ending with bread crumbs (for a thinner mixture, omit 1 cup of the crumbs).
Dot with fat.
Bake in a moderately hot oven (375f) 20 to 30 minutes for ripe tomatoes, 30 to 45 for green.
If desired, sprinkle 1/2 cup grated cheese over the top for the last 10 to 15 minutes of baking.
recipes.name: Scalloped Tomatoes II

author: United States Department of Agriculture

ingredients.name: meat drippings
ingredients.raw: 3 tablespoon meat drippings, or other fat

instructions: Cook the onion in the fat.
Add green tomatoes, cover, and cook until tender.
Add meat and heat thoroughly.
If the mixture is too thick, thin it slightly with meat broth, gravy, or water.
Season to taste with curry powder and salt.
Serve with flaky boiled rice or noodles.
recipes.name: Curry of Meat with Green Tomatoes

author: United States Department of Agriculture

ingredients.name: fresh or canned (No. 2 can) tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 3 1/2 cup fresh or canned (No. 2 can) tomatoes

instructions: Cook potatoes in fat until lightly browned.
Add onion, green pepper, tomatoes.
Cover and cook until potatoes are tender.
Add cooked fish, cut in about 2-inch pieces.
Season with salt, and pepper.
Cook about 5 minutes longer.
recipes.name: Fish-Tomato Stew

author: United States Department of Agriculture
instructions: Slice tomatoes about 1/2 inch thick.
Dip in mixture of bread crumbs or flour, salt, and a little pepper.
Cook in a small amount of fat until brown on both sides.
If desired, dip tomatoes in beaten egg, then in flour or bread crumbs before cooking.
recipes.name: Fried Tomatoes

author: United States Department of Agriculture

ingredients.name: fat
ingredients.raw: 2 tablespoon fat, beef fat may be used

instructions: Boll meat in mixture of salt, pepper, and 2 tablespoons of the flour.
Brown in the fat.
Add onion; cook until lightly browned.
Pour in 2 cups of the water, cover, and simmer about 1 hour or until meat is almost tender.
Wash, remove stem ends, and quarter the tomatoes; add with potatoes, carrots, and 1 cup water to the meat.
Cover and cook until vegetables and meat are tender.
Add more water as needed.
Blend remaining 2 tablespoons flour with the 1/4 cup water; add to stew, and cook until slightly thickened.
recipes.name: Green Tomato Meat Stew

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Place in a greased 8" square pan: apples.
Blend until crumbly; then spread over apples: brown sugar (packed), flour, oats, nutmeg, butter.
Bake at 375 tor 30-35 minutes, until apples are tender and topping is golden brown.
recipes.name: Apple Crisp

author: United States Department of Agriculture

ingredients.name: ground beef
ingredients.raw: 1 pound ground beef, or other lean meat

ingredients.name: fresh or canned (No. 2 can) tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 2 1/2 cup fresh or canned (No. 2 can) tomatoes

ingredients.name: chopped or coarsely shredded cabbage
ingredients.raw: 4 cup chopped or coarsely shredded cabbage

instructions: Brown the meat in fat.
Add onion and celery; cook 5 minutes.
Add tomatoes, salt, and pepper : bring to boiling.
Place alternating layers of cabbage and meat mixture in a baking dish.
Top with bread crumbs.
Bake in a moderately hot oven (375f) 40 to 45 minutes.
recipes.name: Beef, Tomato and Cabbage Scallop

author: United States Department of Agriculture
instructions: Wash tomatoes, ripe or green, and remove stem ends.
Cut tomatoes in 2, and place cut side up in shallow pan or on broiling pan.
Brush with melted fat and sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Place under direct heat with top of tomatoes about 3 inches below tip of flame or broiler unit.
Broil until tender, 10 to 15 minutes for ripe tomatoes, 15 to 25 for green.
If desired, sprinkle with fine bread crumbs or grated cheese for the last few minutes of broiling.
recipes.name: Broiled Tomatoes

author: United States Department of Agriculture

ingredients.name: fresh or canned (No. 2 can) tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 2 1/2 cup fresh or canned (No. 2 can) tomatoes

ingredients.name: fat
ingredients.raw: 1/4 cup fat, chicken fat may be used

instructions: Cut chicken into serving pieces.
Roll in mixture of the flour, salt, pepper, and paprika.
Brown in melted fat.
Add onion; cook 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the water, cover, and simmer about 1 hour or until almost tender, adding more water if necessary.
Stir occasionally to keep from sticking.
Add green pepper and tomatoes.
Simmer about 30 minutes longer.
Serve on seasoned hot noodles or rice.
recipes.name: Chicken Creole

author: United States Department of Agriculture

ingredients.name: fresh or canned (No. 2 1/2 can) tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 2 cup fresh or canned (No. 2 1/2 can) tomatoes

instructions: Soak beans overnight in cold water or about 5 hours in lukewarm water to cover.
Add onion, garlic, green pepper, bacon drippings, tomatoes, and salt; and simmer for 2 hours in the soaking water.
Add more water if needed during cooking.
Add t he chili powder, stirring as little as possible to avoid mashing the beans.
Place in a baking dish or bean pot, cover, and bake in a moderate oven (350f) for about 2 hours.
Uncover during last part of the cooking if brown beans are desired.
If preferred, use lima or navy beans in place of the kidney beans.
recipes.name: Chili Kidney Beans with Tomatoes

author: United States Department of Agriculture
instructions: Cook together the tomatoes, bay leaf, onion, and cloves about 20 minutes for fresh tomatoes, 10 for canned.
Press through a sieve.
Blend the fat, and and sugar (if used); gradually add the cooled, sieved tomatoes.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly for about 5 minutes.
Season with salt and peeper.
If desired, sprinkle with finely chopped parsley and serve with toasted bread cubes.
recipes.name: Clear Tomato Soup

author: United States Department of Agriculture

ingredients.name: fresh or canned (No. 2 1/2 can) tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 3 1/2 cup fresh or canned (No. 2 1/2 can) tomatoes, .

instructions: Cook together the tomatoes and onions about 20 minutes for fresh tomatoes, 10 for canned.
Press through a sieve.
Melt the fat; blend in flour and sugar (if used).
Gradually add cooled, sieved tomatoes.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until thickened.
Gradually add tomato mixture to milk, stirring constantly.
Heat slowly to serving temperature.
Add salt.
Serve at once.
recipes.name: Cream of Tomato Soup III

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Melt butter in heavy sauce pan.
Stir in the onion, cabbage, salt, and dill.
Cover and simmer until just tender, about 15 minutes.
Pour sour cream over cabbage.
Serve hot.
recipes.name: Dill Cabbage

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club
instructions: Drain oil from tuna and break into chunk size pieces.
Add well drained pineapple.
Season with salt.
Marinate with small amount or mayonnaise or french dressing for 30 minutes.
Just prior to serving toss marinated mixture with shredded head lettuce and chow mein noodles.
Serve immediately in lettuce cups or on bed of endive or other similar green.
recipes.name: Tuna-Pineapple Toss

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club

ingredients.name: French cut string beans
ingredients.raw: 1 box French cut string beans, or other fresh vegetables

instructions: Season pan by browning in hot fat, sliced garlic.
Remove garlic from pan.
Brown the pork, out in small pieces.
Add french cut carrots and string beans.
Season with salt and pepper and simmer for about 5 minutes.
Add cut up celery and onions.
Season with salt and pepper.
Cover end simmer for about 20 minutes or until the vegetables are nearly cooked.
Uncover, and add the mushroom sauce and soy sauce.
Cook until done.
recipes.name: American Chinese Chop Suey

author: Stout State College Home Economics Club

ingredients.name: beef chuck
ingredients.raw: 2 pound beef chuck, cut in cubes

instructions: Thoroughly brown meat on all sides in hot fat, add boiling water, lemon juice, worcestershire sauce, garlic, onion, bay leaves, and seasonings.
Simmer 2 hours.
Stir occasionally to keep from sticking.
Add carrots and potatoes (cubed potatoes may be used if desired).
Continue cooking 20-30 minutes or until vegetables are done.
Remove meat and vegetables.
Thicken liquid for gravy.
recipes.name: Country Kitchen Brown Stew

recipes.description: Casio in pastelletto means roughly “cheese treat” in vernacular Italian. It is a medieval recipe and the taste changes a lot depending on the cheese you choose, so there are no exact quantities for the ingredients, and the dish may be considered a main one or a sweet (I think it was probably a dessert, though). You will probably have to do some trial and error before you get a good result.

ingredients.name: cheese. Use a cheese that is mid-aged
ingredients.note: not too savoury and not too delicate.
ingredients.raw: 2 slice cheese. Use a cheese that is mid-aged, not too savoury and not too delicate.

instructions: Place the cheese in a pan with frying butter or lard.
Immediately sprinkle sugar and cinnamon all over it.
As soon as it softens, remove it from the pan.
Serve warm.
recipes.name: Casio in pastelletto

instructions: Mix eggs, sugar, milk, flour, yeast and mistrà and knead them in a soft dough.
Roll out to about 1.5 cm thick.
Cut it to squares about 5 cm long.
Fry them for about 5 minutes.
Dry them and sweeten with sugar or honey.
recipes.name: Castagnole

recipes.description: Italian traditional pizza is Neapolitan pizza. This is not it - it’s a very different dish that just happens to share the same name (as is the case with many Italian traditional recipes).

ingredients.name: Stuffing: 500 g boiled herbs (e.g. spinach
ingredients.raw: Stuffing: 500 g boiled herbs (e.g. spinach, chicory, ribwort)

instructions: Carefully dry the herbs and cut them finely.
Mix them with ricotta, salt, pepper and nutmeg.
Knead flour with warm water and a little salt, and oil or lard.
Add softened butter and yeast and knead a soft dough.
Divide the dough in two parts and roll out each of them to a thickness of about 1 cm.
Place the first disc on baking paper in a baking tray. Cover it with the stuffing, leaving about 1.5 cm free surface all around.
Cover with the other disc and stick them together all over the border. If it’s difficult, you may wet it wit a few drops of water.
Cover with a cloth and let it rise.
Pierce gently all over the top layer with a fork.
Preheat the oven to 180 °C.
Place the pie in the oven and cook for 30 minutes.
recipes.name: Herbs pizza

instructions: Peel off the ginger and cut it to small pieces.
Crush ginger and cardamom seeds.
Bring 1 l water to boiling.
Turn off the stove.
Add ginger, cardamom seeds, black tea and milk to the water and cover the pot.
Wait 5-10 minutes for infusion.
Serve with a teaspoon sugar per cup. You may want to sieve, or wait for the particles to precipitate to the bottom of the cups.
recipes.name: Indian tea

recipes.description: “Limoncini” literally means “little lemons” but is a sweet, whereas “arancini” means “little oranges” but is a main dish (typical of southern Italy). Please, don’t confuse these dishes: they are very different and you may find yourself on the wrong side of a feud.

ingredients.name: Stuffing: 3 lemon untreated. Make sure the skin is edible!
ingredients.raw: Stuffing: 3 lemon untreated. Make sure the skin is edible!

instructions: Cut the butter and let it soften.
Dissolve the yeast in warm milk and softened butter.
Add sugar and stir.
Add the other dough ingredients and knead for a few minutes until you have a soft dough.
Cover the dough and let it rise for about an hour.
Meanwhile, grate the skin of the lemons.
Add sugar and mix.
Store the stuffing in a dry place.
Roll out the dough to 1 or 2 a rectangles about 3 mm thick.
Spread the stuffing on all the surface of the dough.
Roll up the rectangle(s) tightly.
Cut the rolls in slices about 1 cm thick.
Lay them on baking paper in an oven tray.
Let them rise again for another hour.
Preheat the oven to 180 °C.
Cook for about 20 minutes. Pay attention not to overcook: check after about 10 minutes.
recipes.name: Limoncini

recipes.description: Fritatem pomeranciis means “orange omelette” in Latin, but in fact it is a cream made by cooking eggs, which do not coagulate because of orange juice. It is a medieval recipe, so it had to adapted because some ingredients are no longer available. Some versions include the juice of half a lemon, but the result is rather sour: if you like it, I recommend adding only a few drops thereof.
instructions: In a bowl, beat the eggs with sugar, orange juice, and a pinch of salt.
Cook in a pan with frying oil.
Serve warm.
recipes.name: Fritatem pomeranciis

recipes.description: Fumé is a sauce for pasta, typical of central Italy. It is intended to be used in great amounts. Quantities in this recipe are calculated for servings of 100 g pasta each.
instructions: Cut onion to small pieces and pancetta to cubes about 1 cm long.
Fry them on low fire until onion darkens.
Add milk cream and tomato sauce and stir.
Add a small pinch of sugar, then season with salt and paprica. Also add parsely, if you like it.
Cook stirring slowly on low fire for 10 minutes or until the sauce thickens.
recipes.name: Fumé sauce

recipes.description: Purée may be used as a main course, or as a side dish: for example, it is very good with beans. Ingredients below ar calculated for the main course, they should be halved for the side dish.
instructions: Peel the potatoes and cut them to small pieces. The smaller, the faster to cook.
Put them in a pot and cover with water.
Bring to boil and cook until potatoes are soft.
Drain and mash with a fork.
Warm up milk, but don’t let it boil.
Still on the fire, add butter and mashed potatoes, and optionally grated cheese, and stir until uniform.
Keep stirring on the fire to thicken as you like.
recipes.name: Potato purée

instructions: Set aside about 1/6 of the shortcrust pastry and roll out the remaining so that it is slightly larger than the tray.
Place rolled shortcrust pastry in a baking mold and arrange the border along those of the mold, so that the pastry can contain jam.
Pour the jam in the shortcrust pastry “container” you just created and spread it with a spoon.
Use the pastry you set aside to create rolls and place them in a criss-cross pattern all over the surface. Push them through the jam to the bottom.
Preheat the oven to 180 °C.
Cook in the oven for about 45 minutes.
Let the cake cool down to room temperature before removing from the mold, otherwise it will easily break.
recipes.name: Crostata

instructions: Squeeze the lemons. Remove the seeds, but keep both juice and pulp.
Put in a pot the sugar, 175 g of lemon juice and pulp, and 300 ml of water. For the freezing to work as expected, it’s important that you don’t alter the proportions.
Boil for 10 minutes. You should obtain a syrup with fibers floating in it: if you see pieces bigger than a few millimeters, get rid of them with a blender.
Add 700 ml of water and stir.
Wait for the solution to cool down to room temperature.
Pour it in a container that can be frozen. Plastic ones are usually a good choice, whereas glass ones are often cracked by the increase in water volume.
Put it in the freezer.

Now, for the most boring part: you must prevent the separation of the ingredients due to the freezing process, and the formation of one huge ice block. To do so, every 2 hours you must stir vigorously with a fork (if you need, after the first 6 hours you can usually decrease to once every 4 hours). Take some special cares: stir even if you don’t see any ice yet: there may already be small crystals
if you find any ice block, make sure to break them down
don’t worry if the ice melts when you stir: the water stays cold and will freeze again fast enough

Depending on the temperature, the whole thing may take much time to freeze: it’s not unusual for it to require up to 20 hours. That’s expected and depends also on the amount of sugar and fruit. Granita is ready when in the container there are only ice crystals: no liquid water and no ice blocks. You can then use a spoon to serve in small cups.
If you don’t consume all granita at once, it may freeze to a block. If that happens, just scratch it with the spoon or break it with a fork.
recipes.name: Granita

recipes.description: Shortcrust pastry is the base recipe for many baked sweets. The ingredients below are roughly enough for an 8 slices crostata, but servings are reduced if the dough is used alone (e. g. for biscuits).
instructions: Cut the butter in slices, put it in a large bowl and leave it at room temperature until it’s easy to knead.

Add the powdered sugar and knead until uniform. From now on, pay attention to knead fast enough so that the butter doesn’t melt. If it does, place the dough in the fridge for 15-30 minutes before going on.
Add the eggs and knead. It’s not necessary that the dough is perfectly uniform.

Add all the flour and knead. Don’t knead too much after adding the flour, or the dough won’t reach its typical crumbliness. The dough is ready when it’s uniform and the surface cracks when you bend it.
Roll out the dough on baking paper. Don’t make it too thin: it’s not supposed to rise, so it would burn during cooking.
Keep in the fridge for 15-30 minutes before use.
recipes.name: Shortcrust pastry

instructions: Beat the eggs in a bowl.
Heat broth to boiling.
Pour the eggs in the broth without removing from the stovetop.
Stir with a whip until eggs coagulate.
Serve broth and eggs together.
If you want, you may season the dish with some olive oil.
recipes.name: Stracciatella soup

ingredients.name: parsley (fresh is best
ingredients.note: fresh is best, dry is fine
ingredients.raw: parsley (fresh is best, dry is fine)

instructions: Cut all the vegetables in half on the long side. You may remove the seeds and some of the pulp from the tomato and the courgette, but not too much or you will get just burnt vegetable skin.
Place the vegetables on baking paper in a baking tray.
Sprinkle parsley over the vegetables, then, if you want, a little salt.
Add copious grated bread, then sprinkle Parmigiano cheese all over it.
Add enough olive oil to wet all the bread. If you don’t use enough oil, grated bread won’t stick together and may burn.
Bake for about 45 minutes in the oven pre-heated to 170 °C.
recipes.name: Stuffed vegetables

instructions: Separate albumen and yolks and beat the latter with the sugar in a bowl.
Add the mascarpone and stir until uniform.
In another bowl, beat the albumens until stiff.
Add beaten albumens to the mascarpone cream gradually, stirring gently to not destroy the foam.
Cover the bottom of a baking tray with a layer of cream.
Cover it with a layer of savoiardi biscuits soaked in coffee.

Add another layer of cream, then another of coffee-soaked savoiardi. Savoiardi of the second layer should be orthogonal to those of the first, so that the structure is more solid and slices collapse less when they are moved.
Add one last layer of cream.
Sprinkle cocoa powder on top.
Store in the fridge for three hours.
recipes.name: Tiramisù

instructions: Beat the yolks with the sugar.
Add the butter and stir until uniform.
Add the flour. You may sieve it to prevent lumps. Stir until uniform.
Add the yogurt and stir until uniform.
Beat the albumens in another bowl, then add them to the compound and stir until uniform.
The compound should now be thick, but still liquid enough to be poured. If it’s too thick, you may adjust it by adding yogurt or milk.
Add the yeast and stir.

Pour into a mould. If you want to add fruit, cut it to small pieces or slices and add it after 2/3 of the compound, then cover with the remaining. Alternatively, you may add it on top: it will sink during cooking.
You may now sprinkle powdered sugar on top, to create a thin, sweet crust
Cook in pre-heated oven at 180 °C. This will take about 45 minutes, but start checking frequently after 30.
recipes.name: Yogurt cake

recipes.description: This soup is also known as Lohikeitto.
instructions: Wash, clean, and dice all vegetables.
Remove scales from salmon fillet or remove skin entirely, up to you. Dice.
In a pot, melt butter. Add diced leeks and cook on medium-high about 5 minutes until the leeks wilt a bit.
Add water (or stock) and other vegetables. Bring to a boil and cook on medium heat about 10-15 minutes until the potatoes are ready.
Add diced salmon fillet and heavy cream. Cook for additional 5-10 minutes to cook the salmon.
Add salt and pepper to taste at the end. Serve with dill as garnish.
recipes.name: Finnish Salmon Soup

recipes.description: Damper is a no-yeast australian campfire bread. It is easy to scale up and down.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C). Grease a baking sheet.
Mix all the ingredients together, adding a half cup of water and a teaspoon salt.
Knead the bread on a floured surface.
Put the bread into the oven for 25 minutes, then lower the temprature to 175 degrees C for 5 to 10 minutes
recipes.name: Damper

recipes.description: Venezuelan Arepas (not to be confused with Colombian Arepas) are a tipical venezuelan dish. They can be filled with dozens of things, and each presentation has a particular name, but they’re still arepas.
instructions: Combine the water, the precooked corn flour, and a little bit of salt in a large mixing bowl.
Mix the ingredients by hand until no clumps remain in the resulting dough and it has a smooth but solid consistency.
Preheat a pan with oil over low heat.
Take a piece of dough and form a ball the size of the palm of your hand.
Carefully slap the ball side by side to make a disk neither too thick nor too thin.
Repeat the process with the remainder of the dough.
Put the arepas in the preheated pan and wait for it approximately 2 minutes and a half to flip it over.
When both sides are cooked, take them out of the pan.
Cut through the middle of the arepas with a butter knife, and brush them with butter.
Fill them with delicatessen to taste (ham, cheese, beans, mortadella, eggs, etc.)
recipes.name: Venezuelan Arepa

recipes.description: Valencian Baked Rice (Arroz al Horno) is a traditional dish from the Valencian Community, known for being cooked in a clay casserole and baked in the oven. This comforting and flavorful meal combines rice, meats, chickpeas, and vegetables.

ingredients.name: g of pork ribs
ingredients.raw: 500 g of pork ribs, cut into pieces

ingredients.name: g of pork belly
ingredients.raw: 200 g of pork belly, cut into pieces

ingredients.name: ml of extra virgin olive oil
ingredients.raw: 50 ml of extra virgin olive oil

ingredients.name: ml of hot broth (preferably from stew)
ingredients.raw: 800 ml of hot broth (preferably from stew)

instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C (428°F), using both upper and lower heat.
Peel the potato and cut it into 1 cm thick slices. Set aside.
In a clay casserole (oven-safe), heat the olive oil over medium-high heat. Brown the pork ribs and pork belly until golden and crispy. Remove and set aside.
In the same oil, lightly fry the potato slices until golden. Remove and set aside.
Sear the blood sausages for a few minutes, being careful not to break them. Remove and set aside.
Stir the sweet paprika into the remaining oil, mixing quickly to avoid burning. Add the crushed tomatoes and cook until the oil separates from the sauce.
Mix in the cooked chickpeas and rice, stirring for a couple of minutes so the rice absorbs the flavors.

Return the pork ribs, pork belly, and potato slices to the casserole, evenly distributing them over the rice. Place the whole garlic head in the center and arrange the blood sausages and tomato slices on top.
Pour the hot broth into the casserole, ensuring it covers all ingredients. Add the saffron threads and adjust the salt if needed.
Bake in the preheated oven for 20-25 minutes, or until the rice has absorbed all the broth and is tender.
Once done, remove from the oven and let the baked rice rest, covered with a clean cloth, for 5 minutes before serving.
recipes.name: Valencian Baked Rice (Arroz al Horno)

recipes.description: Valencian Paella is one of the most iconic dishes of Spanish cuisine, originating from the Valencia region. It is characterized by a combination of rice, meats, and vegetables, cooked in a paella pan over an open fire.

ingredients.name: g of rabbit
ingredients.raw: 500 g of rabbit, cut into pieces

ingredients.name: of extra virgin olive oil
ingredients.raw: 5 tablespoons of extra virgin olive oil

instructions: Heat the olive oil in a paella pan over medium-high heat. Add the chicken and rabbit pieces and fry them until golden brown on all sides.
Add the green beans and garrofó to the pan. Sauté the vegetables with the meats for a few minutes so they absorb the flavors.
Stir in the grated tomato and cook until it reduces and the oil separates, indicating it is ready.
Sprinkle the sweet paprika over the mixture and stir well, being careful not to burn it to avoid bitterness.
Pour the hot water into the pan and bring it to a boil. Cook over medium heat for about 20 minutes to let the flavors blend and create a rich broth.
Evenly distribute the rice across the paella pan. Add the saffron threads and adjust the salt if needed.

Cook over high heat for 10 minutes without stirring the rice. Then, lower to medium-low heat and continue cooking for another 8-10 minutes, until the rice absorbs all the broth and is perfectly cooked.
If desired, place a few sprigs of fresh rosemary on top of the rice during the last few minutes of cooking for extra aroma.
Once the rice is cooked, remove the pan from the heat and let the paella rest, covered with a clean cloth, for 5 minutes before serving.
recipes.name: Valencian Paella

ingredients.name: vinegar (rice one ideally. 1 teaspoon if high %)
ingredients.note: rice one ideally. 1 teaspoon if high %
ingredients.raw: 1 tbsp vinegar (rice one ideally. 1 teaspoon if high %)

instructions: Cut pork into thin slices about 2x2cm wide. They must be grabbable with chopsticks.
