Stir in carrot, bell pepper, onion, broccoli, soy sauce, black pepper, and garlic powder.
Cook until vegetables are tender.
Remove mixture from pan.
Pour eggs into pan and scramble.
Put vegetable mix and rice back in the pan and mix with scrambled eggs.
Add chicken and cook until hot.
Refrigerate leftovers.
recipes.name: Fried Rice with Chicken and Vegetables
recipes.recipe_by: Adapted from Fried Rice , Colorado State University and University of California at Davis. Eating Smart Being Active Recipes.

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Vanilla and orange peel are the secret to making this delicious cake with chocolate frosting. Serve at your next special occasion for a tasty treat.
instructions: Cake: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 325 °F.
Grease with small amount of cooking oil or use non-stick cooking oil spray on a 10-inch round pan (at least 2 1/2 inches high).
Powder pan with flour.
Tap out excess flour.
Sift together flour and baking powder.
In a separate bowl, beat together margarine and sugar until soft and creamy.
Beat in eggs, vanilla, and orange peel.
Gradually add the flour mixture alternating with milk, beginning and ending with flour.
Pour the mixture into the pan.
Bake for 40-45 minutes or until done.
Let cake cool for 5-10 minutes before removing from the pan.
Let cool completely before icing.
Icing: Cream together cream cheese and milk until smooth.
Add cocoa.
Blend well.
Slowly add sugar until icing is smooth.
Mix in vanilla.
Smooth icing over top and sides of cooled cake.
recipes.name: Frosted Cake
recipes.recipe_by: A Healthier You: Based on the Dietary Guidelines for Americans — US Department of Health and Human Services — Office of Disease Prevention and Health Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Engage your kids in a fun activity by having them slice and dip ripe bananas in orange or lemon juice and place the bananas in the freezer for several hours to create this tasty snack or dessert.

ingredients.name: orange juice or lemon juice
ingredients.raw: 1/8 cup orange juice or lemon juice

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Peel each banana and cut in half (width-wise).
Insert craft stick into bottom of each banana half.
Dip each banana half into juice.
Wrap in foil and freeze for two or more hours.
recipes.name: Frozen Banana Pops
recipes.notes: Optional Toppings: Dip in chocolate, then roll in chopped nuts, crushed cereal, shredded coconut, or sprinkles.
recipes.recipe_by: Simple Healthy Recipes — Oklahoma Nutrition Information and Education — ONIE Project

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Use your own combination of fresh, frozen or canned fruits to create this yummy dessert or snack. It's perfect for a summer day.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Line 18 muffin-tin cups with paper baking cups.
Dice or mash bananas and place in a large mixing bowl.
Stir in remaining ingredients.
Spoon into muffin-tin cups and freeze at least 3 hours or until firm.
Remove frozen cups and store in a plastic bag in freezer.
Before serving, remove paper cups and let stand 10 minutes.
recipes.name: Frozen Fruit Cups
recipes.notes: Watch how to make this kid-friendly recipe on YouTube .
recipes.recipe_by: Kids a Cookin’ — Kansas Family Nutrition Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: These frozen fruit pops contain fruit, juice, and low-fat yogurt to create a refreshing treat on a summer day.

ingredients.name: crushed pineapple
ingredients.raw: 1 cup crushed pineapple, canned, juiced packed

ingredients.name: us fluid ounces orange juice
ingredients.raw: 6 us fluid ounces orange juice, frozen concentrate

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix the ingredients in a medium-size bowl.
Divide into 4 paper cups.
Freeze until slushy - about 60 minutes.
Insert a wooden stick half way through the center of each fruit pop.
Freeze until hard or at least 4 hours.
Peel away the paper cup before you eat the fruit pop.
recipes.name: Frozen Fruit Pops
recipes.notes: You can mix ingredients and freeze in ice cube tray instead of cups, making great "ice cubes" in fruit juice. Try other fruits or juice concentrates for variety.
recipes.recipe_by: The Power of Choice — USDA Food and Nutrition Service and US Department of Health and Human Services Food and Drug Administration (FDA)

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: These frozen pear pops are a refreshing treat! Sweet pears mixed with orange juice and yogurt is a snack that is sure to please.

ingredients.name: frozen orange juice concentrate
ingredients.raw: 6 ounces frozen orange juice concentrate, thawed

ingredients.name: ice cube tray or small paper cups
ingredients.raw: ice cube tray or small paper cups

instructions: Cut canned pears into small pieces.
Add yogurt and orange juice to cut pears and mix well to combine.
Divide into 8 ice cubes squares (or 4 small paper cups).
Place in cut straws or popsicle sticks.
Freeze and enjoy!
recipes.name: Frozen Pear Pops
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Enjoy this super-quick and refreshing salad featuring melon and feta cheese. You can substitute any of your favorite fresh-cut fruit items, such as grapes, mangoes, etc.

ingredients.name: medium red onion
ingredients.raw: 1/4 cup medium red onion, thinly sliced

instructions: Whisk together vinaigrette ingredients.
Toss with remaining ingredients and serve.
recipes.name: Fruit & Feta Salad
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health Foundation

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Use yogurt, peanut butter, and vanilla to create a dip for your favorite fruits.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Prepare fruit by washing and slicing if necessary.
Arrange fruit on a plate around a small bowl.
To make dip, combine yogurt, vanilla, and peanut butter in a small bowl.
Mix well.
Chill dip in refrigerator until ready to serve.
recipes.name: Fruit and Peanut Butter Dip
recipes.notes: Can use six cups of any washed fruit. Be creative! Spread dip on a tortilla, add banana, and roll up.
recipes.recipe_by: Eating Smart, Being Active — Colorado State University and University of California at Davis

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Shake up your day with this quick and easy breakfast. Make this recipe with any of your favorite fruits, especially when they are in season!
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Blend banana with pineapple juice, yogurt, and strawberries in a blender.
Blend until smooth.
Divide shake between 2 glasses and serve immediately.
recipes.name: Fruit and Yogurt Breakfast Shake
recipes.recipe_by: Recipes to Grow On — University of Illinois Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Honey and vinegar give a sweet and sour twist to this fruit and cabbage cole slaw.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Shred cabbage.
Combine all ingredients in a large bowl.
recipes.name: Fruit Cole Slaw
recipes.notes: * Children under the age of one should not consume honey.
recipes.recipe_by: Making It Fit: Piecing Together Your Food Needs — University of Vermont Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This compote has a thick and sweet sauce that is mixed with fruit for a delicious dessert.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Drain the juice from the canned pineapple into a small saucepan.
Stir in orange juice and cornstarch.
Blend until smooth.
Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring constantly.
Let the juice mix cool to room temperature.
While the juice mix is cooling, peel and slice the banana.
Wash the pear and peaches and cut them into cubes.
Pour the cooled juice mix into a large bowl.
Add the pieces of pineapple, banana, pear, and peaches.
Stir together.
recipes.name: Fruit Compote
recipes.notes: You can serve this compote in serving dishes, or over frozen yogurt or waffles.
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Slightly sweetened apples topped with a mixture of flour, oats and brown sugar crumble baked until tender and golden brown. Substitute berries, peaches, or a mix of favorites.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350 °F.
Lightly grease a baking dish with butter or oil.
Combine the apples, flour, and white sugar to make the filling.
To prepare the topping, mix the oats, whole wheat flour, white sugar, brown sugar, and salt.
Add the oil (or butter) and stir into the dry ingredients.
Fill the baking pan with the fruit mixture and then cover with the crumble topping.
Transfer to the oven and bake until the fruit is tender and the topping is golden, about 45 minutes.
Serve right away or cover and refrigerate up to 2 days.
recipes.name: Fruit Crisp
recipes.notes: Frozen unsweetened berries, like blueberries, can be used instead of apples.
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Lime juice and orange concentrate gives this yogurt dip a tangy and sweet flavor. Serve it with your favorite fruits.

ingredients.name: us fluid ounce orange juice
ingredients.raw: 1 us fluid ounce orange juice, 100% juice, frozen concentrate

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a small bowl, combine yogurt, orange juice concentrate, lime juice, and brown sugar.
Mix well.
Place bowl containing dip on a large plate and surround with fruit.
recipes.name: Fruit Dip
recipes.recipe_by: Discover the Secret to Healthy Living — California Department of Health Services — California Children’s 5-A-Day Power Play Campaign

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: With just three ingredients and three steps, this snack recipe is perfect for kids or beginner cooks of all ages.

ingredients.name: fruit (grapes
ingredients.note: grapes, banana slices, apple wedges, strawberries
ingredients.raw: 2 cups fruit (grapes, banana slices, apple wedges, strawberries)

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine yogurt and peanuts.
Mix with a spoon.
Place a toothpick in the center of each fruit.
Dip fruit into the yogurt peanut mixture.
recipes.name: Fruit Dippers
recipes.recipe_by: The Power of Choice — USDA Food and Nutrition Service and US Department of Health and Human Services Food and Drug Administration (FDA)

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Blending your favorite fruit juice concentrate with ice and water will give you a quick and refreshing drink on a warm day.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a blender, place juice concentrate, water, and half of ice.
To prevent spillage, do not pass the top line of the blender.
Blend while gradually adding remaining ice.
Serve.
recipes.name: Fruit Juice Slush
recipes.notes: Use any flavor of juice concentrate. If slush is too thick, add more water.
recipes.recipe_by: Lifeskills in Food Education, Food Skills Cookbook — University of Hawaii at Manoa Cooperative Extension — Food Stamps Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Try this creative and easy way to enjoy your favorite fruit. Make and serve these fun fruit skewers as a dessert or snack.
instructions: Thread the fruit onto the skewers, alternating and arranging the pieces however you like.
Serve right away.
recipes.name: Fruit Kabob
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Fruit kabobs make a colorful and fun snack that kids can help prepare.

ingredients.name: kiwifruits
ingredients.raw: 2 kiwifruits, peeled and cut into quarters

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place fruit chunks on bamboo skewers.
Place fruit kabobs on platter.
Place light strawberry yogurt in bowl.
Serve kabobs with yogurt on the side.
recipes.name: Fruit Kabobs with Yogurt Dip
recipes.recipe_by: Food and Health Communications, Inc.

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This fruit shake is a great way to kick off your day. One minute in the blender and you'll be on your way.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place everything together into a blender.
Blend for 30 seconds to 1 minute.
recipes.name: Fruit Milk Shakes
recipes.recipe_by: Cooking with What You Have — Cornell Cooperative Extension of Onondaga County

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: The crust for this dessert cooks in the oven and is covered with a cream cheese mix and topped with strawberries. For variety, try using any combination of colorful fruits.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 375 °F.
For crust, cream margarine, sugar, vanilla, and egg until light and fluffy.
Add flour and baking powder, mixing well.
Spread mixture about 1/8 inch thick on a pizza pan, baking sheet, or 9x13 inch pan.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes or until lightly browned.
Cool.
For spread, mix together cream cheese, sugar, and vanilla.
Spread on cooled cookie crust.
Arrange fruit on top of pizza.
Refrigerate until serving time.
recipes.name: Fruit Pizza
recipes.notes: Fruit Topping Ideas: Sliced Strawberries, kiwi, bananas, pineapple, mandarin oranges, pears, peaches, blueberries, or grapes.
recipes.recipe_by: Kansas Family Nutrition Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Toasted whole wheat English muffins topped with fat-free cream cheese and fruit make this a quick and easy breakfast or snack.

ingredients.name: whipped fat-free strawberry cream cheese
ingredients.raw: 2 tablespoons whipped fat-free strawberry cream cheese

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Toast the English muffin until golden brown.
Spread cream cheese on toasted muffin.
Arrange sliced strawberries, grapes, and orange slices on top of the cream cheese.
recipes.name: Fruit Pizza To Go
recipes.notes: This recipe can be made with any flavor of cream cheese and any fruit you like.
recipes.recipe_by: University of Maryland Extension — Food Supplement Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This semi-homemade recipe mixes canned fruit cocktail with fresh fruit and yogurt for a quick and tasty fruit salad.

ingredients.name: (8 ounce) container of yogurt
ingredients.raw: 1 (8 ounce) container of yogurt, low-fat piña colada

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix fruit in a large bowl.
Add yogurt and mix well.
Chill in refrigerator before serving.
recipes.name: Fruit Salad
recipes.recipe_by: Easy and Nutritious Family Recipes, Adapted from Easy Fruit Salad — University of California Cooperative Extension — Fresno County
recipes.serving_size: 1/2 cup prepared fruit salad, 1/14 of recipe (109g)

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Mango and papaya add a tropical flavor to this fruit salad while chili powder gives it a kick. The jicama provides a refreshing crunch and the result is a fruit salad that's sure to please.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash, peel, and cut the jicama into thin slices.
Wash, peel, and cut the rest of the fruit (including the lime) into slices or small pieces.
On a large plate, arrange the fruit.
Sprinkle the lime or orange juice over the fruit.
In a small bowl, mix the salt and chili powder.
Sprinkle over the fruit and serve.
Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
recipes.name: Fruit Salad with Jicama
recipes.recipe_by: Pictorial Recipes — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service — Oregon Family Nutrition Program — Recipe submitted by Lynn Myers Steele, 2000

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This colorful salad combines sliced strawberries, pineapple chunks, and blueberries coated in pineapple juice. Serve topped with low-fat yogurt and slivered almonds for a treat that looks as good as it tastes.
instructions: Place fruit in a large bowl and mix with pineapple juice.
Let stand for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Place 1 cup of fruit salad in a small bowl and top with 1/2 cup of yogurt.
Sprinkle almonds on top of each fruit salad.
Serve immediately.
recipes.name: Fruit Salad with Yogurt
recipes.notes: Any 100% fruit juice can be used instead of pineapple juice.
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A salsa that is different from what you may usually have, this fruit recipe can be a great way to help older kids and teens learn safe knife skills in the kitchen.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine fruits in a medium mixing bowl and add lemon juice.
Stir in sugar, nutmeg, and cinnamon.
Mix well.
Refrigerate until serving time.
recipes.name: Fruit Salsa
recipes.recipe_by: Kids a Cookin’ — Kansas Family Nutrition Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Serve this fruit slush as a drink or a dessert, and keep leftovers in the fridge for later. Pour it over fresh ice when you are ready to eat.

ingredients.name: cantaloupe or watermelon
ingredients.raw: 3 cups cantaloupe or watermelon, coarsely chopped, seeded, peeled

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a blender, puree fruit and lime juice until smooth.
Add sugar if desired.
Combine fruit mixture and water in a large pitcher.
To eliminate the pulp pour through a strainer (optional).
Cover and refrigerate for up to a week.
To serve, stir well and pour into tall glasses over ice.
recipes.name: Fruit Slush
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Have fun experimenting with different fruit and juices in this scrumptious smoothie.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Put all ingredients in a blender.
Blend on high until smooth.
Pour into 2 glasses.
Serve right away.
recipes.name: Fruit Smoothie
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Make the youngest members of your family happy with this adorable snack. It's perfect for a mid-morning or afterschool snack.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Peel banana and use butter knife to cut banana in half lengthwise.
Place 2 banana halves on small plate end to end, in an "s" shape.
Add raisins to the top of banana as eyes.
Enjoy your Fruit Snake.
recipes.name: Fruit Snake
recipes.recipe_by: Chickasaw Nation Get Fresh! Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Layer grapes, yogurt, bananas, and cereal for a sweet and crunchy snack.

ingredients.name: dry crunchy cereal
ingredients.note: Grape Nuts or granola cereals are good

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Peel and slice the banana.
Spoon the grapes into a tall plastic cup.
Put 3 spoonsful of yogurt on top of the grapes.
Spoon sliced bananas on top of the yogurt.
Add the rest of the yogurt.
Sprinkle the cereal on top.
recipes.name: Fruit Yogurt Parfait
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: These pops are a fun warm-weather treat that needs only two ingredients. With no cooking, cutting, or special equipment required, kids can learn to make these by themselves.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine ingredients.
Pour into 3 ounce paper cups.
Freeze about 30 minutes; then stick a wooden popsicle/ craft stick in the center of each cup.
Freeze overnight until firm.
To eat pops, peel off paper cups.
For variety, try other fruit flavored yogurts and frozen fruit or fruit juice concentrates.
recipes.name: Fruit Yogurt Pops
recipes.recipe_by: Easy and Nutritious Family Recipes — University of California Cooperative Extension — Fresno County

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Start your day off right with a warm bowl of apple cinnamon oatmeal, a dish that is perfect for a chilly morning at home.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Use a vegetable peeler to remove the skin from the apple.
Cut the core out of the apple.
Chop the apple into small pieces.
Put the water in the saucepan.
Bring the water to a boil on medium heat.
Stir in oatmeal, raisins, chopped apple, and cinnamon.
Turn heat to low.
Cook 5 minutes, stirring often.
recipes.name: Fruity Homemade Oatmeal
recipes.notes: To get more fiber, leave the skin on the apple.
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Bored with the same old sandwich at lunch? Liven up packed lunches with this Thai-influenced pita pocket: a surprising blend of fruits, spinach, and peanut sauce tucked in a very portable pita pocket.

ingredients.name: tropical fruit salad in 100% juice
ingredients.raw: 1 can tropical fruit salad in 100% juice

ingredients.name: reserved juice from tropical fruit salad
ingredients.raw: 3 tablespoons reserved juice from tropical fruit salad

ingredients.name: natural peanut butter
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup natural peanut butter, crunchy or chunky

instructions: In a colander over a bowl, drain fruit salad well; reserve 3 tablespoons juice.
In a small bowl, whisk together reserved juice, peanut butter, cream cheese, and soy sauce.
Place drained fruit, spinach, and cilantro (if desired) in a bowl; mix gently.
Add sauce and toss.
Slice a small portion off each pita.
Tuck the slice inside the bottom of the pita.
Fill each pita pocket with the fruit-spinach mixture.
Wrap individually in plastic wrap and refrigerate.
Will keep well overnight.
recipes.name: Fruity Thai Pita Pockets
recipes.notes: Time-saving idea: Purchase pre-opened pita pockets
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health Foundation

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Fruit, nuts, and chocolate. Do we need to say more?
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place chocolate chips in a small microwave safe bowl.
Heat on high for 10 seconds and stir.
Repeat until chocolate is melted, about 30 seconds.
Place fruit on a small tray covered with a piece of waxed paper.
Use a spoon to drizzle the melted chocolate on top of the fruit.
Sprinkle the fruit with chopped nuts.
Cover the fruit and place in the refrigerator for 10 minutes or until the chocolate hardens.
Serve chilled.
recipes.name: Fudgy Fruit
recipes.recipe_by: Healthy Recipes — CalFresh Healthy Living

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Beans are unique foods that can be counted as either a vegetable or protein. This dish comes together quickly with canned beans but can also be made with dried beans.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat over to 350 °F.
Cook ground beef and onions.
Drain fat.
Add remaining ingredients and mix.
Place in casserole dish.
Bake in the oven at 350 °F for 30 minutes.
recipes.name: Full of Beans Hot Dish
recipes.notes: For convenience this recipe includes canned beans. To lower the sodium, feel free to use dried beans that have been prepared according to the package directions.
recipes.recipe_by: University of Wisconsin Cooperative Extension Service — Family Living Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Break out the barley to make a comforting vegetable soup on a cold or rainy day.

ingredients.name: us fluid ounces tomato juice
ingredients.raw: 46 us fluid ounces tomato juice, low-sodium

ingredients.name: thyme leaves
ingredients.raw: 1/2 teaspoon thyme leaves, fresh or dried

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a Dutch oven or stock pot, combine tomato juice, beef broth, barley, sugar, Worcestershire sauce, bay leaf, thyme and salt (if using).
Bring to boil; reduce heat.
Cover; simmer 1 hour.
Add zucchini, tomato, and green pepper.
Return to boil; reduce heat.
Cover; simmer 15 to 20 minutes or until vegetables and barley are tender.
recipes.name: Garden Barley Soup
recipes.recipe_by: Wellness Ways Resource Book — University of Illinois Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Chopped tomatoes, bell peppers, and cucumbers combine with cannellini (white) beans, almonds, and a simple vinaigrette for a delicious and satisfying salad.

ingredients.name: tomato basil garlic seasoning blend
ingredients.raw: 1 tablespoon tomato basil garlic seasoning blend, no-salt

ingredients.name: 15.5 oz cans cannellini (white) beans
ingredients.raw: 2 15.5 oz cans cannellini (white) beans, low-sodium, drained, and rinsed

ingredients.name: Large lettuce leaves (Boston
ingredients.raw: Large lettuce leaves (Boston, Bibb, or romaine)

instructions: Whisk together dressing ingredients in a small bowl.
In a small sauté pan, toast almond slivers until golden.
Remove from pan and let cool.
In a medium bowl, toss dressing with all ingredients except lettuce.
Refrigerate until ready to serve.
To serve, place lettuce leaves on individual plates; top with salad.
recipes.name: Garden Cannellini Bean Salad
recipes.notes: Serving Suggestion : Serve with a glass of non-fat milk, 1 slice of whole-grain bread, and pear slices.
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health Foundation

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This quick and easy one pan dish is full of veggies, spices, and flavor. Get your kids involved by letting them wash the vegetables.
instructions: Wash your hands with soap and water.
Place ground beef in a skillet sprayed with non-stick cooking spray.
Brown meat over medium-high heat, stirring occasionally to break it into pieces.
Drain fat and blot meat with paper towels.
Transfer beef into a colander and rinse with very hot water to further remove fat.
Add green pepper, onion, and celery.
Cook until softened.
Add beans, corn, tomato sauce, chopped tomatoes, pepper, garlic powder and chili powder.
Cook mixture over low heat for 20 minutes.
Serve hot in bowls.
Or serve as a dip with baked tortilla chips or on a bun.
Cover and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
recipes.name: Garden Chili
recipes.recipe_by: Fix it Fresh! Recipe Series — Kansas State University Research and Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This frittata with its blend of colorful vegetables and fresh eggs makes a deliciously nutritious single-dish meal for breakfast, brunch, or supper.

ingredients.name: Italian kale
ingredients.raw: 4 cups Italian kale, or other kale variety

instructions: Beat eggs, pepper, and salt in large bowl; set aside.

Microwave potatoes until slightly soft, but not completely cooked; then cube. (Alternate method without microwave: Cube potatoes and boil 5 minutes until slightly soft; then drain.) Chop remaining vegetables while potatoes cool.
Mix vegetables together.
Heat oil in a 10-inch non-stick skillet.
Sauté vegetables for 5 to 8 minutes; add to eggs and mix well.
Pour egg-vegetable mixture into the same skillet.
Cook over low to medium heat until eggs are almost set, about 8 to 10 minutes.
Cover and let sit until eggs are completely set, about 5 minutes.
Egg dishes should be cooked to 160 ºF.
recipes.name: Garden Frittata
recipes.notes: Serving Suggestions: Serve with 8-oz glass of fat-free (skim) milk and 1/2 sliced orange.
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health Foundation

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Fresh veggies, peanuts, and apples give this crunchy salad a refreshing flavor, and it is coated with non-fat vanilla yogurt for creaminess.

ingredients.name: apple
ingredients.note: chopped, cored and diced, not peeled

instructions: Wash your hands with soap and water.
Mix all ingredients together in a serving bowl.
Cover and refrigerate for 2 hours or longer to allow flavors to blend.
Serve cold.
Cover and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
recipes.name: Garden Orchard Salad
recipes.recipe_by: Fix it Fresh! Recipe Series — Kansas State University Research and Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: The bananas make this bread moist and add extra flavor. Serve with a salad or main dish, or eat anytime.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350 °F.
In a medium-sized bowl, combine cornmeal, flour, baking powder, and salt.
Set aside.
In a small bowl, combine bananas, water, and egg mix.
Stir until mixed well.
Stir banana mixture into cornmeal mixture.
Mix until dry ingredients are moistened.
Gently stir in raisins and walnuts.
Lightly spray medium-sized skillet or baking pan with nonstick cooking spray.
Spoon batter into skillet or baking pan.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes or until bread is golden brown and pulls away from the edges.
A wooden toothpick or clean fork inserted into the center of the bread should come out clean.
Cut into four equal slices and serve hot or cold.
recipes.name: Garden Pan Bread
recipes.recipe_by: A Harvest of Recipes with USDA Foods — USDA Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations — Adapted from a recipe submitted by Alicson Scott, Chickasaw Nation, Get Fresh! Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Pasta salad is a cool and delightful addition to lunch or dinner. It goes with soup or a sandwich.
instructions: In a medium-sized bowl, combine macaroni, onions, cucumbers, and green peppers.
Mix well.
In a separate bowl, mix vinegar, vegetable oil, salt, and pepper.
If using parsley, add that too.
Pour the prepared dressing over the pasta.
Mix well.
Cover bowl and refrigerate for 30 to 45 minutes.
Serve cold.
recipes.name: Garden Pasta Salad
recipes.recipe_by: A Harvest of Recipes with USDA Foods — USDA Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Italian seasoning and garlic powder bring a punch of flavor to this delicious and easy vegetable soup. Serve it with a whole wheat roll for a satisfying lunch or quick dinner.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large saucepan sprayed with non-stick cooking spray, sauté the carrots, onion, and garlic over low heat about 5 minutes.
Add broth, cabbage, green beans, tomatoes, and Italian seasoning; bring to a boil.
Cover, lower heat.
Simmer about 15 minutes or until carrots are tender.
Stir in zucchini and heat for 3 to 4 minutes.
Serve hot.
Refrigerate leftovers.
recipes.name: Garden Vegetable Soup
recipes.recipe_by: Eating Smart, Being Active — Colorado State University and University of California at Davis

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This quick and simple bok choy recipe uses just garlic, salt, and vegetable oil to give bok choy a delicious flavor.

ingredients.name: garlic
ingredients.note: use 4-6 cloves, minced or 1 to 1 1/2 teaspoons of garlic powder

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cut bok choy crosswise into easy-to-eat pieces.
In a medium skillet over medium-high heat, sauté garlic in oil until fragrant.
If using garlic powder, add with salt in the next step.
Add bok choy and stir quickly.
Add salt.
Stir until greens are wilted and stem pieces are tender-crisp.
Serve hot.
recipes.name: Garlic Bok Choy
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Adding garlic and ginger to ramen is a game changer! This recipe has vegetables, lean protein, and lots of flavor!

ingredients.name: lean ground beef (15% fat or less)
ingredients.raw: 1/2 pound lean ground beef (15% fat or less)

ingredients.name: instant ramen-style noodles
ingredients.note: 3 ounces each, broken into small pieces

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large skillet over medium-high heat (350 °F in an electric skillet), brown the ground beef.
Drain fat from the skillet.
Drain fat from the skillet. (See Notes.) Add water and ONE seasoning packet to cooked beef and mix well.
Add vegetables, green onion, ginger, and garlic.
Bring to a boil over high heat.
Add ramen noodles, reduce heat to low, and simmer 3 to 5 minutes until vegetables are tender, stirring occasionally.
recipes.name: Garlic Ginger Ramen with Beef
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Jazz up your chicken dinner with garlic, lemon zest, and fresh parsley. Serve this dish with brown rice and a side salad for a complete meal.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a small saucepan, bring water to a boil.
Add garlic; cook for 10 minutes.
Drain garlic, peel and cut into thin slices.
In a small bowl, combine garlic, 1/2 cup of chopped parsley, lemon zest, and seasoning.
Mix well.
Loosen skin from each chicken breast to form a pocket.
Place about 1 teaspoon of garlic mixture under skin of each breast.
Heat a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken skin-side down; cook until golden, about 4 minutes.
Turn chicken; reduce heat to medium.
Cover and cook until no longer pink in center, about 10 to 12 minutes.
Transfer chicken to a plate.
Wipe any fat away from the skillet.
Add remaining chopped parsley, broth, and lemon juice to pan.
Bring to a boil; cook for 1 minute.
Spoon mixture over chicken.
recipes.name: Garlic Stuffed Chicken
recipes.recipe_by: Seat Pleasant/ University of Maryland Health Partnership

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Take a trip to Spain in your very own kitchen! Gazpacho, a Spanish favorite, is a cooling puréed vegetable soup topped with extra virgin olive oil for a smooth finish.

ingredients.name: medium tomatoes
ingredients.note: ripe, skinned, seeded, and roughly chopped, about 3 3/4 cup or 2 pounds

ingredients.name: small cucumber
ingredients.note: peeled, seeded, and roughly chopped, about 1 1/2 cup

ingredients.name: green pepper
ingredients.note: seeded and roughly chopped, about 1 cup

ingredients.name: minced garlic
ingredients.note: or 4 cloves fresh garlic, finely chopped

ingredients.name: small tomato
ingredients.note: seeded and finely chopped, about 1 cup

ingredients.name: green bell pepper
ingredients.note: seeded and finely chopped, about 1/2 cup

instructions: Tear bread into small pieces; transfer to medium bowl and cover with 1 cup water.
Soak until bread is saturated, about 15 minutes.
Squeeze water from bread, discarding soaking water.
In bowl of blender or food processor, add bread, tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, garlic, and 1/4 cup of water.
Blend until well combined, about 1 minute.
With motor running, add oil in steady stream until well blended.
Stir in vinegar, season with low-sodium adobo.
Strain puréed soup through small-hole strainer, into soup terrine, pressing firmly to pass all liquid through strainer, discard any solids.
Cover terrine; transfer to refrigerator.
Chill at least 1 hour, or up to 48 hours.
To serve, divide soup evenly among serving bowls.
Garnish with tomatoes, onions, peppers, and eggs.
recipes.name: Gazpacho
recipes.notes: Serving Suggestions: Serve with Spanish Garlic Shrimp, Garlic and Spanish Rice, and a glass of non-fat milk to make the meal complete.
recipes.recipe_by: The Best of La Cocina GOYA: Healthy, Tasty, Affordable Latin Cooking/ Lo Mejor de la Cocina GOYA: Cocina Latina Saludable, Rica y Económica — GOYA Foods

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This yummy chilled tomato soup makes a great addition to lunch or dinner.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Chop the tomato, cucumber, and peppers into very small pieces.
Put all the ingredients in a large glass or plastic bowl.
Stir well with a wooden or plastic spoon.
Chill in the fridge for 1 to 2 hours before serving.
recipes.name: Gazpacho Soup
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Make this mix ahead of time and use it as a base for the Ginger Orange Muffins recipe.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine all ingredients in a large bowl.
Mix well.
Store mix in a covered jar until ready to use.
recipes.name: Ginger Bread Mix
recipes.notes: Use this mix to make Ginger Orange Muffins .
recipes.recipe_by: Pictorial Recipes — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service — Oregon Family Nutrition Program — Recipe submitted by Lynn Myers Steele, 2000

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Use our Ginger Bread Mix and make these muffins ahead of time for a quick and healthy breakfast on the go.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Combine the Ginger Bread Mix and bran cereal in a bowl.
Beat the egg slightly in another bowl.
Add the egg and other ingredients to the gingerbread and cereal mixture.
Stir only until combined.
Let stand for 15 minutes.
Fill 12 muffin cups (well-greased pans or paper liners) 2/3 full.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes or until done in the center.
recipes.name: Ginger Orange Muffins
recipes.notes: 2 servings of Ginger Bread Mix = 2 cups
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Fresh green beans work well when they’re in season. If they’re not, try frozen in this recipe that combines a whole grains and veggies into one satisfying and eye-catching dish.

ingredients.name: olive oil or cooking oil
ingredients.raw: 1 tablespoon olive oil or cooking oil

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Toast quinoa in a dry skillet over medium heat, stirring constantly for about 3 minutes.
Transfer toasted quinoa to a medium pot and add water or broth.
Bring to a boil, then let simmer until all of the water is absorbed and quinoa is tender (10 to 15 minutes).
Set aside and leave uncovered to cool.
While quinoa is cooling, place green beans in a microwave-safe dish.
Add a small amount of water, cover, and microwave for 4-6 minutes or until just tender.
Rinse green beans in cold water to stop the cooking process.
In a large bowl, combine the quinoa, green beans, olive oil or cooking oil, sesame oil, soy sauce, lemon juice, and ground ginger.
Stir well.
Season with salt and pepper, as needed.
Serve warm or at room temperature.
recipes.name: Gingery Quinoa with Green Beans
recipes.recipe_by: Bronson Wellness Center — Bronson Healthcare - Michigan

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Take care not to burn the carrots at the end of this recipe. They should be browned (but not blackened) for a tasty side dish.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Peel the carrots.
Cut in half lengthwise, then cut into 1 inch pieces.
Melt the margarine in a heavy saucepan on low heat.
Add the carrots.
Stir to coat them with the margarine.
Add the water, salt, and pepper.
Cover and simmer for about 15 minutes until tender.
Drain the water.
Add the sugar.
Cover the pan.
Shake the pan back and forth on the burner for 1 minute.
Cook for 1 more minute, until the carrots are glazed but not brown.
recipes.name: Glazed Carrots
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This family favorite is flavored with garlic, thyme, tomato paste, and mustard then coated with a tangy glaze and a sprinkle of oats.

ingredients.name: green bell pepper
ingredients.raw: 1/2 green bell pepper, cored and diced

instructions: Preheat the oven to 325 °F.
Lightly grease a baking sheet.
Put a skillet over medium heat and when it is hot, add the oil.
Add the onion, bell pepper, garlic, and thyme and cook about 10 minutes until golden.
Lower the heat and add the water and tomato paste.
Cook about 10 minutes until the onion is soft and most of the liquid has been absorbed.
Set aside to cool.
Add the mustard, salt and pepper.
While the onion mixture is cool, put the ground beef, 4 tablespoons rolled oats and the egg in the bowl and gently mix, by hand.
Add the cooled onion mixture and gently mix again until everything is thoroughly incorporated.
Do not over mix.
Form the mixture into a loaf about 8x4 inches and put on the prepared baking sheet.
To make the glaze: Put the tomato paste and mustard in a small bowl and mix well.
Rub on top of the meatloaf and sprinkle with the remaining 2 tablespoons rolled oats.
Put in the oven to cook about 1 hour until deep brown and cooked throughout.
Serve right away or cover and refrigerate up to 2 days.
recipes.name: Glazed Meatloaf
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This soup is great for lunch or dinner. Serve it with a salad and a whole wheat roll for a delicious meal.

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.note: or cooking oil of your choice

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place the oil in a large pot or Dutch-oven style pan.
Heat over medium-high.
Add the onion and sauté until golden, about 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the rest of the ingredients and mix well.
Bring to a boil and then lower the heat to a simmer.
Cook uncovered until the peas are tender, about 45 minutes.
Serve hot.
recipes.name: Golden Split Pea Soup
recipes.recipe_by: Food and Health Communications, Inc.

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This stuffing has lots of crunch and flavor from the apples, celery, and onions. Whole wheat bread gives this recipe a boost of whole grains.

ingredients.name: whole wheat bread
ingredients.note: or white bread or buns, dry

ingredients.name: apples
ingredients.note: optional - medium, pared, cored and chopped, or 1/4 cup raisins

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Put cubes in a large bowl.
Set aside.
Put water in medium saucepan.
Add onion, celery, parsley, salt, and pepper.
Cook for 5 minutes.
Do not drain.
Pour over bread cubes.
Stir in milk and egg.
Gently stir in apples, and raisins, if desired.
Spoon into a greased 2-quart baking dish.
Bake at 350 °F for 1 hour.
recipes.name: Grandma's Stuffing
recipes.recipe_by: University of Wisconsin Cooperative Extension Service — Family Living Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Make your own granola bars at home. This recipe combines raisins, carrots, oats, and honey for a healthy snack or breakfast on-the-go.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Peel and grate the carrots.
Put the honey and peanut butter in a large saucepan.
Cook on low heat until they melt.
Remove the pan from the heat.
Turn off the burner.
Add oatmeal, raisins, carrots, and coconut to the saucepan.
Stir well, and let it cool until you can safely touch it with your hands.
Put the mix into a 9x13 inch baking pan.
Press the mix firmly into the bottom of the pan.
Bake for 25 minutes.
Cut into 24 bars.
recipes.name: Granola Bars
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Learn to make your own granola in an oven, skillet, or even the microwave. It's easy and you can be creative with what you put in it.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Conventional Oven: Heat oven to 350 ºF.
Combine all ingredients in a large bowl, except raisins, mix well.
Bake in 13x9 inch baking pan at 350 ºF for 25 to 30 minutes or until golden brown.
Stir every 5 minutes.
Stir in raisins.
Cool thoroughly.
Store in tightly covered container.
Electric Skillet: Combine all ingredients except raisins in a large microwave safe bowl; mix well.
Set electric skillet at 300 ºF and stir mixture constantly until lightly browned.
Place in a bowl and stir in raisins.
Cool thoroughly.
Store in tightly covered container.
Microwave: Combine all ingredients, except raisins in a large microwave safe bowl; mix well.
Place in 11x7 glass baking dish.
Cook at HIGH about 8 minutes or until golden brown, stirring after every 2 minutes of cooking; stir in raisins.
Place onto un-greased cookie sheet or aluminum foil to cool.
Cool thoroughly.
Store in a tightly covered container.
recipes.name: Granola with Oatmeal, Coconut, and Pecans
recipes.notes: Honey should not be fed to children under 1 year of age.
recipes.recipe_by: Adapted from: Awesome Granola — Texas A&M Agrilife Extension Service — Expanded Nutrition Program - Hidalgo County

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: The creamy and tangy goodness of low-fat cottage cheese is the perfect balance to sweet grapes and cashews. Enjoy this salad as a sandwich filling or on a bed of lettuce.

ingredients.name: dry roasted unsalted cashews
ingredients.raw: 3/4 cup dry roasted unsalted cashews, coarsely chopped

instructions: In a medium bowl, mix cottage cheese, grapes, celery, cashews, parsley, and ground black pepper.
Toast bread and build sandwiches following steps 3 and 4.
Spread 1/4 salad mix on 4 of the bread slices.
Add two lettuce leaves to each sandwich; top with 2nd bread slice.
recipes.name: Grape and Cashew Salad Sandwich
recipes.notes: Serving Suggestions: Serve with a side of raw baby carrots and 1 cup of sparkling water with a lemon wedge.
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health Foundation

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A fruit-packed, refreshing twist on salsa. Perfect for topping tacos or scooping up with tortilla chips.

ingredients.name: Anaheim chili
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup Anaheim chili, fresh or canned

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine all ingredients in a medium bowl and mix well.
Let stand at least 1 hour.
Drain off excess liquid before serving.
recipes.name: Grape Salsa
recipes.notes: Try adding chopped cucumber for more crunch.
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Water chestnuts give this spinach salad a delightful crunch when served with the spicy and tangy dressing.

ingredients.name: fresh spinach
ingredients.raw: 4 1/2 cups fresh spinach, washed and drained

ingredients.name: sliced mushrooms
ingredients.raw: 1 can sliced mushrooms, drained (2 ounce cans)

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Tear spinach coarsely and place in large salad bowl.
Add mushrooms, water chestnuts, and grapefruit.
Mix together oil, vinegar, grapefruit juice, soy sauce, hot pepper sauce, salt, and dry mustard.
Toss dressing with spinach mixture and serve.
recipes.name: Grapefruit Spinach Salad
recipes.recipe_by: North Dakota State University Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Great Northern beans are white beans that have a mild flavor.

ingredients.name: chicken
ingredients.note: thawed, cut up, and skin removed from each piece
ingredients.raw: 1/2 pound chicken, thawed, cut up, and skin removed from each piece

ingredients.name: tomatoes
ingredients.note: or 1/2-8 ounce can low-sodium diced tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 1 cup tomatoes, diced (or 1/2-8 ounce can low-sodium diced tomatoes)

instructions: In a medium-sized bowl, soak beans in 3 cups of water overnight.
Drain the water and rinse beans.
In a large pot, brown onion, chicken, and ham in oil over medium to high heat for about 5 minutes.
Add water, beans, and salt to pot.
Mix well.
Bring pot to a boil and cook for 5 minutes.
Lower heat and cook for about 1 hour.
Stir pot every 15 minutes.
Add tomatoes and vinegar to pot.
Keep cooking over low heat for about 20 minutes.
Serve hot.
recipes.name: Great Northern Bean Soup
recipes.notes: Tip for cooking chicken: The recommended safe minimum internal temperature for chicken is 165 °F, as measured with a food thermometer.
recipes.recipe_by: A Harvest of Recipes with USDA Foods — USDA Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: These pork chops are marinated in oregano and garlic and then pan-fried in a hot skillet until crispy. These tasty chops make an easy meal with quick clean up.
instructions: Put the pork, oil, vinegar, oregano, and garlic in the glass or ceramic bowl, or in a sealed plastic bag and mix well.
Cover bowl and refrigerate at least 4 hours or overnight.
Sprinkle the pork with the salt and pepper.
Place a large skillet on the stove over high heat.
When hot, add the pork to the dry skillet, waiting about 30 seconds between each addition.
Cook about 7 minutes on each side until crispy.
Serve right away.
recipes.name: Greek Pork Chops
recipes.notes: Lemon, lime, or orange juice can be used instead of red wine vinegar.
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: While feta cheese is the star of any Greek salad, this recipe contains all of the must-have ingredients for a classic salad that is sure to please.

ingredients.name: romaine lettuces leaves
ingredients.raw: 6 romaine lettuces leaves, torn into 1 1/2-inch pieces

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine lettuce, cucumber, tomato, onion, and cheese in large serving bowl.
Whisk together oil, lemon juice, oregano, and salt in small bowl.
Pour over lettuce mixture; toss until coated.
Serve immediately.
recipes.name: Greek Salad
recipes.recipe_by: Healthy Recipes, Adapted from Easy Greek Salad — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A colorful salad loaded with lettuce, cucumbers, tomatoes, onions, and olives topped with chicken and a creamy yogurt dressing.

ingredients.name: cherry tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup cherry tomatoes, cut in half

ingredients.name: black olives
ingredients.raw: 1/4 cup black olives, cut in half

instructions: To make the dressing, add Greek yogurt, lemon juice, olive oil, garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper to a small bowl.
Mix well to combine.
Cover dressing and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Wash lettuce and tear into bite-sized pieces.
Place in large salad bowl and add tomatoes, cucumbers, red onion, olives, and chicken.
Sprinkle with feta cheese.
Top with yogurt dressing and enjoy.
recipes.name: Greek Salad with Chicken
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Lemon pepper seasoning and garlic salt give a flavor punch to this mushroom, carrot, and green bean side dish.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place green beans and carrots in 1 inch of boiling water.
Cover, and cook until tender but still firm.
Drain.
Add oil to heated skillet.
Sauté onions and mushrooms until almost tender.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer 3 minutes.
Stir in green beans, carrots, lemon pepper, garlic salt, and toasted almonds.
Cover and cook for 5 minutes over medium heat.
recipes.name: Green Bean and Mushroom Medley
recipes.recipe_by: North Carolina Cooperative Extension — Wayne County

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This no-fuss side dish is a great addition to any meal and can be prepared in a flash.

ingredients.name: diced tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 1 can diced tomatoes, no salt added

instructions: In a medium-sized pan, cook onions in vegetable oil until they start to turn light brown.
Add the rice, green beans, tomatoes, and water.
Bring to a boil.
Cover the pot with a lid and cook over low heat for 10 minutes.
recipes.name: Green Bean and Rice Casserole
recipes.recipe_by: A Harvest of Recipes with USDA Foods — Adapted from a recipe in Healthy Diabetes Recipes and More — South Dakota Diabetes Control Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Jazz up green beans with mushrooms, onions, and garlic in a quick and easy vegetable side dish.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Spray a skillet with non-stick cooking spray.
Sauté onions, mushrooms, and garlic.
Add green beans and heat thoroughly.
recipes.name: Green Bean Sauté
recipes.recipe_by: Quick and Healthy, Vol.II — ScaleDown Publishing, Inc.

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Frozen green beans and potatoes are boiled in a pot with onion and salt to make an easy side dish for dinner.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Add all ingredients to a large stock pot and cover with water.
Bring to a boil and reduce to medium heat.
Cook until green beans and potatoes are tender.
recipes.name: Green Beans and New Potatoes
recipes.recipe_by: Healthy Cookbook for African American Populations

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Green beans get a flavor boost from fresh or dried parsley and basil, canned tomatoes, and onion.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook beans in a large saucepan of boiling water for 5 minutes; beans will still be crisp.
Drain and rinse under cold running water.
Set aside.
In a large frying pan, heat olive oil over medium heat.
Add onion and cook 2-3 minutes until softened.
Add tomatoes, basil, and parsley.
Cook 3 minutes to heat and combine flavors.
Stir beans into pan and cook 5-6 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper (optional).
recipes.name: Green Beans with Tomatoes and Basil
recipes.recipe_by: University of Maryland Extension — Food Supplement Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: In the spring, in areas where they grow, wild onions can be used in place of green onions. Yellow or white onions work as well.

ingredients.name: no salt added tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 1/2 can no salt added tomatoes, drained

ingredients.name: green onion (or wild onion)
ingredients.raw: 1 tablespoon green onion (or wild onion), chopped

instructions: Open and drain can of sliced potatoes.
Cut sliced potatoes into strips.
In a large skillet over medium heat, lightly brown potatoes in the vegetable oil for 5 to 10 minutes.
In a mixing bowl, add egg, egg whites, milk, and salt.
Mix well.
Stir in ham, tomatoes, and green (or wild) onions.
Pour egg mixture over potatoes in the skillet.
Cover skillet and continue to cook eggs over medium heat until firm, not runny (about 8 minutes).
Cut the omelet into four pieces and serve.
recipes.name: Green Onion Omelet
recipes.recipe_by: A Harvest of Recipes with USDA Foods — USDA Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A small handful of ingredients makes a big splash in this smoothie. The smoothie looks deep purple, but you can definitely taste the green tea thanks to the strong brew. Enjoy it as an on-the-go breakfast, a refreshing afternoon snack or a sweet ending after a meal.

ingredients.name: medium bananas
ingredients.note: peeled, cut in half and frozen
ingredients.raw: 2 medium bananas, peeled, cut in half and frozen

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Add the water to a small saucepan.
Bring the water to a boil over high heat.
Remove the pan from the heat.
Add the tea bags. (Be sure the tea bags are submerged.) Let steep for 4 minutes.
Discard the tea bags.
Let the tea mixture cool for 30 minutes.
Pour into a water pitcher.
Refrigerate for 2 hours, or until chilled.
In a food processor or blender, process the tea, berries, bananas, yogurt, gingerroot and vanilla until smooth.
Pour into four glasses.
Sprinkle with the chia seeds.
recipes.name: Green Tea Berry Banana Smoothie
recipes.recipe_by: Created by the Lipton Teas and Infusions & AHA, a member of the MyPlate National Strategic Partnership Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Grilling brings out the flavor in fresh vegetables like asparagus. Add shrimp, quinoa, and refreshing lemon vinaigrette, and you have a delicious and quick spring or summer salad.

ingredients.name: fresh asparagus
ingredients.raw: 2 cups fresh asparagus, large spears, cut into 1" pieces

ingredients.name: yellow or red bell pepper
ingredients.raw: 1/2 yellow or red bell pepper, cut into 1/2" pieces

ingredients.name: 14 ounce can quartered artichoke hearts
ingredients.raw: 1 14 ounce can quartered artichoke hearts, drained

ingredients.name: fresh or frozen large raw shrimp
ingredients.raw: 12 ounces fresh or frozen large raw shrimp, peeled and deveined

ingredients.name: fresh or bottled lemon juice
ingredients.raw: 3 tablespoons fresh or bottled lemon juice

instructions: Place vinaigrette ingredients in a small bowl and whisk; set aside.
Cut vegetables as directed.
Heat grill and grilling tray.
Place vegetables and shrimp in a large bowl; add about 1/3 of the vinaigrette (about 3 tablespoons) and toss.
Spread shrimp-vegetable mixture over hot grilling tray.
Grill, turning shrimp and vegetables, until the flesh of the shrimp is an opaque color (about 5 to 6 minutes); remove from grill.
Serve grill mixture over cooked quinoa, and drizzle with vinaigrette.
recipes.name: Grilled Asparagus and Shrimp Quinoa Salad with Lemon Vinaigrette
recipes.notes: Serving Suggestions: Serve with non-fat milk and grapes.
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health Foundation

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This grilled cheese packs an unexpected twist with the sweetness of canned peaches! Not only is this sandwich a quick and easy lunch, but also a fun way to add more fruit and veggies to your day.

ingredients.name: whole grain bread
ingredients.raw: 8 slices whole grain bread, thin slice

instructions: Heat the 4 teaspoons of vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat.
Place 4 slices of whole grain bread in the pan.
Layer (in this order) one slice of cheese, a handful of spinach, 4 to 6 peach slices, another slice of cheese, and a slice of bread on top of each original slice of bread.
After 4 to 5 minutes, flip each sandwich and cook another 4 to 5 minutes.
recipes.name: Grilled Cheese with Peaches
recipes.notes: Try this recipe with other leafy greens, such as arugula, and other cheeses.
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This pilaf recipe pairs avocados and bell peppers with red quinoa and grilled chicken, for a satisfying, colorful meal.

ingredients.name: fresh or bottled lemon juice
ingredients.raw: 2 tablespoons fresh or bottled lemon juice

instructions: Heat grill.
Peel and cut avocado into chunks; place in a medium bowl.
Mix lemon juice, basil, an 1/2 teaspoon black pepper.
Drizzle over avocado chunks, toss, and set aside.
Cut chicken breasts in half crosswise.
Mix 1/2 tablespoons olive oil, salt, and remaining black pepper.
Brush mixture on chicken and red bell pepper.
Grill chicken and pepper until done.
Set chicken breasts aside.
Cut pepper into thin strips.
While chicken and peppers are grilling, heat remaining olive oil in a large pan, add garlic and onion, and cook until tender, about 5 minutes.
Add water, bouillon, and quinoa to pan; bring to boil, cover, reduce heat, and simmer until liquid is absorbed and quinoa is cooked (about 15 to 20 minutes).
Place quinoa pilaf in a large bowl and add chicken, red peppers, and avocado.
Toss gently.
recipes.name: Grilled Chicken and Avocado Quinoa Pilaf
recipes.notes: Serving Suggestions: Serve with non-fat milk and orange slices.
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health Foundation

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Set the stage for a delicious plate with these healthy fish tacos with peach salsa. Perfect for a summertime taco night!

ingredients.name: 15.25 ounces peach halves
ingredients.raw: 1 can 15.25 ounces peach halves, drained and chopped

ingredients.name: whole jalapeno pepper
ingredients.raw: 1 whole jalapeno pepper, seeded, and finely chopped

instructions: Make the salsa: In a medium bowl, stir together chopped peaches, bell pepper, onions, jalapenos, cilantro, and lemon juice.
Cover and refrigerate until ready to use.
For the fish: Heat grill or grill pan over medium-high heat.
Using paper towels, pat fish dry, transfer to plate.
In a small bowl, stir together chili powder, low-sodium adobo and Sazon packet.
Rub fish with spice mixture to coat completely.
Place fish on hot greased grill grates.
Cook, flipping once until fish is opaque and flakes easily with a fork (145 °F), about 8 minutes.
Thinly slice fish.
To serve, fill each tortilla with 1/2 fish fillet and about 1/3 cup of salsa.
recipes.name: Grilled Fish Tacos with Peach Salsa
recipes.notes: Serving Suggestions: Serve with a Summer Corn Salad, chock full of vegetables, and a quick Mango Banana Shake for your best taco night yet!
recipes.recipe_by: The Best of La Cocina GOYA: Healthy, Tasty, Affordable Latin Cooking/ Lo Mejor de la Cocina GOYA: Cocina Latina Saludable, Rica y Económica — GOYA Foods

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Fruit kabobs cooked on the grill make a tasty and healthy dessert.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place fruit chunks on a skewer to make kabobs.
Grill or broil on low heat until the fruit is hot and slightly golden.
recipes.name: Grilled Fruit
recipes.notes: If using wooden skewers, thoroughly soak skewers in water prior to using to prevent burning (approximately 30 minutes). For a twist, try changing the fruit. Other fruits that grill well are apples, figs, pears, plums, cantaloupe, honeydew, and watermelon.
recipes.recipe_by: University of Wyoming Extension — Cent$ible Nutrition Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Grilled lamb is delightful with any green salad, especially this Asian-inspired version.

ingredients.name: boneless leg of lamb
ingredients.note: if cubed lamb is not available, ask the butcher to prepare it for you
ingredients.raw: 12 ounces boneless leg of lamb, cut into 1-inch cubes

ingredients.name: shredded Savoy
ingredients.raw: 6 cups shredded Savoy, Napa, or green cabbage

ingredients.name: black or white sesame seeds
ingredients.raw: 2 tablespoons black or white sesame seeds

instructions: Mix marinade/dressing ingredients; divide evenly.
Place lamb cubes in a glass dish; pour half of the marinade/dressing over the lamb.
Cover and refrigerate at least two hours.
In a large bowl, toss cabbage, carrots, jicama (optional), onions, and sesame seeds.
Remove lamb and discard marinade.
Soak bamboo skewers in water for 30 minutes; divide lamb among the 4 skewers.
On hot grill, cook the lamb skewers 5 to 6 minutes per side (or to desired degree of doneness).
Remove lamb from skewers, add to salad, and toss.
To serve, divide salad evenly on four plates.
Drizzle with remaining dressing.
recipes.name: Grilled Lamb Salad
recipes.notes: Serving Suggestions: Serve with nonfat milk and orange slices/wedges. Tips on Cooking Lamb: Cooking temperature: 145 °F (medium-rare); 160 °F (medium); 170 °F (well-done)
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health Foundation

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Fresh pineapple chunks and an easy glaze made with pineapple juice add tropical and zingy flavors to grilled chicken.

ingredients.name: sweet yellow onion
ingredients.raw: 1 sweet yellow onion, cut into wedges

instructions: To make the glaze, combine pineapple juice, vinegar, brown sugar, soy sauce, ginger and mustard in a medium saucepan set over medium-high heat.
Bring to a boil; boil for about 15 minutes.
Preheat grill to medium heat.
Cook couscous according to package directions.
While couscous is cooking, toss chicken breast with oil, salt and pepper.
Grill chicken, for 2 minutes per side or until grill-marked.
Continue to grill, basting and turning with Pineapple Ginger Glaze, for 5 to 6 minutes or until cooked.
Grill onion, zucchini, red pepper, orange pepper and pineapple spears, basting with Pineapple Ginger Glaze, for 3 to 5 minutes or until grill-marked and tender.
Serve chicken with vegetables and pineapple over couscous.
Garnish with green onions.
recipes.name: Grilled Pineapple Ginger Glazed Chicken with Zucchini and Peppers
recipes.notes: Serve with 8 ounces non-fat milk.
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health Foundation

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Savory sweet salsa featuring cantaloupe and avocado is the perfect complement to grilled shrimp.

ingredients.name: lime
ingredients.note: divided, half for salsa and half for garnish

ingredients.name: canned black beans
ingredients.raw: 1 cup canned black beans, low sodium, drained and rinsed

ingredients.name: large or jumbo shrimp
ingredients.raw: 1 pound large or jumbo shrimp, uncooked

instructions: Preheat grill.
Slice lime in half.
In a small bowl, squeeze juice from one half of lime; reserve other half for garnish.
Add remaining salsa ingredients and gently mix.
Peel shrimp, leaving the tails on.
Skewer shrimp on bamboo skewers.
In a small dish mix together canola oil and garlic.
Coat shrimp with oil-garlic mix.
Grill 4 to 5 minutes or until cooked.
To serve, top shrimp with salsa, garnish with lime wedges.
recipes.name: Grilled Shrimp with Cantaloupe Avocado Salsa
recipes.notes: Serve with 8 ounces non-fat milk and brown rice.
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Grill whole bell peppers along with steak, then add pear slices, and you have the foundation of a delicious and colorful Italian-influenced salad.

ingredients.name: white-wheat rotini pasta
ingredients.raw: 2 cups white-wheat rotini pasta, uncooked (about 4 oz)

ingredients.name: boneless choice beef top sirloin
ingredients.raw: 12 ounces boneless choice beef top sirloin

ingredients.name: 100% white grape juice or apple juice
ingredients.raw: 1/4 cup 100% white grape juice or apple juice

instructions: In a small bowl, whisk olive oil, vinegar, grape or apple juice, salt, and herb blend.
Boil water and cook pasta according to package instructions.
Drain pasta, rinse in cool water.
Heat grill, rub peppers with 1/2 tsp olive oil.
Grill whole peppers, turning as needed, until skin begins to brown and bubble.
At the same time, grill beef sirloin to 145 °F, turning once.
Remove from grill, let cool slightly.
Slice peppers into strips, discarding seeds and stem.
Cut sirloin across the grain into thin slices.
Slice pears into thin wedges.
Toss arugula and pasta in large bowl.
To serve, evenly divide pasta-arugula onto four plates, arrange beef, peppers, and pears on top, drizzle with vinaigrette, and sprinkle with crumbled Gorgonzola cheese.
recipes.name: Grilled Steak and Peppers Salad with Pears
recipes.notes: Serving Suggestions: Serve with a glass of non-fat milk.
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health Foundation

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Veggies are wrapped in foil and cooked on the grill for an easy side dish to your cookout. Don't have a grill? This recipe can also be made in the oven.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat grill to medium heat or 350 °F.
Wash vegetables and slice.
Toss in a large bowl.
Add dressing and toss until all vegetables are coated.
Tear 2 large squares of aluminum foil and place half of the vegetable mixture on each piece.
Place an equal piece of foil over the top of vegetable mixture and fold bottom piece with top sheet to form a packet.
Place on heated grill for 20 to 30 minutes or until the potatoes are tender.
If you don't have a grill, bake Veggie Packets in the oven at 400 °F for 20 to 30 minutes.
Before you open the packets, poke holes in the foil with a fork.
Be very careful opening the foil as the steam will be very hot and could burn you!
Empty vegetables onto serving plate or serve from foil packets.
recipes.name: Grilled Vegetable Packets
recipes.recipe_by: Connecticut Food Policy Council

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Cooking out tonight? Try cooking vegetables coated in oil and garlic on the grill for a delicious side dish. If you don't have a grill, you can make these vegetables in the oven.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix oil and garlic in a large bowl.
Add vegetables and toss.
Place vegetable on broiler pan or grill.
Cook 10 minutes, turning twice until vegetables are tender.
Place vegetables on platter.
Serve.
recipes.name: Grilled Vegetables
recipes.recipe_by: US Department of Health and Human Services — Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Ground beef and canned tomato soup make a tasty base for the vegetables in this delicious and hearty stew.

ingredients.name: ground beef
ingredients.raw: 1/2 pound ground beef, or ground turkey, or venison

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Brown meat.
Drain fat, if any.
Season lightly with salt and pepper (optional).
Add soup and 1 can of water to fry pan.
Add vegetables.
Bring to a boil, then simmer, covered, about 25 minutes or until tender.
Remove from heat, cover for last 10 minutes to thicken.
Serve.
Refrigerate leftovers.
recipes.name: Ground Beef Stew
recipes.recipe_by: Simply Good Eating Recipe Cards, Vol. 1, 2000 — University of Minnesota Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Chili powder and lime juice provide a zesty dressing to this salad, which is full of root vegetables.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine romaine lettuce and cilantro, and divide onto four plates.
Place parsnips, carrots, and turnips into 1 quart of boiling water.
Return water to a simmer, cook vegetables for 2 minutes.
Strain into a colander.
Mix ingredients for the dressing right before use.
Place hot vegetables on top of greens and top with homemade dressing.
recipes.name: Harvest Vegetable Salad
recipes.recipe_by: 5 A Day: Eat 5 to 9 Fruits and Vegetables — US Department of Health and Human Services — Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) — National Center for Chronic Disease Prevention and Health Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This soup is full of flavor and is so easy to prepare. Using canned beans and salsa, along with cumin and cilantro, this soup is a great way to throw dinner together in minutes.

ingredients.name: (15.5 ounces each) low-sodium black beans
ingredients.raw: 2 cans (15.5 ounces each) low-sodium black beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Lightly purée one can of black beans with broth, salsa, and cumin in a blender.
In a medium saucepan, combine puréed bean mixture with remaining beans and heat through.
To serve, ladle soup into 4 bowls.
Top each bowl with one tablespoon of sour cream and garnish with the cilantro.
recipes.name: Healthy Black Bean Soup
recipes.recipe_by: Adapted from "Easy and Healthy Black Bean Soup" — Bronson Wellness Center — Bronson Healthcare - Michigan

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This tasty and satisfying soup can be served for lunch or dinner. The leftovers can be frozen for later.

ingredients.name: winter squash
ingredients.raw: 2 cups winter squash, chopped (or 2 cups cabbage, finely chopped)

ingredients.name: large tomato
ingredients.raw: 1 large tomato, chopped (or 15-ounce can low-sodium diced tomatoes)

instructions: In a large pot, brown beef in oil over medium to high heat for 8 to 10 minutes.
Drain fat.
Add water, squash, onion, celery, garlic, and oregano.
If using parsley, add that too.
Mix well.
Bring pot to a boil.
Lower heat and cook for 20 minutes.
Add macaroni, tomatoes, green pepper, salt, and pepper.
Keep cooking over low heat for 20 minutes.
Serve hot.
recipes.name: Hearty Beef Soup
recipes.notes: Tip for cooking beef roast: The recommended safe minimum internal temperature for beef roast is 145 °F, as measured with a food thermometer.
recipes.recipe_by: A Harvest of Recipes with USDA Foods — USDA Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Turn ordinary mashed potatoes up a notch with garbanzo beans for extra protein and fiber!

ingredients.name: potatoes
ingredients.note: baking, peeled and cut in chunks, about 2 pounds

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water Place the potatoes in a large sauce pan and cover with water.
Bring to a boil over high heat then reduce to a simmer.
Add the garbanzo beans 10 minutes after potatoes start cooking.
Continue cooking until potatoes are fork tender, about 20 minutes.
Drain water and place the sauce pan back on the stove.
Mash the beans and potatoes using a potato masher or hand beaters.
Add the milk, cheese and seasonings.
Reheat if necessary.
Serve hot.
recipes.name: Hearty Mashed Potatoes
recipes.recipe_by: Food and Health Communications, Inc.

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Easy to make and delicious to eat, this soup can be made in under an hour! Squeeze the other half of the lime over the soup before serving for extra flavor.

ingredients.name: black beans
ingredients.note: 15 ounce can, low sodium, drained and rinsed

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large pot cook onion, garlic and tomatoes on medium-high heat for 3 minutes.
Stir often.
Add beans, potatoes and water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to low-medium heat.
Cover and continue to cook slowly for 20 minutes.
Add cilantro, cumin and lime.
Stir and continue to simmer for 10 minutes.
Serve warm; sprinkle cilantro on top.
recipes.name: Hearty Mexican Soup
recipes.recipe_by: Simple Healthy Recipes — Oklahoma Nutrition Information and Education — ONIE Project

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Created for junior chefs, this simple and delicious recipe skewers just three ingredients -- omega-3-rich salmon, cherry tomatoes, and pineapple -- for a quick dinner served over whole grain brown rice.

ingredients.name: kosher salt
ingredients.raw: kosher salt, freshly ground pepper, and paprika (to taste)

instructions: Cook rice according to package instructions and set aside.
Cut salmon into 24 1/2-inch cubes and coat all sides with topping of kosher salt, freshly ground pepper, paprika, or any desired spice.
Cut fruit into cubes and cut tomatoes in half.
Set aside.
Slide piece of salmon onto skewer, then tomato, then fruit.
Repeat 3 times on each skewer (or until skewer is full).
Heat 1/2 cup of canola oil in large skillet over medium-high heat for one minute.
Place skewers in pan and turn every 2 minutes per side.
Squeeze lemon on skewers as they are cooking.
To serve, place 1/2 cup rice on plates and with 2 skewers on top.
Squeeze a hint of lemon, if desired.
recipes.name: Hearty Salmon Skewers over Brown Rice
recipes.recipe_by: Seafood Nutrition Partnership

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Frozen vegetables, canned tomatoes, and chicken broth make this an easy soup to throw together on a cold work night. Noodles and beef make it extra hearty and comforting.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water Heat broth and water.
Add vegetables, meat, and seasonings.
Bring to boil.
Reduce heat and boil gently, uncovered, for 15 minutes.
Add noodles.
Cook until noodles are tender, about 10 minutes Remove bay leaf.
Serve.
recipes.name: Hearty Vegetable Beef Soup
recipes.recipe_by: North Dakota State University Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Make this vegetable salad ahead of time and allow the flavors to blend in the refrigerator for a few hours before serving.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In large bowl, combine all salad ingredients.
In a small jar with a tight fitting lid, combine all dressing ingredients and shake well.
Pour dressing over vegetables and stir to coat vegetables.
Cover; refrigerate 1 to 4 hours to marinate, tossing occasionally.
recipes.name: Hearty Vegetable Salad with Herb Dressing
recipes.recipe_by: Montana State University Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Versatile and easy to prepare, these deviled eggs are great as an appetizer, side dish, or snack.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Put eggs into a saucepan.
Cover with cold water.
Bring eggs to a simmer (small bubbles) and cook for 12 minutes.
Remove from the heat and drain.
Crack eggs under cold water and allow to cool.
Remove shells.
Split eggs in half lengthwise and remove yolks.
Put yolks, dressing and mustard into a small zipper-lock plastic bag to mix.
Cut a small hole in a lower corner of the bag.
Squeeze mixture into egg white halves.
Garnish as desired.
recipes.name: Heavenly Deviled Eggs
recipes.notes: Garnishes: paprika, cayenne pepper (if you like it hot), pickle relish, sliced scallions, sliced green or black olives. 1/8 teaspoon each of salt and pepper may be substituted for 1 teaspoon of mustard.
recipes.recipe_by: Simple Healthy Recipes — Oklahoma Nutrition Information and Education — ONIE Project

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Prepare this marinated beef the night before, and have dinner on the table in less than half an hour!

ingredients.name: boneless beef chuck shoulder steak
ingredients.raw: 1 pound boneless beef chuck shoulder steak, cut 1-inch thick

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix onion, parsley, vinegar, mustard, garlic powder, and basil or thyme.
Place meat in plastic bag and pour in marinade.
Close bag securely, place in a bowl and marinate in refrigerator six to eight hours or overnight, turning at least once.
Pour off marinade and discard.
Place meat on rack in broiler.
Broil 15 to 20 minutes or until desired doneness, turning once.
Cut into thin slices to serve.
recipes.name: Herb Broiled Beef
recipes.recipe_by: Eat for Health Toolkit — Recipe by Missouri Nutrition Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Dried herbs and spices make this zesty side dish a family favorite!
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Scrub potatoes and cut into cubes.
Place in medium saucepan and cover with water.
Bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce heat, and simmer 12 minutes or until potatoes are done.
Drain.
Mix dressing ingredients.
Combine hot potatoes, dressing, radishes, basil, thyme, and onion powder.
Serve hot or cold.
recipes.name: Herb Potato Salad
recipes.notes: The mustard and seasoning make this a tasty potato salad. Try using new red potatoes for added color.
