recipes.notes: To decrease fat and cholesterol, omit the beef and add vegetables such as broccoli or zucchini to the sauce.
recipes.recipe_by: Eating Right Is Basic — Michigan State University Cooperative Extension Service — Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This creamy casserole can be easily prepped in advance. Enjoy it with roasted sweet potatoes or winter squash for a colorful meal.

ingredients.name: cream of mushroom soup
ingredients.raw: 1 can cream of mushroom soup, low-sodium

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Bring 1 quart of water to a boil in a large pot and cook the egg noodles in the water for 2 minutes.
Cover the pot, remove from heat, and let stand for 10 minutes.
In the meantime, mix the water, soup, and milk together in a bowl.
Combine tuna and peas with the mixture and pour into a 1-quart casserole dish.
Drain the noodles well and combine with the tuna mixture.
Sprinkle the top with bread crumbs if desired.
Bake for 30 minutes.
recipes.name: Quick Tuna Casserole
recipes.notes: To lower sodium content, use reduced-sodium cream of mushroom soup.
recipes.recipe_by: Healthy Cookbook for African American Populations — Recipe by Tara Caulder, Soaad Ali, and Laide Bello — (Supervised by Dr. Mira Mehta and Terri Kieckhefer)

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Quinoa (pronounced "KEEN-wah") is a whole grain with origins in South America. It is combined in this recipe with black beans, savory vegetables, and spices for a cold salad that is light and refreshing. This salad is high in protein and can be served as a main or side dish.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Rinse the quinoa in cold water.
Boil water in a saucepan, and then add the quinoa.
Return to boil, and then simmer until the water is absorbed, 10 to 15 minutes.
Cool for 15 minutes.
While quinoa is cooking, mix olive oil, lime juice, cumin, coriander, chopped cilantro, and scallions in a small bowl, and set aside.
Combine chopped vegetables with the black beans in a large bowl, and set aside.
Once quinoa has cooled, combine all ingredients and mix well.
Cover and refrigerate until ready to serve.
recipes.name: Quinoa and Black Bean Salad
recipes.recipe_by: Delicious Heart-Healthy Latino Recipes/ Platillos Latinos Sabrosos y Saludables — US Department of Health and Human Services — National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Red, orange, and yellow bell peppers stuffed with garbanzo beans, kale, walnuts, and brown rice make a delicious Mediterranean-influenced vegetarian dish.
instructions: Preheat oven to 375 °F.
Cook rice according to package directions.
Slice bell peppers in half vertically and remove seeds.
Reserve about half of garbanzo beans; mash remaining portion with a fork.
Mix rice with kale, garbanzo beans (mashed and whole), nuts, salt, and pepper.
Fill peppers with mix; place in baking dish and cover.
Bake about 30 minutes.
Remove lid and bake more 5 more minutes.
recipes.name: Rainbow Bell Pepper Boats with Garbanzo Beans and Kale
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health Foundation

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This easy and colorful salad tastes best after marinating it overnight. Enjoy it as a side dish at lunch or dinner.

ingredients.name: (15.5 ounces) red kidney beans
ingredients.raw: 1 can (15.5 ounces) red kidney beans, low-sodium

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix all the vegetables together in a large bowl.
Pour dressing over vegetables.
Sprinkle with pepper.
Stir gently, coating all vegetables.
Cover and refrigerate at least 8 hours.
recipes.name: Rainbow Veggie Salad
recipes.recipe_by: 2009 Recipe Calendar — University of Maryland Extension — Food Supplement Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Simmer eggplant, zucchini, red peppers, and tomatoes with onion, garlic, and seasonings for a delicious flavor in this classic dish.

ingredients.name: large yellow onion
ingredients.note: peeled and chopped into 1/4 inch pieces

ingredients.name: medium eggplant
ingredients.note: peeled and diced into 1/4-1/2 inch pieces

ingredients.name: zucchini
ingredients.note: diced into 1/4-1/2 inch pieces or use 2 cups of frozen zucchini

ingredients.name: red bell pepper
ingredients.note: cored, seeded, and diced into 1/4 inch pieces

ingredients.name: canned low-sodium tomatoes
ingredients.note: including the juice or fresh tomato

instructions: Put the pot on the stove over medium-low heat and when it is hot, add the oil.
Add the onion and garlic and cook until golden, about 10 minutes.
Add the eggplant, zucchini, bell pepper, basil, and oregano and cook, covered, until the eggplant is very, very soft, about 40 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and cook, uncovered, for 20 minutes.
Serve right away, garnished with lemon quarters and basil, or cover and refrigerate up to 3 days.
recipes.name: Ratatouille
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Here is the perfect recipe to make when your garden or market is overflowing with peppers, eggplant, and tomatoes. Add cooked chicken or tofu to make this side dish a complete meal.

ingredients.name: eggplant
ingredients.note: peeled and cut into 1 inch cubes

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in a large saucepan and sauté onion, garlic, bell peppers, and eggplant until tender, about 15 minutes.
Add tomatoes and basil, cook about 10 minutes.
Add pepper and parsley before serving.
Serve hot.
Cover and refrigerate within 2 hours.
recipes.name: Ratatouille
recipes.notes: Optional: Use a bag of frozen vegetables. It will be more economical than fresh vegetables and contain less sodium than canned vegetables.
recipes.recipe_by: Simple Healthy Recipes — Oklahoma Nutrition Information and Education — ONIE Project

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Whole grain tortillas filled with mashed red beans, spinach, cheese, and avocado are heated until and warm, melted, and golden brown.

ingredients.name: frozen spinach
ingredients.note: thawed and squeezed to remove excess liquid

ingredients.name: shredded Monterey Jack or Cheddar cheese
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup shredded Monterey Jack or Cheddar cheese

ingredients.name: 15.5 ounce low-sodium red kidney beans
ingredients.note: drained and rinsed with cold water
ingredients.raw: 1 can 15.5 ounce low-sodium red kidney beans

instructions: Using a fork, mash beans in a bowl until slightly chunky.
Add no-salt seasonings such as garlic powder and dried or fresh herbs, if desired.
Place 1 tortilla on a plate and top with half the mashed beans.
Top the beans with 1/2 cup of the spinach.
Top the spinach with half the cheese.
Top the cheese with half the avocado. (optional) Put the other tortilla on top of the avocado, gently pressing it down so the top half sticks.
Repeat with the remaining 2 tortillas.
Place a nonstick skillet on the stove over medium and heat until warm, then place 1 quesadilla in the dry skillet.
Cook until golden brown, about 1 to 2 minutes on each side. (Or put the plate in the microwave and heat until the cheese melts, about 45 seconds.) Repeat with the remaining quesadilla.
Cut each quesadilla into quarters.
Serve warm.
recipes.name: Red Bean Quesadilla
recipes.notes: Black beans or white cannellini beans can be used instead of kidney beans.
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Red kidney beans and tomatoes and flavored with garlic, onions, peppers, and seasonings and simmered until tender. Serve the bean mixture over rice and top with avocado and cilantro for a traditional meal or side dish.

ingredients.name: (15.5 ounce) low-sodium red kidney beans
ingredients.raw: 2 cans (15.5 ounce) low-sodium red kidney beans

instructions: To prepare the rice: Put the rice and water in the pot and bring to a boil over high heat.
Turn the heat down to low and cook, covered, until the rice is tender, about 45 minutes.
To prepare the beans: Place the large skillet on the stove over medium-high heat.
When it is hot, add the oil.
Add the garlic, onion, bell pepper, and 2 tablespoons water.
Cook until the mixture is golden, about 10 minutes.
Add the tomato, salt, cumin, beans, and water and cook until the beans are very soft, about 20 to 30 minutes.
Divide the cooked rice among 4 bowls or plates, and top with equal amounts of the bean mixture.
Top with avocado and sprinkle with cilantro, if using.
Serve right away, or cover and refrigerate up to 3 days.
recipes.name: Red Beans and Rice
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This flavorful dish is a Monday night tradition in many homes. This vegetarian recipe uses dry beans, onion, pepper, and spices.

ingredients.name: red bell pepper
ingredients.note: chopped - could also use green pepper

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Pick through beans to remove shriveled or broken beans.
Rinse beans thoroughly.
In a 5-quart pot, mix beans, water, onion, celery, and bay leaves.
Bring to boiling; reduce heat.
Cover and cook over low heat for about 1 to 1/2 hours or until beans are tender.
Stir and mash beans against side of pan.
Add garlic, parsley, thyme, salt, black pepper, and red or green pepper.
Cook uncovered, over low heat, until creamy, about 30 minutes.
Remove bay leaves.
Serve over hot cooked rice.
recipes.name: Red Beans and Rice
recipes.notes: See how to make this recipe and more on USDA’s MyPlate Kitchen YouTube site.
recipes.recipe_by: Food and Drug Administration (FDA) — US Department of Health and Human Services

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This flavorful dish is traditionally eaten on Monday nights in many homes and uses dry beans, onion, pepper, and spices.

ingredients.name: medium green bell pepper
ingredients.raw: 1 medium green bell pepper, washed, seeded and chopped

ingredients.name: (15.5 ounces) low-sodium kidney beans
ingredients.raw: 1 can (15.5 ounces) low-sodium kidney beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Spray skillet with cooking oil spray, if using.
Cook onion and pepper over medium heat for 5 minutes or until tender.
Add garlic powder, tomatoes, and kidney beans.
Bring mixture to a boil.
Reduce heat to low and simmer for 5 minutes.
Serve over rice.
recipes.name: Red Beans and Rice
recipes.notes: See how to make this recipe and more on USDA’s MyPlate Kitchen YouTube website .
recipes.recipe_by: Adapted from Easy Red Beans and Rice — UConn Husky Nutrition & Sport

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Spicy and savory, this four ingredient stew is simple and delicious.

ingredients.name: dried red chiles
ingredients.note: more or less depending on taste

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash chilies, removing stems and seeds.
Place in blender with 1 cup water and blend into paste Brown pork lightly in non-stick skillet.
Add the chili paste and mix well, adding water if mixture is too thick.
Add oregano and garlic powder.
Cover and simmer slowly for one hour.
recipes.name: Red Chile Stew
recipes.recipe_by: A River of Recipes: Native American Recipes Using Commodity Foods — USDA Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Spice up your weeknight dinner plans with this Red Hot Fusilli. Loaded with juicy tomatoes, this dish is wonderful with or without the optional chicken!
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in a medium saucepan.
Saute garlic and parsley until golden.
Add tomatoes and spices.
Cook uncovered over low heat 15 minutes or until thickened, stirring frequently.
If desired, add chicken and continue cooking for 15 minutes until chicken is heated through and sauce is thick.
Cook pasta firm in unsalted water.
To serve, spoon sauce over pasta and sprinkle with coarsely chopped parsley.
Serve hot as a main dish and cold for the next day's lunch. *Cost estimate and nutritional analysis does not include chicken.
recipes.name: Red Hot Fusilli
recipes.notes: If pre-cooked chicken is not available, cook 3/4 pound raw chicken and chop into 1/2 inch pieces when cooled down.
recipes.recipe_by: Stay Young at Heart: Cooking the Heart-Healthy Way — US Department of Health and Human Services — National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Traditionally, latkes are pancakes made from potatoes, but these latkes also include lentils, cheese, and hot sauce. Flavorful and tasty, this dish makes a great weeknight meal. Enjoy it along with a side salad.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Add the lentils to a medium saucepan and add water to cover by about an inch.
Bring to a boil, then lower heat to a simmer and cook until tender, about 15 minutes.
Drain and set aside.
Meanwhile, remove the excess water from the potato: you can either squeeze it by the handful, or put the entire pile on a clean tea towel and wring it out.
Crack the egg in a medium bowl and beat it lightly.
Add the potato, cooked lentils, garlic, and green onion.
Add cheese and hot sauce if you're using them.
Add the salt and a good grinding of black pepper and stir until combined.
Heat a large skillet over medium heat, then add a generous drizzle of oil (1-2 tablespoons).

Working in batches, so as not to crowd the pan, add clumps of the potato-lentil mixture (about the size of a golf ball or slightly larger works well), and flatten each as soon as it's in the pan, making them about a half inch thick.
Cook for about 4 to 5 minutes per side, until the latkes are deeply golden brown and cooked through.
Add a little more oil to the pan for each additional batch.
Serve immediately or keep the latkes warm in a 200 °F oven for up to an hour.
recipes.name: Red Lentil Latkes
recipes.recipe_by: The Big Book of Lentils Cookbook — Canadian Lentils

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Dal is a lentil-based dish commonly eaten in India as a part of a more complex meal. This version is an aromatic red lentil dish, flavored by turmeric, cumin, and chili peppers. You can use other varieties of lentils if red lentils are hard to find at your store.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Rinse the lentils in a strainer under running water two to three times.
In a bowl, combine the washed lentils, 1 teaspoon oil, and 1/2 teaspoon salt.
Boil lentils in 1 1/2 cups water until they turn yellow and soft.
Add turmeric powder, cumin powder, and sugar to the boiled lentils and mix them well.
In a separate pan, add rest of the oil and allow it to heat.
Split the chili peppers in half and add to the heated oil.
Add onion to the oil and stir until it starts to turn light brown.
Add 2 tablespoons boiled lentils (mixed with spices) into the fried onion and stir well for 1 minute.
Add the rest of the boiled lentil mix and stir.
Add 1 cup of water and allow it to boil for two minutes.
Serve over white rice.
Add parsley garnish if desired.
recipes.name: Red Lentils with Onion | Masoor Dal
recipes.notes: This is a very common food item in Bengali as well as in Pakistani and Indian communities. Generally, lunch or dinner is started with this item followed by two to three main courses. On special occasions, or when preparing this for someone special, one may garnish it with coconut flakes or cilantro leaves.
recipes.recipe_by: North Dakota Food and Culture: A Taste of World Cuisine — North Dakota State University Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This smoothie has two cups of fruit per serving and kale for an added veggie boost. Try it for breakfast or as a snack.

ingredients.name: water (optional almond milk or coconut milk)
ingredients.note: optional almond milk or coconut milk
ingredients.raw: 1 cup water (optional almond milk or coconut milk)

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Using a blender, mix the greens and the liquid of your choice.
Gradually add in the rest of the ingredients, blending after each addition.
Separate into two cups and reserve one serving for later.
recipes.name: Red Monster Smoothie
recipes.recipe_by: UConn Husky Nutrition & Sport

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Hearty, delicious, and sure to please any crowd. This recipe is filling enough to stand alone or could make a great side dish.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Scrub potatoes, but do not peel.
Cut into quarters.
Cook in boiling water or steam until tender, about 15 to 20 minutes.
While potatoes cook, heat butter or margarine in a large skillet over medium high heat.
Add onion and cook until it becomes clear, about 3 to 5 minutes.
Add cabbage and cook, stirring occasionally, until cabbage begins to brown, about 4 to 6 minutes.
Reduce heat to low.
Add milk, salt, and pepper.
Cover and cook until cabbage is tender, about 6 to 8 minutes.
Drain potatoes.
Add cabbage mixture to potatoes.
Mash with a potato masher or large fork to reach desired texture.
Serve warm.
recipes.name: Red Potato and Cabbage (Colcannon)
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This all-time favorite mix of tender potatoes, celery, and onions has been updated with a tangy yogurt sauce. This classic side is sure to please a hungry family or backyard BBQ guests.
instructions: To prepare sauce, combine yogurt, mayonnaise and mustard in a small bowl.
Mix well and refrigerate.
Wash potatoes and place in pot.
Cover with water about 1 inch above potatoes.
Bring water and potatoes to a boil and simmer until potatoes are fork tender.
Drain potatoes and set aside to cool.
When potatoes are cooled, cut into bite-sized cubes.
Place cut potatoes into large bowl.
Add celery, onions, salt, and pepper to potatoes.
Top with sauce and mix well.
Garnish with parsley and enjoy.
recipes.name: Red Potato Salad
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This traditional side dish is versatile, flavorful, and delicious. There are different ways to prepare refried beans. This recipe uses dry beans, oil, garlic, onions, and cumin.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook beans and reserve some of the cooking liquid before draining.
Sauté onions and garlic in oil until onions become clear.
Add a little water if vegetables stick.
Mash half of the beans, and add to onion and garlic.
Continue to sauté for 10 minutes, stirring frequently.
Allow some of the mashed beans to brown.
Add cumin.
Add remaining beans and continue cooking until they are warmed through.
Water or liquid from beans may be added to keep the beans soft and mushy.
recipes.name: Refried Beans
recipes.recipe_by: The Bold and Beautiful Book of Bean Recipes — Washington State WIC Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A great twist on a classic dish, this is the perfect mix of sweet and tart. Whether you are making this for an event or for your family at home, this treat is sure to please!
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
In a medium bowl, stir together brown sugar, flour and oats.
Stir in the butter and set aside.
Spread the rhubarb and blueberries in an 8x8 inch baking dish and set aside.
In a medium saucepan, mix cornstarch and sugar and stir in the juice.
Cook over medium heat, stirring all the time, until the mixture has thickened.
Turn off the heat.
Stir in vanilla and pour the mixture over the rhubarb and blueberries.
Crumble oat mixture on top of the fruit.
Bake for 45 minutes or until topping is browned and fruit is bubbling at edges.
Serve warm or cold.
recipes.name: Rhubarb Blueberry Crisp
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: The sweet and savory combination of ingredients in this rice bowl makes it a great start to your day. Rice, fruit, and nuts come together to create a nutritious, filling breakfast.

ingredients.name: chopped fruit (try a mixture - apples
ingredients.note: try a mixture - apples, bananas, raisins, berries, peaches
ingredients.raw: 1 cup chopped fruit (try a mixture - apples, bananas, raisins, berries, peaches)

ingredients.name: chopped nuts (try walnuts or almonds)
ingredients.raw: 2 tablespoons chopped nuts (try walnuts or almonds)

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine cooked rice, milk and cinnamon in a microwave-safe bowl.
Microwave on HIGH for 45 seconds.
Stir and heat for another 45 to 60 seconds, or until rice mixture is heated through.
Divide rice mixture between two bowls.
Top with fruit and nuts.
Serve warm.
Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
recipes.name: Rice Bowl Breakfast with Fruit and Nuts
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Easy, delicious, and full of fruit, Rice Dessert is a nice way to end a good meal.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Put aside 1/4 cup of drained pineapple.
Mix all other ingredients together in a medium-sized bowl.
Serve in small dishes.
Top with the remaining crushed pineapple.
recipes.name: Rice Dessert
recipes.recipe_by: Eating Smart, Being Active — Colorado State University and University of California at Davis

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Serve this recipe fresh off the stove or after it has chilled in the refrigerator.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In sauce pan, heat milk and water.
Add rice, bring to boil, lower heat to simmer; stir mixture every 10 minutes.
Cook uncovered until rice is tender, about 30 minutes.
In large bowl, mix eggs, 3/4 cup evaporated milk, vanilla, and sugar.
Set aside.
Add remaining 1/4 cup evaporated milk to rice mixture.
Spoon 1 cup of rice mixture into egg mixture and stir.
Pour egg-rice mixture into remaining rice.
Heat pudding until it boils, stirring continuously.
Remove from heat, and sprinkle with cinnamon.
recipes.name: Rice Pudding
recipes.recipe_by: Recipes and Tips for Healthy, Thrifty Meals — USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Enjoy this classic rice pudding recipe that uses cinnamon and raisins, or any other favorite dried fruit, to make a wholesome dessert that has just the right amount of sweetness.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Combine rice, 2 cups of water, and butter or margarine in large microwave safe dish.
Cover loosely, so steam will escape.
Cook in microwave on high for 5 minutes or until mixture comes to a boil.
Reduce setting to defrost (50% power), and cook an additional 10 minutes.
Mix dry milk, sugar, vanilla, cinnamon, 1 cup water, and raisins together while rice is cooking.
Without allowing rice to cool, remove cover and quickly stir the dry milk mixture into hot rice.
Cover loosely again and continue cooking on defrost (50% power) for 10 minutes.
After cooking time is finished, let pudding sit, covered, for 10 minutes.
Stir gently and put in individual serving dishes.
Eat warm or cover and refrigerate immediately.
Enjoy the refrigerated pudding within 2 days.
recipes.name: Rice Pudding
recipes.notes: A 9-10 year-old child can learn how to use measuring spoons and cups while helping make this recipe.
recipes.recipe_by: Simply Good Eating Recipe Cards, Vol. 1, 2000, Adapted from Easy Rice Pudding — University of Minnesota Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Enjoy this versatile recipe with family and friends. You can substitute other frozen and fresh veggies than the ones listed in the ingredients depending on what you have on hand.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix rice, vegetables, and raisins in a medium-sized bowl.
Mix mayonnaise, dressing and salt in a small bowl.
Stir into rice/vegetable mixture.
Refrigerate leftovers.
recipes.name: Rice Salad
recipes.recipe_by: Eating Smart, Being Active — Colorado State University and University of California at Davis

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This stewed chicken and rice dish comes together with tomatoes and traditional seasonings. This one-pan meal is an all-time favorite.
instructions: To trim, lay chicken thighs on the cutting board, skin side up.
Push the chicken down so the excess fat is on the cutting board (the excess is the part that isn’t right on top of the chicken).
Using kitchen scissors or a sharp knife, cut off excess fat and discard.
Pat chicken dry with paper towels, and discard towels.
Place the skillet over medium high heat and when it is hot, add the chicken thighs, skin side down and cook until browned, then flip, about 5 minutes on each side.
Turn the heat off, carefully remove the chicken from the skillet and transfer to the plate.
Pour off all but 1 tablespoon fat.
Reheat the skillet over low heat and add the onion, pepper, garlic, cumin, and oregano and cook until the onion is softened, about 10 minutes.
Add the uncooked rice and tomatoes and stir well.
Add the water and bouillon cube and bring to a boil over high heat.
Return chicken to pan, skin side down, turn the heat down to low and cover.
Cook chicken for 20 minutes and then carefully flip so that the skin side is up.
Cover and cook for an additional 20 minutes.
Serve right away.
recipes.name: Rice with Chicken | Arroz con Pollo
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A fun and unique twist on pizza using rice as the crust. Enjoy this main dish with all of your favorite toppings!
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oven to 350 °F.
Grease a 12-inch pizza pan or baking sheet.
Cook rice following directions on the package; set aside.
Grate cheese; set aside.
Crack egg and place in mixing bowl, stirring to blend.
Measure and add 2 cups cooked rice, 1 cup grated cheese, and salt.
Mix well to combine ingredients.
Spread rice mixture in prepared pan, pressing firmly and making outer edge slightly raised.
Spread tomato purée evenly over rice mixture.
Place pan in oven.
Bake for 25 minutes.
Remove pan from oven sprinkle pizza with remaining cheese.
Bake 5 minutes longer or until cheese melts.
Remove pizza from oven.
Cut into 12 slices.
Create-a-Flavor Changes: Try different kinds of rice.
Try different kinds of cheese.
Use sliced or chopped green peppers, onions, mushrooms, or other vegetables as toppings.
recipes.name: Rice-Crusted Pizza
recipes.recipe_by: Cooking Up Fun - A Pyramid of Snacks — Cornell University Cooperative Extension — Division of Nutritional Sciences

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This cobbler can be made quickly in the microwave. Enjoy this tasty treat for breakfast or as a sweet dessert.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large microwave-safe bowl, mix peaches, pears, prunes, and vanilla extract.
Rub an orange against a grater to remove 1 teaspoon of the orange peel.
Then, cut the orange in half and squeeze 1/4 cup orange juice.
Add orange peel and juice to fruit mixture.
Stir.
Top with granola.
Microwave on high for 5 minutes.
Let stand for 2 minutes.
Spoon into 4 bowls and serve warm.
recipes.name: Rise and Shine Cobbler
recipes.recipe_by: Kids… Get Cooking! — California Department of Health Services — California Children’s 5-A-Day Power Play Campaign

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Roasted chicken is a simple and classic recipe that will never go out of style. Experiment with different seasonings, if you'd like. Try it with your favorite vegetables on the side for a delicious meal.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 375 °F.
Combine Italian seasoning, garlic powder, salt, and pepper (optional).
Rub chicken with oil, then rub with spice mixture.
Place chicken, breast side down, in roasting pan or Dutch oven.
Bake, uncovered, until internal temperature reaches at least 165 °F.
Let chicken rest for 10 minutes before cutting.
recipes.name: Roast Chicken
recipes.recipe_by: University of Minnesota Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Perfect for a holiday gathering, this roast turkey breast can be prepated in less time than a whole turkey. Enjoy!
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 °F.
Place turkey breast in roasting pan along with onion and carrot.
Mix spices with olive oil.
Rub turkey with olive oil.
Roast turkey at 400 °F for 15 minutes.
Baste with margarine and chicken broth (optional).

Reduce turkey temperature to 350 °F and roast turkey, basting every 20 minutes with pan juices (or margarine and chicken broth), about 1 hour and 15 minutes, or until meat thermometer inserted in thick part of meat registers 165 °F.
Remove to carving board and let rest for 10 minutes.
recipes.name: Roast Turkey Breast with Rosemary, Sage, and Thyme
recipes.recipe_by: Utah State University Cooperative Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Roasting brings out the natural sweetness of the bell peppers. Modify this recipe by trying other seasonings, such as oregano or dried basil.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 450 degrees F.
Wash bell peppers and remove tops and seeds.
Cut peppers in half and rub with vegetable oil.
Place cut side up on a rimmed baking sheet and sprinkle with Italian seasoning, garlic powder, salt, and pepper.
Roast until peppers are tender and blistered in spots, about 30 to 35 minutes.
recipes.name: Roasted Bell Peppers
recipes.notes: No Italian seasoning? Use 1 teaspoon dried oregano, 1 teaspoon dried basil, and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder.
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Roasting Brussels sprouts creates a warm, flavorful, and versatile vegetable dish. This recipe is simple and does not require many ingredients.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 degrees F.
Wash and trim Brussels sprouts.
Cut large Brussels sprouts in half from top to bottom; leave small Brussels sprouts whole.
In a large bowl, toss Brussels sprouts with the oil, salt, and pepper.
Place Brussels sprouts in a single layer on a large baking sheet.
Lining the baking sheet with foil or baking parchment will help with clean-up.
Roast for 20 to 30 minutes, stirring once after 10 to 15 minutes.
Sprouts should be tender and browned.
Remove from oven and drizzle with lemon juice.
recipes.name: Roasted Brussels Sprouts
recipes.notes: Try adding other seasonings with the lemon juice such as red pepper flakes or parmesan cheese.
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A versatile, fall, baked dish, our tasty version features potatoes and Brussels sprouts. Other fall vegetables -- such as parsnips, carrots, and cabbage -- could be substituted.

ingredients.name: Brussels sprouts
ingredients.note: fresh or frozen halved vertically, about 3/4 pound

instructions: Preheat oven to 325 °F.
In a 2 quart baking dish coated with cooking spray, toss Brussels sprouts, potatoes, onion, and garlic with 1 tablespoon olive oil, salt, and pepper.
In a small bowl, mix cheese with milk.
Coat chicken breasts with remaining olive oil.
Nest among vegetables in baking dish.
Top with cheese mix.
Cover with foil and bake for 40 to 45 minutes or until chicken is done.
recipes.name: Roasted Brussels Sprouts, Potatoes, and Chicken
recipes.notes: Serve with 8 ounce non-fat milk and orange slices.
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health Foundation

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Oven-roasted cauliflower sprinkled with cheese is a simple and delicious side dish that pairs well with any entrée.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Remove outer leaves of cauliflower.
Cut florets off the stem.
Wash and drain.
Combine oil, salt, and pepper in a large bowl.
Toss the cauliflower florets in the oil mixture.
Spread cauliflower on a large rimmed baking sheet.
Roast in the oven at 450 degrees F for 15 to 20 minutes until the cauliflower starts to soften and begins to brown.
Sprinkle with cheese.
Continue to roast for 5 to 10 minutes.
recipes.name: Roasted Cauliflower
recipes.recipe_by: University of Maryland Cooperative Extension — Food Supplement Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Cauliflower steaks are a fun way to get in some of your daily vegetables! This simple recipe spices up cauliflower using lemon juice and garlic powder.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 degrees F.
Lightly grease a large baking sheet.
Slice cauliflower from top to bottom through the core into 1- to 1 1/2- inch thick steaks.
Put steaks on the baking sheet along with end pieces, flat side down.
In a small bowl, mix the rest of the ingredients, except cheese.
Spoon on and spread or brush the cauliflower with half the mixture.
Roast for 20 minutes.
Remove baking sheet from the oven, carefully turn the steaks and spread the rest of the mixture.
Roast for 15 to 20 minutes or until the cauliflower is browned and tender.
Sprinkle with cheese, if desired, and serve.
recipes.name: Roasted Cauliflower Steaks
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: These crunchy chickpeas make a great on-the-go snack or a healthy topping to your favorite salad. Experiment with different spices to see which ones you like best.

ingredients.name: (15 ounces) low-sodium garbanzo beans
ingredients.raw: 1 can (15 ounces) low-sodium garbanzo beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 400 degrees F.
Drain and rinse the beans until there is no foamy residue.
Pick out the skins and discard.
Wrap the drained beans in a clean towel to dry thoroughly.
Measure oil into a 9x13-inch baking dish or foil lined pan.
Pour beans into dish, sprinkle with salt and spices.
Mix oil and spices well to coat all the beans.
Bake for 45 to 60 minutes, stirring or shaking every 15 minutes.
Longer makes more crunch, but watch to prevent burning!
recipes.name: Roasted Chickpeas (Garbanzo Beans)
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP)

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Rosemary adds a delicious flavor and aroma to these potatoes. Enjoy your herb roasted potatoes as a side to your favorite protein food entrée.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat the oven to 450 degrees F.
Coat a baking sheet with vegetable cooking spray.
Wash and peel the potatoes.
Cut the potatoes into 1/2-inch cubes, and put them in a large bowl.
Put the oil, rosemary, and salt in a small bowl.
Stir together.
Pour the oil mix over the potatoes.
Stir to coat the potatoes evenly.
Spread the potatoes on the baking sheet.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, or until lightly browned.
recipes.name: Roasted Herb Potatoes
recipes.recipe_by: Pennsylvania Nutrition Education Network

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Enjoy the bold flavors of roasted pork steak tacos, perfectly complemented by a fresh and zesty pico de gallo. This vibrant dish brings together tender meat and a medley of vibrant ingredients for a satisfying meal that’s sure to impress.

ingredients.name: red onion
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup red onion, cut into small cubes

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Pico de gallo: In a bowl, mix all the ingredients.
Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Seasoning: In a small bowl, mix the paprika, onion powder, garlic powder, salt and pepper.
Remove the silver skin from the pork tenderloin, rub it with oil and coat the entire loin with the seasoning.
Place the pork tenderloin on the grill at medium/high heat (400˚F), over indirect heat, for approximately 6 minutes on each side, 18 minutes total.
Cook until it reaches internal temperature of 145˚F with a 3-minute rest.
Then chop it into small pieces.
To make the tacos, heat the tortillas and place some pork tenderloin and pico de gallo on top.
recipes.name: Roasted Pork Tacos with Pico de Gallo
recipes.recipe_by: Created by the National Pork Board, a member of the MyPlate National Strategic Partnership Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Everyone loves these roasted potatoes, and they are easy to make.

ingredients.name: green pepper
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup green pepper, chopped into 1-inch cubes

instructions: In a medium-sized bowl, mix potatoes, onions, green peppers, and garlic.
Add vegetable oil, salt, and pepper to bowl.
If using parsley and paprika, add that too.
Mix well.
Cover bowl and refrigerate for 15 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Spread potato mixture evenly on a cookie sheet.
Bake for about 35 minutes.
Serve hot.
recipes.name: Roasted Potatoes
recipes.recipe_by: A Harvest of Recipes with USDA Foods — USDA Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A quick and tasty snack mix that can be tossed together and enjoyed instantly while you are on the go, no cooking required.

ingredients.name: crispy rice or wheat cereal squares
ingredients.raw: 2 cups crispy rice or wheat cereal squares

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix all ingredients together and serve.
recipes.name: Roasted Pumpkin Seed Snack Mix
recipes.recipe_by: Regional Mental Health Center Cookbook — Regional Mental Health Center

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A variety of root vegetables like sweet potatoes, beets, and turnips make this colorful dish festive and nutritious.

ingredients.name: root vegetables (choose a variety from potatoes
ingredients.raw: 4 root vegetables (choose a variety from potatoes, rutabagas, turnips, parsnips, beets, sweet potatoes, etc.)

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 °F.
Cut vegetables into large chunks.
Place in a medium-sized bowl and pour oil over top.
Add seasonings or Parmesan and mix well.
Spread an even layer on a baking sheet or pan.
Bake for 1 hour or until tender.
Check a few vegetables to see if they are tender.
recipes.name: Roasted Root Vegetables
recipes.recipe_by: Montana State University Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: For a delicious way to enjoy heirloom tomatoes in peak season, here is a great recipe to celebrate your tomato harvest.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 425 degrees F.
Spray a large baking sheet with cooking oil spray.
Cut each tomato in half.
Place tomatoes on the sheet, cut side up.
Drizzle tomatoes with 1 tablespoon of oil and season with pepper.
Cook for 30 minutes, or until tomatoes are beginning to brown on the bottom.
Mix the remaining oil, parsley, garlic, and cheese in a small bowl.
Remove tomatoes from the oven and sprinkle the herb mixture over the tomatoes.
Return to oven for another 10 minutes, or until spices begin to brown.
recipes.name: Roasted Tomatoes with Herbs
recipes.recipe_by: 2009 Recipe Calendar — University of Maryland Extension — Food Supplement Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A hearty, savory, and delicious dish that is packed with meat, potatoes, and tomatoes that can be easily prepared in a slow cooker.

ingredients.name: round steak
ingredients.raw: 2 pounds round steak, cut 1/2 inch thick

ingredients.name: (14.5 ounces) low-sodium French-style green beans
ingredients.raw: 1 can (14.5 ounces) low-sodium French-style green beans, drained

ingredients.name: (14.5 ounces) low-sodium tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 1 can (14.5 ounces) low-sodium tomatoes, peeled and whole

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Season round steak lightly with garlic salt, salt and pepper.
Cut into serving pieces and place in crock pot with sliced onion, which has been separated into rings.
Add potatoes and green beans.
Top with tomato soup and tomatoes.
Cover and cook on Low for 8 hours.
Remove cover during last half-hour if there is too much liquid.
To cook in 2-quart crock pot, reduce ingredients slightly.
recipes.name: Round Steak Casserole
recipes.notes: Menu Idea: round steak casserole, canned pears, lowfat milk
recipes.recipe_by: For Cooking Without Looking, Use a Crock Pot — University of Wisconsin Cooperative Extension Service — Dunn County UW-Extension Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This dish is overflowing with fresh veggies and fun flavors. Pineapple adds extra tang.

ingredients.name: canned pineapple chunks (in juice)
ingredients.raw: 1 cup canned pineapple chunks (in juice), drained

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Put mixed salad greens on a large platter or in a salad bowl.
In a large bowl, mix chopped vegetables and pineapple or orange segments.
Spoon onto the mixed greens.
Mix vinegar, orange juice, and yogurt in a small bowl and pour dressing over salad greens and vegetables.
Top with nuts and raisins.
Serve.
recipes.name: Salad with Pineapple, Nuts, and Raisins
recipes.notes: Tomatoes used in nutrition and cost analysis for vegetables.
recipes.recipe_by: California 5 A Day, It’s So Easy, Adapted from Oprah's Outtasight Salad — Contra Costa Health Services

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Onions, carrots, and cabbage give this dish a crunchy and crisp texture. Lemon juice and vinegar give the veggies a tangy flavor. Enjoy along side of your favorite entrée.

ingredients.name: onions
ingredients.note: cut into slivers or thin slices
ingredients.raw: 1 cup onions, cut into slivers or thin slices

ingredients.name: cabbage
ingredients.note: cut into slivers or thin slices
ingredients.raw: 1 cup cabbage, cut into slivers or thin slices

ingredients.name: carrots
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup carrots, cut into very thin slices

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a salad bowl, combine onions, cabbage, carrots, and tomatoes.
Toss with olive oil, lemon juice, vinegar, salt, and pepper.
Sprinkle garlic and Parmesan over salad.
recipes.name: Salata Ma Jibna (Salad with Parmesan Cheese)
recipes.notes: Salata Ma Jibna is a Sudanese dish.
recipes.recipe_by: North Dakota Food and Culture: A Taste of World Cuisin e — North Dakota State University Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This simple recipe makes good use of canned salmon, or you can also use leftover salmon if you have some on-hand. Out of both? Try canned tuna!

ingredients.name: (16 ounces) salmon
ingredients.note: OR two 5 oz cans of tuna in water, drained

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large bowl, mix all ingredients together.
Mixture will be moist.
Spray a large skillet with non-stick cooking spray.
Heat skillet.
Drop fish mixture onto the skillet using a 1/3 or 1/2 cup measuring cup.
Brown on both sides.
recipes.name: Salmon Burgers
recipes.notes: *Dry bread crumbs, crushed unsweetened cereal, or uncooked oatmeal can be used instead of cracker crumbs.
recipes.recipe_by: University of Nebraska at Lincoln — Nebraska Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A colorful, casual meal that's surprising simple to prepare.

ingredients.name: For the Sweet Potato Oven Fries:
ingredients.raw: For the Sweet Potato Oven Fries:

instructions: Place oven rack in center, heat oven to 425 °F.
Wash and scrub sweet potatoes, slice into wedges, length-wise.
In a large bowl, toss potato wedges with canola oil and seasoning.
Spread on cookie sheet.
Roast in the oven, turning occasionally, until tender and golden brown, about 30 to 40 minutes.
While sweet potatoes are roasting, prepare salmon burgers.
Drain salmon; place in a medium mixing bowl and flake.
Fold in green onions and red pepper, crushed crackers, lemon juice, egg whites, and yogurt.
Shape into 4 patties.
Coat large nonstick skillet lightly with cooking spray; heat.
Cook salmon burgers until golden brown, turn, and continue cooking until other side is golden brown.
Serve burgers with sliced tomatoes and lettuce, and sweet potato oven fries.
recipes.name: Salmon Burgers and Sweet Potato Oven Fries
recipes.notes: Serving Suggestions: Serve with a glass of 100% berry juice blend.
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health Foundation

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This delicate salmon loaf is lower in calories than traditional meat loaf, and pairs well with steamed spinach or broccoli and roasted sweet potatoes.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 325 degrees F.
Drain salmon and remove skin if desired.
Mash bones with meat.
Add the other ingredients.
Add enough milk so that the mixture is moist but not runny.
Place in a lightly oiled 9x5 inch loaf pan.
Bake for 45 minutes.
Serve.
recipes.name: Salmon Loaf
recipes.recipe_by: Wellness Ways Resource Book — University of Illinois Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Tasty patties cooked in a skillet that are perfect topped with fresh lettuce, tomato, and a side of fresh or canned pineapple.

ingredients.name: bread crumbs or cracker crumbs
ingredients.raw: 1/3 cup bread crumbs or cracker crumbs

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash fresh vegetables (if using).
Collect, mince, and measure all ingredients before starting to prepare the recipe.
Open salmon, and drain liquid into a liquid measuring cup.
Add lemon juice and cold water to the salmon liquid to make 1/2 cup liquid total, and set aside.
Put the salmon in a separate mixing bowl.
Mix in the celery (if using), green pepper (if using), and onion.
In another small bowl, beat the eggs.
Then, add them to the salmon mixture.
Add the bread or cracker crumbs, flour, pepper, and the salmon liquid mixture to the salmon mixture, and stir until all ingredients are mixed together.
Use 1/3 cup measuring cup to measure salmon mixture.
Shape into a 1/2 inch thick patty, and place on a plate.
Repeat to make 6 patties.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat, then add 3 patties.
Cook for about 2 to 3 minutes (or until golden brown) on each side.
Remove patties from skillet, and place on a clean paper towel-lined plate to drain.
Cook remaining 3 patties, then serve immediately.
Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Eat within 3 to 5 days .
recipes.name: Salmon Patties
recipes.recipe_by: Eat for Health Toolkit — Recipe by Missouri Nutrition Network — Optional additions from ONIE Project & Colorado State University Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A zesty spread that is perfect as a snack. Serve with whole grain bread, crackers, or rice cakes.

ingredients.name: green onion
ingredients.note: or 1/4 cup onion, or onion powder to taste

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Drain salmon and flake with a fork into a bowl.
Mix in all other ingredients.
Serve on bread, crackers, or a rice cake.
Sprinkle chopped parsley to garnish.
recipes.name: Salmon Spread
recipes.recipe_by: University of Connecticut Family Nutrition Program — Senior Nutrition Awareness Project (SNAP) Newsletters

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This fresh tasting salsa is easy to whip up for your next get together.

ingredients.name: (14.5 ounces) low-sodium diced tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 2 cans (14.5 ounces) low-sodium diced tomatoes, drained

ingredients.name: (4.5 ounces) diced green chiles
ingredients.raw: 1 can (4.5 ounces) diced green chiles, drained

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large bowl, stir together all the ingredients until well mixed.
Cover and chill at least 4 hours.
Serve with Baked Tortilla Chips or raw vegetables.
recipes.name: Salsa
recipes.recipe_by: Nebraska SNAP-Ed, Adapted from Easy No-Cook Salsa

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Spicy, savory beans make a great fiber-filled side dish.

ingredients.name: (15 ounces each) low-sodium pinto beans
ingredients.raw: 2 cans (15 ounces each) low-sodium pinto beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Add the onion and garlic and cook until tender.
Stir in the beans and salsa.
Cook for 10 minutes.
Serve over rice, pasta, or baked potato.
recipes.name: Salsa Pinto Beans
recipes.recipe_by: 2009 Recipe Calendar — University of Maryland Extension — Food Supplement Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: There are endless options for where you would want to add this seasoning blend -- rice, meat, fish, vegetables, and more! Try on your favorite dish to boost flavor but not salt.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Mix all ingredients in a small bowl, using a spoon.
Place mix into a container that allows you to shake to dispense.
recipes.name: Salt-free All Purpose Blend
recipes.recipe_by: Eat Smart New York! — Cornell University Cooperative Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This tuna salad gets its creamy flavor from the avocado and a slight punch from the crushed red pepper.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Drain tuna.
Transfer to a mixing bowl and mix well with avocado for texture.
Add tomatoes, onion, lime juice, crushed red pepper, salt, and mango.
recipes.name: Sanchico Tuna Salad
recipes.recipe_by: Houston Food Bank — Chef Jose Montoya

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This is a healthier version of my mom’s green bean casserole recipe. My version has more vegetables and almost half the sodium per portion. The secret ingredient is the onion powder mixed with the cracker crumb topping. It tastes a lot like the fried onions in my mom’s recipe. I knew the result was good when my husband said he liked it better than the original. Enjoy!
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350 °F.
Blanch the green beans in boiling water for about 4 minutes for crisper beans or longer for a softer texture.
Then plunge in ice water.
Drain and set aside.
Place diced onions and mushrooms in a microwaveable bowl and microwave for about 2 1/2 minutes on high to soften.
Set aside.
Melt the butter over medium heat.
Once melted, stir in flour with a whisk and cook for about 1 minute (continuously whisking).
Whisk in the milk and cook over low heat until you have a thick white sauce.
Stir in Worcestershire sauce, garlic powder, black pepper, and salt.
Stir the drained green beans, onions, and mushrooms into the white sauce (including any liquid with the onions and mushrooms).
Pour into a casserole dish sprayed with nonstick spray.
Crush the crackers and toss cracker crumbs with olive oil and onion powder.
Sprinkle over the top of the casserole.
Bake at 350 °F for about 30 minutes or until crackers are golden brown.
recipes.name: Sarah’s Green Bean Casserole
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion — Recipe submitted by Sarah, MyPlate Nutritionist
recipes.serving_size: 1 portion of Sarah's Green Bean Casserole

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This turkey curry soup is a fun and flavorful dish to make with turkey dinner leftovers. You can use your leftover cranberry sauce to garnish the soup. A spoonful of cranberry sauce or chutney adds a cooling sweet, tangy flavor to balance the spicy curry.
instructions: Heat the olive oil and butter in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and celery and cook for about 7 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in flour, curry powder, and cinnamon and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in chicken broth and scrape up any brown bits at the bottom of the pan.
Bring to a simmer.
Then add carrots, spinach, potatoes, and turkey.
Bring to a boil.
Then reduce the heat to low.
Simmer (covered) for about 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Serve in bowls and garnish with a spoonful of cranberry sauce.
recipes.name: Sarah’s Spicy Curry Turkey Soup
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion — Recipe submitted by Sarah, MyPlate Nutritionist
recipes.serving_size: 1 cup of Sarah's Spicy Curry Turkey Soup

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Toasted whole grain bread is stacked with cucumbers, sardines, tomato, and sliced red onion. Try canned tuna or salmon as tasty alternatives for sardines.
instructions: Put 4 slices toasted bread on the cutting board.
Arrange cucumber slices on top of each slice.
Distribute the sardines evenly on top of the cucumber and using the fork, gently mash them.
Spread the mashed sardines to cover the cucumber.
Squeeze the lemon juice over the sardines.
Put the tomato slices on top of the sardines.
Add the red onion.
Top with the remaining slices of toast and press down gently to hold the sandwich together.
Cut the sandwich in half and serve right away.
recipes.name: Sardine, Cucumber, and Tomato Sandwich
recipes.notes: Canned tuna or salmon can be used instead of sardines
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Don’t throw away your beet greens! The leafy tops of beets can be so tasty. In this recipe, lemon juice, vegetable oil, and seasonings give them a bold flavor profile.

ingredients.name: chopped beet greens (2 bunches with stems removed)
ingredients.raw: 4 cups chopped beet greens (2 bunches with stems removed)

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in a medium-sized pan over medium heat.
Add the beet greens and garlic to the pan.
Stir until just wilted, then reduce the heat to low and stir occasionally until soft, about 5 to 8 minutes.
Stir in lemon juice, red pepper flakes, and salt.
Serve right away or use in another recipe.
recipes.name: Sautéed Beet Greens
recipes.notes: No beet greens? Use other leafy greens such as mustard greens or chard.
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Cabbage, onion, and caraway seeds make this simple and inexpensive side dish a flavorful way to eat more veggies.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in a large sauté pan.
Sauté onion over medium heat, until light brown, about 5 to 6 minutes.
Add sliced cabbage, salt, black pepper, and caraway seeds.
Stir and cook for 30 minutes.
Serve immediately.
recipes.name: Sautéed Cabbage and Onion
recipes.recipe_by: "Cabbage Comfort" National Cancer Institute (NCI) — 5 A Day for Better Health Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Cauliflower can be made into a rice alternative with just a few simple ingredients. Make this fresh-tasting side dish by pairing cauliflower with garlic, onion, and more.

ingredients.name: medium cauliflower
ingredients.note: grated or finely chopped, 4 to 5 cups

ingredients.name: lemon juice or lime juice
ingredients.raw: 1 tablespoon lemon juice or lime juice

ingredients.name: chopped fresh parsley or cilantro
ingredients.raw: 2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley or cilantro

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Heat oil in a large skillet or saucepan on medium heat.
Add onion and cook until soft, 3 to 5 minutes.
Add garlic, cauliflower, salt, and pepper.
Stir until cauliflower is tender, 3 to 5 minutes.
Stir in lemon juice and sprinkle with parsley, if desired.
Serve warm.
recipes.name: Sautéed Cauliflower Rice
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This pan-seared walleye recipe uses fresh herbs and lemon to bring out the mild flavor and flaky texture of this omega-3-rich white fish.

ingredients.name: walleye fillets (4–6 ounces each)
ingredients.raw: 2 walleye fillets (4–6 ounces each), thawed and patted dry

ingredients.name: chopped fresh tarragon or parsley (or 1/2 teaspoon dried)
ingredients.raw: 1 teaspoon chopped fresh tarragon or parsley (or 1/2 teaspoon dried)

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Season walleye on the flesh side with salt and pepper.
Sprinkle with tarragon or parsley and press lightly into the flesh to help it stick.
Melt the butter in a pan over medium high heat.
Place the fillets seasoned side down in the pan, tilting the pan to make sure the butter surrounds the fillets, and cook for about 3 minutes.
Gently flip the fillets and cook on the second side, about 2 minutes.
Walleye should reach a final internal cook temperature of 145 °F as measured with a food thermometer before serving.
Plate and serve immediately with lemon wedges.
recipes.name: Sautéed Walleye with Tarragon
recipes.notes: This recipe contains one or more ingredients considered to be traditional or indigenous to Native American communities in certain regions across North America.
recipes.recipe_by: Recipe adapted from Red Lake Nation Fishery

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Ground beef is the surprise ingredient in this savory and spicy succotash dish.

ingredients.name: frozen lima beans
ingredients.raw: 1 cup frozen lima beans, cooked and drained

ingredients.name: (14.5 ounces) low-sodium tomatoes
ingredients.raw: 1 can (14.5 ounces) low-sodium tomatoes, broken up

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Brown ground beef in 9-inch skillet.
Drain excess liquid.
Stir in remaining ingredients except nutmeg.
Cover and simmer 5 minutes or until thoroughly heated.
Sprinkle with nutmeg before serving.
recipes.name: Savory and Spicy Ground Beef & Succotash
recipes.recipe_by: A River of Recipes: Native American Recipes Using Commodity Foods — USDA Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Bread, cheese, and kale make up this savory bread pudding. Bake ahead of time and slice for quick meals and snacks.

ingredients.name: shredded low-sodium mozzarella or cheddar cheese
ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup shredded low-sodium mozzarella or cheddar cheese

instructions: Preheat the oven to 375 °F.
Lightly grease a 2-quart baking pan.
Put a skillet over medium heat and when it is hot, add the oil.
Add the onion and cook about 10 minutes, until tender.
While the onion is cooking, put eggs and milk in a bowl and mix until combined.
Add the cheese, bread, kale, squash, and salt and mix well.
Let the mixture stand at least 15 minutes until the bread absorbs most of the milk.
When the onion has finished cooking, add it to the bread mixture and mix well.
Pour the mixture into the prepared pan and transfer to the oven.
Bake uncovered for 50 to 60 minutes until lightly browned and set.
Let stand 15 minutes before serving.
recipes.name: Savory Bread Pudding with Kale and Butternut Squash
recipes.notes: It is important to use stale bread that has dried out. If you don’t have stale bread, put fresh bread in a preheated 250 °F oven and bake until dried, usually about 15 minutes.
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: These savory meatloaf muffins are full of flavor and have a beautiful presentation. Enjoy one with a side of steamed spinach, kale, or a fresh green salad.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Combine all ingredients and mix well.
Spoon mixture and divide evenly into 12 greased muffin cups.
Bake for 1 hour, or until temperature in center of meatloaf is 160 °F.
Cool slightly before removing from muffin cups.
recipes.name: Savory Meatloaf Muffins
recipes.recipe_by: Kids a Cookin’ — Kansas Family Nutrition Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A perfect side dish to your favorite stir-fry recipe. Enjoy the added flavor from the scallions.

ingredients.name: brown rice
ingredients.raw: 4 1/2 cups brown rice, cooked in unsalted water

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Cook rice according to directions on the package.
Combine the cooked rice, bouillon granules, and scallions and mix well.
Measure 1-cup portions and serve.
recipes.name: Scallion Rice
recipes.recipe_by: DASH Eating Plan: Lower Your Blood Pressure — US Department of Health and Human Services — National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A hearty side dish that would go well with a flavorful fish recipe and a fresh green salad.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash potatoes; peel and slice into thin slices.
Melt 1 tablespoon of margarine in heavy, deep skillet.
Remove skillet from heat; spread half of potato slices in skillet.
Cover potatoes with onions.
Sprinkle half of flour and pepper over potato mixture.
Add remaining potato slices, flour, and pepper.
Cut 1 tablespoon of margarine into small pieces and place on top of potato mixture.
Pour milk over potato mixture; bring to boil over high heat.
Reduce heat to medium low, cover, and cook until potatoes are tender, about 15 minutes.
recipes.name: Scalloped Potatoes
recipes.notes: Leave potato skins on for more nutrition!
recipes.recipe_by: Recipes and Tips for Healthy, Thrifty Meals — USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: We've turned scalloped potatoes into a one-dish meal with the addition of chicken and fennel that's big in flavor but low in fat. The potatoes are first par-boiled in the microwave to reduce baking time.
instructions: Place rack in center of oven and preheat to 350 °F.
Leaving skin on, thinly slice potatoes.
Cut stalks and fronds from fennel bulb.
Discard stalk.
Thinly slice fennel bulb.
Chop fennel fronts and set aside.
Place potato and fennel slices in 2-quart covered baking dish, and add water to cover vegetables.
Cover with lid and microwave on high for about 5 minutes.
Let cool slightly and drain vegetables into a colander.
Wipe baking dish dry and spray with cooking spray.
Add vegetables back to dish and sprinkle with minced garlic.
Cut chicken breasts in half (total of four pieces).
Place atop the potato-fennel mix.
In a bowl, mix melted margarine and flour into a smooth paste.
Add 1 1/4 cups skim milk, salt, and pepper, stir until smooth.
Pour over chicken, potatoes, and fennel.
Cover baking dish and place in oven.
Bake about 30 minutes.
Mix remaining milk with sour cream.
Increases oven temperature to 425 °F.
Remove dish from oven.
Spread with sour cream mixture and sprinkle with Parmesan cheese and fennel fronds.
Return to oven uncovered and bake an additional 10 minutes until top is golden and bubbling.
Internal temperature of chicken should be 165 °F.
recipes.name: Scalloped Potatoes and Chicken with Fennel
recipes.notes: Serving Suggestions: Serving with 8 ounce glass of sparkling water and 1/2 orange, sliced.
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health Foundation

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Enjoy this classic potato dish along side green or orange veggies to keep your plate colorful.

ingredients.name: russet potatoes
ingredients.note: peeled and sliced into 1/4 inch slices

instructions: Quickest Method: Wash hands with soap and water.
Prepare a large casserole baking pan by coating lightly with oil or cooking oil spray.
Place a layer of potatoes in pan, using approximately 1/4 of potatoes.
Sprinkle layer with 1/4 cup chopped raw onion, 1/2 tablespoon margarine, 1 tablespoon flour, 1/4 teaspoon salt, and sprinkling of black pepper.
Repeat layers, making a total of 4.
Meanwhile heat milk over low heat.
Pour warm milk over all ingredients in casserole dish.
Bake at 350 °F for 1 hour.
Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Creamiest Method: Wash hands with soap and water.
Prepare a large casserole baking pan by coating lightly with oil or cooking oil spray.
Make a white sauce by melting margarine in a small pan.
Stir in flour.
Gradually add milk, stirring constantly.
Cook, stirring constantly, until slightly thickened.
Remove from heat.
Add salt and pepper.
Place a layer of potatoes and onion in a prepared casserole pan, using approximately 1/4 of the potatoes and 1/4 cup onion.
Spread with 1/2 cup of the sauce prepared in steps 2 and 3.
Repeat layers, making a total of 4.
Bake at 350 °F for 1 hour.
Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
recipes.name: Scalloped Potatoes II
recipes.notes: Leave potato skins on for more nutrition!
recipes.recipe_by: Favorite Recipes for Family Meals — Washington State University Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This zucchini recipe brings you a flavorful dish loaded with vegetables and low-fat dairy.

ingredients.name: garlic and herb seasoning mix
ingredients.raw: 1 tablespoon garlic and herb seasoning mix

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Wash and chop zucchini, measure out about 2 cups.
Dice the onion and pepper, set aside along with the zucchini.
Stir the egg and milk together and set aside.
Sauté the vegetables in oil on medium heat.
Remove from the pan.
Scramble the egg mixture until cooked thoroughly.
Stir in the vegetable mixture and fold together.
Cook together until temperature reaches 145 °F.
Sprinkle the seasoning and cheese on top.
When the cheese is melted, serve warm.
Add fresh or other dried herbs as desired.
recipes.name: Scrambled Eggs and Zucchini
recipes.recipe_by: Original recipe name - Zucchini Recipe

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Scrambled tofu is a powerful protein packed dish for any meal of the day. Add your favorite veggies for increased flavor and crunch.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Drain tofu.
In small bowl, dice or mash tofu.
For optional ingredients, crush garlic and/or slice watercress, mushrooms, cheese, bell peppers, and green onions.
In a pan, melt butter.
Add tofu.
Add bean sprouts and optional ingredients.
Saute over medium heat until lightly browned.
Beat eggs and add to tofu mixture.
Cook until firm.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper to taste.
Stir and cook until firm.
recipes.name: Scrambled Tofu
recipes.notes: Optional ingredients: garlic, watercress, mushrooms, cheese, bell peppers, green onions, and chop suey mix.
recipes.recipe_by: University of Hawaii at Manoa Cooperative Extension

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This quick and delicious way to cook greens will give you a tasty side dish in minutes.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Clean the greens thoroughly and cut stems away.
Dry well and tear into salad pieces or slice across leaf into 1/2 inch pieces.
In a large deep pot or skillet with a cover, sauté garlic in oil over medium heat.
Add greens in pan with 1 cup water.
Cover pan and steam for 4 minutes.
Uncover, stir constantly until greens shrink.
Add salt and pepper and continue to stir on high until mixture is thoroughly wet.
Sprinkle cider vinegar on mixture.
Cover.
Turn off heat.
Let stand until ready to serve.
recipes.name: Seared Greens
recipes.notes: You can also try this recipe using turnip greens, mustard greens, spinach, swiss chard, or beet greens.
recipes.recipe_by: USDA Food and Nutrition Service — Team Nutrition

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Italian salad dressing brings flavor to this veggie dish that cooks in just half and hour in the oven. Pairs well with fish, chicken, or tofu.

ingredients.name: medium yellow squashes
ingredients.raw: 2 medium yellow squashes, washed and sliced

ingredients.name: medium bell pepper (green or red)
ingredients.raw: 1/2 medium bell pepper (green or red), washed, seeded, and sliced

ingredients.name: fat free Italian salad dressing
ingredients.raw: 1/4 cup fat free Italian salad dressing

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Stir vegetables and dressing in large bowl.
Spread vegetables in the center sheet of aluminum foil on top of baking sheet.
Bring together and seal to make packet.
Bake for 20 to 30 minutes.
recipes.name: Seasoned Roasted Vegetables
recipes.recipe_by: University of Maryland Cooperative Extension — SNAP-Ed Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This quick and easy recipe uses carrots and turnips for a warm, fall flavor. Garlic and honey (or brown sugar) work together to create a sweet and savory blend.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a large skillet on medium-high heat, add oil and sauté turnips, carrots, and salt until vegetables begin to soften.
Stir in garlic and sesame seeds and cook until vegetables begin to brown.
Stir in honey.
Serve warm.
recipes.name: Sesame Turnips and Carrots
recipes.notes: *Children under the age of one should not consume honey.
recipes.recipe_by: Food Hero — Oregon State University Cooperative Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A quick and easy dessert that kids will love making. Experiment with different flavors of pudding and fruit combinations.

ingredients.name: carton (3.4 ounces) instant vanilla pudding mix
ingredients.raw: 1 carton (3.4 ounces) instant vanilla pudding mix

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place 2 cups of milk in a quart jar with tight-fitting lid.
Add one small package of instant vanilla pudding mix to the jar; screw lid on jar.
Shake until mixture is smooth.
Place pieces of fruit in a serving bowl or paper cups.
Pour pudding over fruit and chill.
recipes.name: Shake-A-Pudding
recipes.recipe_by: UMass Extension Nutrition Education Program

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: This shepherd's pie recipe is a twist on the classic comfort food. Using frozen veggies helps you get it on the dinner table quickly.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place diced potatoes in saucepan.
Cover with water and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer (about 15 minutes).
Drain potatoes and mash.
Stir in milk and set aside.
Preheat oven to 375 degrees F.
Brown turkey in a large skillet.
Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add vegetables and broth.
Bring to a slow boil.
Spoon vegetable-meat mixture into an 8-inch square baking dish.
Spread potatoes over mixture.
Bake 25 minutes.
Serve hot.
Garnish with shredded cheese (optional).
recipes.name: Shepherd's Pie
recipes.recipe_by: Oklahoma Nutrition Information and Education — ONIE Project

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A tasty pumpkin dessert that will delight your dinner companions. Be cautious when making the syrup as it will be extremely hot.

ingredients.name: winter squash
ingredients.note: 1 1/4 pounds of butternut, acorn, or pumpkin

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Boil the sugar and water until it forms a thick syrup in a medium saucepan.
Wash the pumpkin, peel it, remove the seeds, cut into pieces, and cook in the syrup until it is very thick and almost all absorbed.
Arrange the pumpkin on a plate and decorate with walnuts and cinnamon (optional).
recipes.name: Shirini
recipes.recipe_by: North Dakota Food and Culture: A Taste of World Cuisine — North Dakota State University Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: A hearty and delightful stew to warm your family's table. Enjoy this cozy stew with a grapefruit or orange for dessert.

ingredients.name: lamb bones (or lean beef ribs)
ingredients.raw: 3 pounds lamb bones (or lean beef ribs)

ingredients.name: carrots
ingredients.raw: 1/2 pound carrots, peeled and cut into chunks

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a 6-quart saucepan, simmer bones in 2 quarts of water and 2 teaspoons of salt (optional) for one hour.
Add onions, carrots, cabbage, string beans, and garlic.
Simmer for one hour until vegetables are thoroughly cooked.
Remove lamb bones and purée the mixture.
Add 4 tablespoons peanut butter thinned with lemon juice.
Add cooked rice (optional).
Add salt and pepper to taste.
recipes.name: Shorba (Lamb and Peanut Soup)
recipes.notes: Shorba is a Sudanese dish based around lamb. In Sudan, lamb bones commonly are used to flavor the soup-like dish.
recipes.recipe_by: North Dakota Food and Culture: A Taste of World Cuisine — North Dakota State University Extension Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: No need to precook the noodles in this easy lasagna. Add a layer of extra veggies if you desire. Spinach would make a fantastic addition.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Spready 1/2 the sauce on the bottom of a 2-quart baking dish or pan.
Layer half the dry noodles, ricotta, and Parmesan.
Top with 1 cup sauce and layer rest of the noodles, ricotta, and mozzarella.
Top with remaining spaghetti sauce.
Bake 60 minutes at 350 °F.
Remove and let is set for 20 minutes.
Top with Parmesan cheese.
recipes.name: Short Cut Lasagna
recipes.notes: Add browned, drained meat or cooked vegetables if desired. Mix with middle layer of sauce. Spinach would make a fantastic addition.
recipes.recipe_by: Simple Healthy Recipes — Oklahoma Nutrition Information and Education — ONIE Project

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Grapes are a natural balance to this sweet and savory shrimp salad. Enjoy as a sandwich or over lettuce.

ingredients.name: leaves Bibb lettuce or other leaf lettuce
ingredients.raw: 4 leaves Bibb lettuce or other leaf lettuce

instructions: Chop shrimp coarsely.
Mix together shrimp salad ingredients (everything except for the bread, tomato slices, and lettuce).
Divide salad evenly among 4 slices of bread; spread to edges of bread.
Top with tomato slices, lettuce, and second bread slice.
recipes.name: Shrimp Confetti Salad Sandwich with Grapes
recipes.recipe_by: Produce for Better Health Foundation

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Savory simmered beans are simple and satisfying. Enjoy as a side to your favorite entrée.
instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Place beans, water, onion, and bay leaf in a large pot.
Cover and bring to a boil over high heat.
Reduce heat to low.
Simmer for 1 to 1 1/2 hours or until beans are tender.
Remove bay leaf and stir in salt.
Cook 15 minutes longer.
Top each serving of simmered beans with 1/2 cup fresh salsa, or store beans in refrigerator for up to 3 days in a covered plastic or glass container.
recipes.name: Simmered Beans
recipes.recipe_by: Healthy Latino Recipes Made with Love — California Department of Health Services — California Latino 5-A-Day Campaign

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Seasoned chunks of cod topped with fresh diced tomatoes, shredded cabbage, a squeeze of lime, and a dollop of cilantro-infused sour cream are all served on top of a warm corn tortilla. These fish tacos are the perfect combination of simplicity and excitement.

ingredients.name: cod or white fish fillets
ingredients.raw: 1 pound cod or white fish fillets, cut into 1-inch pieces

ingredients.name: red and green cabbage
ingredients.raw: 2 cups red and green cabbage, shredded

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
In a small bowl, combine sour cream, mayonnaise, cilantro, and 2 tablespoons seasoning mix.
In a medium bowl, combine cod, oil, lemon juice, and remaining seasoning mix; pour into large skillet.
Cook stirring constantly, over medium-high heat for 4 to 5 minutes or until cod flakes easily when tested with a fork.
Fill warm tortillas with fish mixture.
Top with cabbage, tomato, sour cream mixture, lime wedges, and taco sauce.
recipes.name: Simple Fish Tacos
recipes.recipe_by: US Department of Health and Human Services — Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Add kale or spinach to this fruit smoothie for a quick and delicious breakfast or snack.

ingredients.name: low-fat milk (or fortified soy
ingredients.note: or fortified soy, coconut, or almond milk
ingredients.raw: 1 cup low-fat milk (or fortified soy, coconut, or almond milk)

ingredients.name: frozen fruit
ingredients.note: all one fruit or a combination of mixed frozen fruit

instructions: Wash hands with soap and water.
Add the kale or spinach and the liquid of your choice to a blender.
Blend.
Add in the rest of the ingredients, blending after each item.
Serve and enjoy, cold.
Reserve the leftover smoothie in the refrigerator for later in the day or the next day.
recipes.name: Simple Green Smoothie
recipes.notes: Consume within 24 hours.
recipes.recipe_by: Northern Valley Catholic Social Service

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Even the youngest junior chefs love massaging the kale in this simple salad recipe, which adds canned tuna, tomatoes, and homemade dressing for a refreshing dish.
instructions: Wash kale.
Set aside to drain water off.
Cut tomatoes in half and lightly toss in bowl with balsamic vinegar, oil, and pinch of salt and pepper.
Set aside.
In a salad bowl, mix tuna and juice from the can gently with the squeeze of 1/2 lemon and a pinch of pepper.
Massage kale for about 3 minutes to soften it.
Add the kale and 1/2 the tomatoes to the tuna.
Gently toss until all is coated with dressing.
Add remaining tomatoes.
Squeeze remaining lemon all over and serve.
recipes.name: Simply Satisfying Kale and Tuna Salad
recipes.recipe_by: Seafood Nutrition Partnership

author: USDA Center for Nutrition Policy and Promotion
recipes.description: Catfish fillets are coated in a spicy cornmeal rub and pan-fried until browned to perfection. Try substituting with cod or tilapia for delicious variety.
instructions: Make the spice rub.
Put the cornmeal, oregano, cayenne pepper, thyme, paprika, salt, and pepper on a plate and combine well.
Dredge both sides of the catfish in the spice mixture.
